rooms.room_note: The entryway is small, high traffic, and usually the darkest part of the house, so shoot on a bright overcast day with the front door open for fill and a white foam board propped against the wall opposite the door as the only bounce. This is a one-person shoot: a tripod, a clamp arm for overheads, and window light. No second operator, so anything that moves through the room is shot as a locked-off frame the hands and objects pass through, never as a follow. Setups here are tight, so work at bench height for three-quarter angles and clamp the overhead arm to the door frame or the hall architrave, since there is rarely floor space for a full spread of legs. Grit is this room's real dirt and it is abrasive, so lay a moving blanket under the tripod feet and keep the lens capped between takes. Two staging notes for Safety segments: use a spray bottle to place the umbrella drip line rather than genuinely soaking a surface near a live outlet, and stage the chained power strip unplugged, plugging in only for the beat where it matters. Nothing above the wrists appears in any frame, so tape a floor mark showing where the operator stands to stay outside the overhead's edge.

videos.title: Entryway Landing Spot Reset: Keys, Mail, and the Paper With No Verdict
videos.cold_open_problem: Open on the six sheets that live on this surface being slid from one end to the other and back, the same shuffle, twice. Show what each one is actually waiting on: a form to fill, a phone call to make, a payment to authorise. Land it that the keys were never the problem on this surface, the paper with no verdict is.

segments.covers: Nothing returns to this surface without one of three verdicts, and the objects that decide nothing leave first.
beats: Tray and the whole paper stack tipped onto the floor in one motion so the real volume sits outside the tray for the first time.
Keys that open nothing, loyalty cards, dead batteries and last month's flyers pulled out as the first exit, named as objects that decide nothing and hold a spot anyway.
Each piece of mail picked up once and given a verdict of act, file, or recycle, with the point made that the surface accepts only those three answers.
Act sheets going upright into the folder with the date written into the corner, set up as the clock that will force the decision later.
shots: Overhead, tray tipped onto bare floor, hands withdrawing to leave the pile alone in frame.
Three-quarter at surface height, hands fanning the paper into one readable layer.
Macro, pen writing a date into the top corner of one sheet.
Close, dead keys and loyalty cards dropping into a discard bag.

short.hook: A key tray and a stack of mail tipped onto the floor from overhead, hands out of frame, the pile just sitting there before a single decision gets made.
short.standalone_note: Name the zone as the surface where pockets empty by the front door, and state the three verdicts inside the opening seconds, since no cold open is carrying them in.

segments.covers: The tray goes where the hand actually opens on the way in, and only four things live on this surface.
beats: Walk the entry path carrying a bag to find the point where the hand opens on its own, and set the tray there rather than where the furniture already stands.
Keys and sunglasses into the tray, one upright folder beside it holding act-on paper only.
Charger plugged in at the far end of the surface, away from anything that drips off a sleeve or an umbrella, called out as a placement decision made now rather than a tidy-up later.
shots: Overhead, tray placed once, lifted, placed again at the second position and left there.
Three-quarter from the door threshold, a hand entering frame and arriving over the tray without a reach or a stretch.
Close on the charger plugged in at the dry end, umbrella stand soft in the background of the same frame.

short.hook: The same key tray placed twice on the same hall surface, and a hand coming through the door reaches naturally over only one of the two spots.
short.standalone_note: Re-establish that this is the drop spot inside the front door and that the tray holds keys and sunglasses only, before the placement test runs.

segments.covers: You clean this surface to read it, because the grey film keys and coins leave tells you how long it has been.
beats: Tray lifted straight out and set aside, revealing the ring underneath it.
Surface wiped first and the tray itself second, in that order because the tray was hiding the evidence.
The grey film read as a record of elapsed time rather than as dirt, which is what cleaning to inspect means on a landing surface.
shots: Macro on the grey ring left where the tray sat.
Close, cloth pulling the film off in a single stroke so before and after sit in one frame.
Overhead of the cleared and wiped surface with the tray still off to one side.
on_screen_text: The film is a date stamp

short.hook: A key tray lifted off a hall surface and the ring underneath it is darker than everything around it, in macro, before a cloth touches anything.
short.standalone_note: Say what the tray is and where it sits, and that the film is shed by keys and coins, since the reveal means nothing without that.

segments.covers: Water, electricity and the floor, the three hazards this one surface produces.
beats: Trace the drip line that falls from wet umbrellas and rain-soaked sleeves, then move the dock or power strip out from under it, keeping water and electricity apart by distance rather than by care.
Count what else shares the outlet feeding the dock, showing the lamp, the seasonal heater and the four-port charger chained together, then unchain it to one dock on one outlet.
Work bag lifted off the floor beside the tray, named as the thing you go over in the dark with your arms full of shopping.
shots: Close, water off a spray bottle falling onto the surface below the hooks, power strip sitting in the drip path.
Macro on the chained plugs of the strip, staged unplugged, then the same frame with one plug only.
Low three-quarter at ankle height, bag on the floor in the dark walking line, then the same frame clear.

short.hook: A spray bottle places exactly where umbrella water lands on a hall surface, and a power strip is sitting directly in it.
short.standalone_note: State that this is the surface just inside the front door and that umbrellas and coats drip here every wet day, so the strip's position reads as a real risk rather than a stunt.

segments.covers: A photograph of the finished tray, taped where the next person already looks.
beats: Photograph the cleared tray with the folder standing beside it, framed straight down so the finished state is unambiguous.
Print it small and tape it inside the coat cupboard door at the height people glance while hanging a coat.
Make the point that the tray then teaches itself to whoever did not do the reset, which is the ideal-state photo from Chapter 25 doing its job on one surface.
shots: Hands holding a phone squared over the finished tray, screen visible in frame.
Macro on the small print being trimmed and taped.
Three-quarter of the print taped inside the cupboard door as a coat swings past on its hanger.

short.hook: A cleared key tray gets photographed from straight down, printed small, and taped inside the coat cupboard door where a hand reaches past it every day.
short.standalone_note: Hold the finished tray on screen first so the photograph has something to be a photograph of, and name it as the landing spot inside the front door.

segments.covers: The folder empties after dinner, one sheet at a time, until it stands loose again.
beats: Folder lifted off the surface as you sit down after dinner, hung on something that already happens every night.
Sheets worked one at a time rather than in a batch, with the folder visibly thinning across the sequence.
Folder returned to the surface standing loose and upright, which is the signal that tonight's job is finished.
The fourteen day rule: a sheet that passes fourteen days stops being paperwork and becomes a decision, so it either gets done tonight or gets recycled honestly.
shots: Close, hands lifting the folder from beside the tray.
Overhead on a side table, sheets coming out one at a time into two small piles.
Macro on the folder standing loose and upright, air visible between the sheets.
on_screen_text: When you sit down after dinner

short.hook: A folder of household paper crammed tight enough that the sheets stand rigid, beside the same folder standing loose with daylight between the pages.
short.standalone_note: Explain that the folder holds act-on paper only and sits beside the key tray by the front door, before the loose against tight comparison lands.

close.standard_beat: Show the finished surface holding the tray and the folder and nothing else, with the standard stated as keys never riding out of the house in a coat pocket that lives on a hanger. Trigger shown on camera: hands full and already stopped as the coat comes off, and everything in them going into the tray in that one pause.
close.next_zone_teaser: Next we go three feet left to the coat rail, and count coats by weather instead of by number.

shot_list: Overhead arm clamped to the door frame, squared to the surface, for the tip-out, the mail verdicts and the finished-state photograph.
Three-quarter tripod at the door threshold for the arrival path and the hand arriving over the tray.
Macro setup at surface height for the dated corner, the grey ring and the loose folder spine.
Low three-quarter at ankle height for the work bag in the dark walking line.
Close on the outlet and power strip, staged unplugged, with a matching one-plug version.
Spray bottle clamped above the surface for the water and electricity beat, camera locked off.
Cupboard door interior setup for taping the printed standard, with a coat passing through frame.
Side table setup for the after-dinner folder sequence, one warm practical lamp plus window light.
videos.description_hook: The surface inside the front door where keys, wallet and mail land is not failing from mess, it is failing from unmade decisions. This is the full 6S reset for that one spot, hands only, no presenter on camera.

videos.title: Entryway Coat Rail Reset: Count Coats by Weather, Not by Number
videos.cold_open_problem: Open close on the one good coat on this rail, the one that cost real money and goes outside roughly never. Show it surviving a pass of the hand along the rail while three cheaper coats come off. Land it that this rail is holding coats kept for reasons that have nothing to do with weather, and that getting rid of the expensive one feels like admitting to the money.

segments.covers: Every coat comes down and gets held, and the last cold season is the test, not the hanger.
beats: Rail stripped completely, coats and bags to the floor, so the rail hangs empty and the real count is out in the open.
Each coat held by the shoulders against one question, whether it went outdoors even once through the last cold season, with the ones that did not going straight out.
The guilty coat given its one trial instead of a verdict: front hook, most reachable spot, two weeks, shown being hung there alone.
Single gloves fanned out and let go, and off-season coats routed to a bedroom closet rather than the far end of the same rail, which is the difference between moving a problem and solving it.
shots: Three-quarter, rail stripped in one continuous pass, coats leaving frame to the floor.
Overhead of the full pile on the floor with the empty rail at the top of frame.
Close on hands holding one coat by the shoulders and turning it once.
Macro, a drawer of single gloves fanned across the shelf.

short.hook: An entryway coat rail stripped completely bare in one continuous pass, and the pile that lands on the floor keeps growing after the rail is empty.
short.standalone_note: Say up front that this is the coat rail by the front door and that the test is one full cold season of actual outdoor use, since the strip alone reads as chaos without the rule.

segments.covers: Hooks and hangers do different jobs, and hook height is set by the shortest person who uses this rail.
beats: Pile split into hook items and hanger items, daily on and off to hooks, the wool coat that creases to a hanger.
Hook height set by holding the shortest person's own coat flat to the wall and marking at its shoulder, so the height is measured off the coat that will hang there rather than guessed.
The two hooks nearest the door left deliberately empty for visitors, which becomes the read on this rail later.
Hats and gloves consolidated into one bin on the shelf above, umbrellas moved into the stand.
shots: Overhead of two clear piles building on the floor, hooks and hangers.
Three-quarter, a child's coat held flat to the wall and a pencil marking the wall at its shoulder, hands only.
Close on the two empty hooks nearest the door, coats crowding at the right of frame.
Close, hats and gloves going into a single bin on the shelf.

short.hook: A child's coat is held flat against the wall by an entryway rail and a pencil marks the wall at its shoulder, well below the hook that has been there for years.
short.standalone_note: Establish that this is a shared coat rail used by adults and children, so setting the lowest hook off the smallest coat has a stated reason.

segments.covers: Brush, wipe and tip out, and find the water that has been sitting in the umbrella stand.
beats: Shoulders of the hanging coats brushed down, showing the dust that settles on the one surface of a coat nobody touches.
Shelf wiped with the hat bin lifted off rather than wiped around, since the dust line sits on the lid and under the base.
Umbrella stand tipped out over a tray on the doorstep, revealing water and grit in the bottom, which nobody checks because the stand is opaque.
shots: Close, brush drawn along a coat shoulder in raking window light so the dust reads.
Macro on the dust line across the hat bin lid, before and after.
Three-quarter on the doorstep, umbrella stand tipped over a tray, water and grit coming out.

short.hook: An umbrella stand from beside a front door tipped out onto a tray, and what comes out is not dust, it is standing water.
short.standalone_note: Name the umbrella stand and its spot by the door, and say that it has most likely never been emptied, because that is the entire reveal.

segments.covers: Hooks, brackets and loops, the three ways a loaded coat rail hurts somebody.
beats: Full weight hung on each hook in turn before any of them is trusted with a soaked winter coat, which is the only honest test of a hook.
A hook driven into plasterboard without an anchor shown pulling out with a lump of wall behind it, and the anchored version fitted alongside as the fix.
Weight redistributed on the shelf above: heavy boots and holdalls come down, light bulky things go up, because anything heavy above head height lands on whoever tugs the coat underneath.
Long scarves and bag straps moved off the low hooks and up high, since a strap on a low hook hangs as a loop at a small child's neck height.
shots: Close on a hand pulling its full weight down on a single hook, wall filling frame.
Macro on a bare hook screw beside a fitted wall anchor.
Three-quarter of the shelf above the rail, the heavy bin coming down and out of frame.
Close, a long scarf hanging as a visible loop at low hook height, then the same hook with a coat only.

short.hook: A hand pulls its full weight down on each hook along an entryway rail, and the third one moves in the wall.
short.standalone_note: Say this is a coat hook rail by the front door and that a soaked winter coat is far heavier than the dry one you hang, so the weight test has a purpose on screen.

segments.covers: The shelf bin says contents and season, so nobody opens it in October to find out.
beats: Contents and season written on the face of the shelf bin, hats and gloves, winter, sized to be read from standing on the floor.
The label tested from where it is actually used: a reach up from the floor in October by someone who needs to know before the lid comes off whether this is the right bin.
The point made that a label here is the same visual control as the taped mat outline later in this room, which is Chapter 14 doing the work instead of someone's memory.
shots: Macro, marker writing on the bin face.
Three-quarter from floor level looking up at the shelf, label legible at that distance.
Close, a hand reaching up and taking the bin down without pausing.

short.hook: Two words and a season go onto the face of a storage bin above a coat rail, then a hand reaches up from floor level and takes it down without checking inside.
short.standalone_note: Establish that the bin lives above the entryway coat rail and holds seasonal hats and gloves, so the October reach makes sense on its own.

segments.covers: The rail gets walked on the way back from putting a wash on.
beats: Trigger shown: a wash goes on, and the rail sits on the walk back.
The rail walked and anything left over a chair back or the bannister collected and returned to a hook.
The two empty hooks read as the state of the whole zone: no empty hook means one coat is in the wrong room.
shots: Close, washing machine door closing, hands only, then the same hands leaving frame toward the hall.
Locked-off three-quarter at the bannister, a coat lifted out of frame, then the same coat arriving on a hook in a matching locked-off frame at the rail.
Straight-on close on the two empty hooks at the end of the sequence.
on_screen_text: When you put a wash on
Walk the rail on the way back

short.hook: A coat over a bannister and a coat over a chair back, and one walk back from the washing machine collects both onto the rail by the door.
short.standalone_note: Name the trigger plainly as putting a wash on, and land the two empty hooks standard at the end so the Short resolves without the parent video.

close.standard_beat: Finish on the rail holding one coat per person, one bag, the labeled bin above, umbrellas in the stand, and two hooks visibly empty, with the standard stated as those two empty hooks. Seasonal trigger shown: on the first morning cold enough that you go looking for gloves, the swap happens that morning, standing there, rather than noted for later.
close.next_zone_teaser: Next, down to floor level and the rack that decides how much grit reaches every other floor in the house.

shot_list: Three-quarter tripod square to the rail wall, wide enough for the full rail plus the shelf above, for the strip and the rebuild.
Overhead arm clamped in the hall doorway for the floor pile and the hook against hanger sort.
Macro setup at rail height for glove pairs, dust lines, marker on the bin and the bare screw beside the wall anchor.
Low three-quarter from floor level looking up at the shelf for the label reach test.
Raking window light across the coat shoulders with a white card opposite so the brushed dust reads, no lamps.
Doorstep setup for tipping the umbrella stand into a tray.
Tight close on individual hooks for the weight test, wall filling frame.
Two matching locked-off frames, bannister and rail, for the Sustain collection walk, coats passing through.
videos.description_hook: The coat by the front door that cost real money and goes outside roughly never is the reason this rail never stays clear. Here is the full 6S reset for an entryway coat zone, hands only, no presenter on camera.

videos.title: Entryway Shoe Rack Reset: Turn the Shoe Over and Let the Sole Decide
videos.cold_open_problem: Open in macro on a sole with the tread rubbed smooth and the heel worn through on its outer edge, the pair that survives every clear-out because it is fine for mucky jobs. Set two more pairs like it down beside it. Land it that this rack is holding footwear kept on a memory rather than on a condition, and that a smooth sole is not gardening footwear, it is rubbish with sentiment attached.

segments.covers: Every shoe comes out, gets paired on the floor, and the unpaired and the finished go.
beats: Rack emptied completely onto the floor and shoes paired up in the open, because a rack lets an odd shoe pass as half of something.
Each pair turned sole up before it is allowed back, with smooth tread and worn outer heels going out as a group alongside outgrown children's pairs and the trainers with a split sole.
One dirty-job pair per person kept and set aside to be stored where the dirty jobs actually happen, not at the front door.
The tin of polish that has dried solid goes with the discards, a supply that quietly stopped being a supply.
shots: Overhead, rack emptied in one pass, shoes landing loose on the floor.
Overhead of the same floor after pairing, pairs in rows, odd shoes in their own line to one side.
Macro on a split sole flexing open under a thumb, then a smooth tread beside a good one.
Close on a polish tin opened to show it cracked and solid.

short.hook: A shoe rack by a front door emptied onto the floor, then every pair turned sole up in a row, and the smooth ones are easy to spot from above.
short.standalone_note: State that this is the shoe rack inside the front door and that the sole decides, not the memory, since the turned-over shoes need that rule attached to mean anything.

segments.covers: Daily pairs at standing reach, boots in the tray, and the strip between door and rack stays clear.
beats: Daily pairs returned to the rack at a height reachable standing up, without crouching, soles down.
Boots put in the tray on the reasoning that they will always come in wet, so the tray is where they live rather than where they occasionally land.
Off-season pairs boxed and carried out of the room to a closet.
Floor between the door and the rack cleared to a full stride wide and marked, with nothing placed back inside it.
shots: Three-quarter, hands placing pairs onto the rack at chest and waist height, soles down.
Close on boots standing upright in the tray, tray edges in frame.
Overhead from above the door looking down the cleared strip, a full stride marked with tape.
on_screen_text: A full stride of clear floor

short.hook: A tape line goes down on the floor between a front door and a shoe rack, one full walking stride wide, and then everything sitting inside it gets removed.
short.standalone_note: Name the zone as the shoe rack inside the front door and say the cleared strip is permanent, not a staging step for filming.

segments.covers: The grit in the boot tray is exactly what scratches the hallway floor, so it goes outside.
beats: Boot tray carried outdoors and hosed, showing salt and grit sluicing off rather than being wiped around.
The point made that this material is what scratches the hallway floor once it is tracked back in, which is why the tray gets tipped and never wiped.
Rack shelves wiped, showing they hold far more dried mud than they look like they do.
Room rhythm named: the tray goes out for a hose when it looks dry, because dry is when it is worst.
shots: Three-quarter outdoors, hose running over the tipped tray, grit and salt coming off.
Macro on the salt line in the tray corner before the water hits.
Close, cloth drawn along a rack shelf leaving a clean stripe through dried mud.
on_screen_text: Tip it, do not wipe it

short.hook: A boot tray hosed on a doorstep, and the water running off it comes away grey with road salt and grit.
short.standalone_note: Establish that the tray sits just inside the front door under wet boots, and say plainly that this grit is what ends up scratching the hallway floor.

segments.covers: Wet soles, solvents at toddler height, and a rack that tips forward.
beats: Wet soles on hard floor shown as how people go down in this room, with the tray positioned to catch the drip.
Anything that walked in soaked stays on the tray until it is dry rather than being carried through the house.
Polish, suede cleaner and waterproofing spray taken out of the open basket at toddler height and moved up onto a shelf or out of the room, named plainly as solvents.
Heavy pairs moved to the bottom shelf and the rack bracketed to the wall if it is narrow, because a tall rack loaded heaviest on top comes forward when a child climbs it to reach their own boots.
shots: Close at floor level, a wet sole set on hard floor leaving a smear, then the same sole on the tray.
Macro on solvent labels in an open basket at low height, then the same basket empty.
Three-quarter of the rack with heavy boots moving from top shelf to bottom.
Close on a wall bracket being fitted to the back of the rack.

short.hook: An open basket at ankle height beside a front door shoe rack, shot in macro, and every label in it reads as a solvent.
short.standalone_note: Say where the basket sits, beside the shoe rack inside the front door, and that this height is exactly toddler reach, because the hazard is entirely about position.

segments.covers: A named shelf per person makes a third pair visibly homeless without anyone counting.
beats: Each person given their own shelf on the rack, the name written at the shelf edge where it is read from standing.
A third pair set down against a named shelf, showing it has nowhere to stand, so nobody has to count pairs or police anyone.
The named shelf placed in the same family of standards as the boot tray rhythm, a rack that checks itself rather than a rule someone has to remember, which is Chapter 24.
shots: Macro, a name being written on a label at the shelf edge.
Three-quarter of the full rack with every shelf named, read from standing height.
Close, a third pair set down on a named shelf with nowhere to sit flat.

short.hook: Names go on the edge of every shelf of a shoe rack, then a third pair is set down and there is visibly no floor left for it to stand on.
short.standalone_note: State the cap of two pairs per person at the door before the third pair appears, or the demonstration has no rule behind it.

segments.covers: Shoes go on the rack before the coat comes off, while your hands are still free.
beats: Sequence shown on camera: door, shoes off, shoes onto the rack, and only then the coat.
The ordering reason shown by running it the wrong way round: coat off first, hands full, shoes stay where they landed.
Second trigger shown: on bin night the boot tray goes out alongside the bins and comes back empty.
shots: Three-quarter from inside, framed below the wrists and ankles, shoes coming off and going straight to the rack.
Close on the rack receiving both shoes soles down before any coat enters frame.
Exterior at dusk, boot tray carried out beside the bin, hands only.

short.hook: The same arrival home shot twice: coat off first and two shoes stay lying on the hall floor, shoes away first and the floor by the door stays clear.
short.standalone_note: State the rule as shoes onto the rack before the coat comes off, and give the reason, hands are still free, because the two-take comparison depends on it.

close.standard_beat: Close on the finished rack, two pairs per person, soles down, boots standing in the tray, one pair of slippers each, and a full stride of clear floor between the door and the rack, with the standard stated as everything else living somewhere that is not the entryway. Bin night trigger shown, the tray going out and coming back empty.
close.next_zone_teaser: Next we open the drawer under the bench, the one that turns back into a junk drawer within a month.

shot_list: Overhead arm clamped in the hall doorway for the empty-out, the pairing grid and the cleared stride strip.
Three-quarter tripod at rack height for shelf placement, the heavy-pair move and the wall bracket.
Macro setup for split soles, smooth tread, salt lines, solvent labels and shelf-edge names.
Floor-level close, lens near the boards, for wet sole smears and the tray drip line.
Doorstep setup with a hose for the boot tray wash.
Dusk exterior setup, hands only, for the bin night trigger.
Door-side three-quarter framed below the wrists and ankles for the shoes-before-coat sequence, shot twice for the comparison.
videos.description_hook: Everyone keeps a worn out pair for mucky jobs, and everyone has about three of them and roughly one muddy job a year. This is the full 6S reset for the shoe and boot zone inside the front door, hands only, no presenter on camera.

videos.title: Entry Bench Reset: Giving the Junk Drawer One Job
videos.cold_open_problem: Open on the drawer under the entry bench being pulled out and tipped, with the note that this drawer was emptied not that long ago and filled straight back up, because it is the nearest place to set down something you do not want to carry further. Land the decision actually being avoided: not what to throw away, but admitting the drawer needs a job at all.

segments.covers: The drawer holds far more than its size suggests, and the dead stock leaves before any test is applied.
beats: Drawer tipped out fully onto the bench top so the volume sits beside the drawer that held it.
Dead batteries, pens that do not write, single earbuds, sunscreen from three summers ago and takeaway menus swept out in a first pass with no deliberation.
Every remaining pen tested against paper before it is allowed back, run as a fast pass rather than an inspection.

The one test question introduced and applied out loud to three real items: would you need this while wearing your outdoor shoes, on the way out or in the first seconds back in. The screwdriver, the birthday candles and the case for a phone nobody owns all fail.
shots: Three-quarter, drawer pulled fully out and tipped across the bench top in one move.
Overhead of the spread on the bench with the empty drawer beside it for scale.
Macro on a pen scribbling and leaving nothing.
Close on the failed items going into a box bound for another room.
on_screen_text: Tip it out, all of it
Would you need it in shoes?

short.hook: One shallow drawer from an entry bench tipped out, and the spread it makes on the bench top is wider than the drawer it came from.
short.standalone_note: Name the drawer as the one in the bench inside the front door, and say it has been emptied before and refilled, because that is what makes the volume land.

segments.covers: Named sections in the drawer, and the space under the bench takes what the seat must not.
beats: Drawer divided into sections with each one named as it is set: dog lead and waste bags, sun cream and insect spray, a torch, one pen.
The point made that a section without a name absorbs anything, which is exactly how this drawer refills.
Bags and the vacuum placed underneath the bench, never on the seat, because a seat with something on it stops being a seat you can lace a boot on.
Finished drawer shown with the base visible between the sections, which is the check that nothing is overfull.
shots: Overhead, dividers dropped into the empty drawer, then each named category placed in turn.
Macro on the visible drawer base between two sections.
Three-quarter of the bench with bags and the vacuum sliding underneath and the seat left bare.
on_screen_text: See the base of the drawer
Under the bench, not on it

short.hook: Dividers go into an empty entry bench drawer and every section gets named out loud before a single object is allowed into it.
short.standalone_note: Explain that this is the drawer in the bench by the front door and that unnamed space is what refills it, otherwise the naming looks like decoration.

segments.covers: The drawer comes fully out, and the seat carries the same grit as the floor.
beats: Drawer lifted right out of the carcass rather than cleaned in place, then tipped so the sand and crumbs come out of its corners.
Corners shown specifically, since that is where a drawer holds what a wipe never reaches.
Seat wiped, on the reasoning that people sit here in outdoor clothes, so it collects the same grit the floor does.
shots: Three-quarter, drawer lifted clear of the carcass and carried out of frame.
Macro on a drawer corner, sand and crumbs tipping onto paper.
Close, cloth drawn across the bench seat leaving a clean stripe.

short.hook: A drawer taken fully out of an entryway bench and tipped over paper, and what comes out of the back corners is sand.
short.standalone_note: Say the drawer belongs to the bench inside the front door and that people sit on it in outdoor clothes, which is where the sand came from.

segments.covers: A narrow console is a climbing frame, and a shallow drawer opens at a toddler's head height.
beats: Console strapped or bracketed to the wall if it is taller than it is deep, since it comes over forwards with the drawers out.
An open drawer front shown from low down reading as the bottom step of a ladder, and the heaviest contents moved into the bottom drawer.
Box cutter and scissors taken out of the shallow drawer that opens at toddler head height and moved to another room.
Back corners swept for loose button batteries, coins and small magnets, with batteries going into a lidded tin or out of the room entirely.
shots: Three-quarter, anti-tip strap being fitted between the console back and the wall.
Close on an open drawer front from a low angle, reading as a step.
Macro on button batteries, coins and magnets swept out of a back corner onto a pale surface.
Close, batteries going into a lidded tin and the lid closing.

short.hook: An entry console drawer left open, shot from a toddler's eye height, and the drawer front reads as the bottom step of a ladder.
short.standalone_note: State that this console sits inside the front door and is taller than it is deep, since that shape is exactly what lets it come over forwards.

segments.covers: The cap on the bench top gets written down where the next person will meet it.
beats: Three permitted top items written on a card in the words a household member would actually use.
Card taped inside the drawer so it is met by whoever opens it, which is everyone, including the people who never read a word about any of this.
The frozen line said plainly, a standard is the best way you know today, written down, with the card offered as something to rewrite when the drawer's job changes. See Chapter 23.
shots: Macro, three lines being written on a small card.
Overhead of the card taped inside the open drawer, named sections visible around it.
Close, the drawer opening and the card being the first thing in frame.
on_screen_text: The best way you know today

short.hook: A card with three lines on it gets taped inside an entry bench drawer, so the rule meets whoever opens the drawer instead of living in one person's head.
short.standalone_note: State the cap first, three items on the bench top and nothing on the seat, because the card means nothing without the number.

segments.covers: The reset rides on two things that already happen, the dog lead going back and the table being cleared.
beats: Dog lead dropped back into its named section after a walk, and the glance up at the bench top while the drawer is already open.
Top taken back down to three in that same pause, with no separate trip made for it.
Second trigger: plates carried past the bench when the dinner table is cleared, with one item swept off the top on the way through.
Both named as habits hung on a movement already happening rather than tasks added to anyone's day.
shots: Close, dog lead dropping into its named drawer section, drawer open in frame.
Three-quarter, two items lifted off the bench top while the drawer is still open.
Locked-off close at the bench, plates passing through frame and one item leaving the bench top with them.

short.hook: A dog lead goes back into its section of an entry bench drawer, and before the drawer closes two things come off the bench top in the same movement.
short.standalone_note: Establish the three item cap on the bench top and that the drawer holds the dog lead, so one continuous movement reads as the whole habit.

close.standard_beat: Close on three items on the top, an empty seat, and a drawer where every section holds one named category with the base visible between things, with the standard restated as the test question that keeps it that way: would you need this while wearing your shoes, on the way out or in the first seconds back in. Trigger shown as the drawer opening for the dog lead and the top coming back to three while it is open.
close.next_zone_teaser: Last zone in this room is the smallest one, the mat, and it is the one doing the most work.

shot_list: Three-quarter tripod square to the bench for the drawer tip-out, the drawer removal and the anti-tip strap.
Overhead arm over the bench top for the spread, the divider layout and the taped card.
Macro setup for pen tests, drawer corner sand, button batteries and the written card.
Low angle at toddler eye height, lens near the floor, for the open drawer front as a step.
Under-bench close for bags and vacuum placement with the seat bare in frame.
Locked-off hallway frame at the bench for plates passing through on the way from the table.
Entry-door close for the dog lead returning to its named section.
videos.description_hook: The drawer in the entry bench turns back into a junk drawer within a month of being emptied, every time, because nobody has decided what it is for. This is the full 6S reset that gives it one job, hands only, no presenter on camera.

videos.zone: The Door, Mat, and Immediate Floor
videos.title: Doormat Reset: How to Tell When a Mat Has Stopped Working
videos.cold_open_problem: Open in macro on mat fibres flattened all one way with grit sitting on top of the pile instead of down inside it, then a shoe crossing and carrying that grit straight off. Land it that a mat looks perfectly fine long after it has stopped working, that the decision being dodged is spending money on something not visibly broken, and that this mat is quietly sanding the finish off every floor between the door and the kitchen.

segments.covers: Nothing is stored on this patch of floor, so everything currently on it leaves tonight.
beats: Everything sitting on the floor inside the door lifted out in one pass: the recycling bag, the parcel waiting to go back, the sports kit.
Outgoing returns given one named spot in another room and shown being set down there, because a returns pile with no home always comes back to this floor.
Sports kit and recycling carried to where they actually belong rather than to the nearest surface in the hall, done tonight because this strip refills the same evening it is cleared.
shots: Overhead from above the door looking down at the loaded floor strip, then the same frame bare.
Three-quarter, hands lifting each item out of the strip in sequence.
Close on a named box or shelf in another room receiving the outgoing parcel, label in frame.

short.hook: The strip of floor just inside a front door, loaded with a recycling bag, a return parcel and a sports kit, then the same overhead frame completely bare.
short.standalone_note: State the rule as nothing being stored on the floor inside the door's swing, permanently, since the before and after means nothing without the rule attached.

segments.covers: Two mats doing two different jobs, and the inside one has to be long enough to walk on.
beats: Coarse mat placed outside to scrape and absorbent mat inside to dry, with the two jobs named separately as you set each one.
A normal walking pace crossing of the inside mat, showing whether both feet land on it, which on most mats they do not.
The point made that a mat too short for a walking stride is exactly how the grit gets past, so length is the specification rather than the pattern on it.
Anything beyond two mats removed, since a third mat only adds edges to catch a toe.
shots: Three-quarter from outside the threshold holding both mats in one frame, inside and out.
Overhead of a walking stride across the inside mat, feet only, the second foot landing past the end onto bare floor.
Close on the coarse outside surface, then the absorbent inside one, cut together.
on_screen_text: Both feet must land on it

short.hook: A normal walking stride across a doormat shot from overhead, and the second foot lands past the end of the mat onto bare hallway floor.
short.standalone_note: Name the two mats and their separate jobs first, scrape outside and dry inside, so the stride test reads as a length problem and not a tidiness one.

segments.covers: The mat is honestly the whole job here, and the dark line at the threshold is what it never caught.
beats: Inside mat vacuumed on both faces, with the underside called out as the face everybody skips.
Mat taken outdoors, beaten and washed, showing the line of dirt a working mat drops when it is shaken out.
Cloth run along the bottom edge of the door and along the threshold strip, revealing the dark line and naming it as all the grit that got past the mat.
Room rhythm set: both mats vacuumed every time the vacuum comes out, inside mat beaten outdoors monthly.
shots: Close, vacuum head crossing the mat, then the mat flipped and the underside done.
Three-quarter outdoors, mat beaten against a wall or rail with the dust cloud lit from behind by daylight.
Macro on the dark threshold line with a cloth pulling half of it away in one stroke.

short.hook: A cloth pulled once along the threshold strip of a front door, in macro, leaving one clean half and one black half in the same frame.
short.standalone_note: Say the line sits at the threshold of the front door and is made of grit the mat failed to catch, which is the entire point of the shot.

segments.covers: A curled edge, a sliding mat and a loose hinge, the three ways this threshold puts somebody down or catches a hand.
beats: Curled mat corner at the doorway catching the toe of someone stepping in with their arms full, staged from the ankles down.
Edges gripped or taped flat, with the fix going down on camera and the corner tested by hand afterwards.
A mat pushed sideways on hard floor to show it sliding, then held after the same fix, since a mat that moves is a hazard even lying flat.
Door hinge screws tightened while you are already down there with the cloth, because a loose hinge or a failing closer swings harder than expected and catches fingers against the frame.
shots: Floor level close on a curled mat corner with a shoe toe catching it, ankles down only.
Macro on grip tape going onto the mat edge and being pressed flat.
Close, a hand pushing the mat sideways on hard floor, then the same push with the mat holding.
Close on a screwdriver at a door hinge, hand only.
on_screen_text: A sliding mat is a hazard

short.hook: A shoe toe catches the curled corner of a doormat at floor level, and the corner is the only thing in frame.
short.standalone_note: Establish that this is the mat inside the front door and that people step in with arms full and eyes down, which is why a curled edge matters at this threshold specifically.

segments.covers: A taped outline makes a kicked mat obvious to everybody, not only to you.
beats: Thin line of tape run around the mat's correct position while it is still in place, then revealed when the mat is lifted.
Mat kicked out of position deliberately, with the offset now obvious to anyone walking in.
The difference drawn between a rule only you can see and a boundary anyone can read, which is what Chapter 14 means by an outline.
shots: Overhead, tape run along the mat edge, then the mat lifted to show the closed outline.
Overhead of the mat sitting off square inside its own outline.
Three-quarter from the door of a foot nudging the mat back onto the line.

short.hook: A doormat is lifted and there is a taped rectangle underneath it, then the mat goes back down slightly crooked and the offset is impossible to miss.
short.standalone_note: Say the tape was run around the mat's correct position by the front door before it was lifted, since the reveal only works if the viewer knows the tape came first.

segments.covers: The mat is on the route back to the vacuum cupboard, so it gets done last, every time.
beats: Mat shown sitting directly on the walking route between the room being vacuumed and the cupboard where the vacuum lives.
Mat done last as part of putting the vacuum away, so it is never a separate decision anyone has to make.
Second trigger: whoever comes home last and locks the door straightens the mat with a foot before turning the key.
shots: Locked-off three-quarter down the hall with the mat in the foreground, the vacuum passing through frame toward the cupboard.
Close on the vacuum head crossing the mat as the last action before the cupboard door closes.
Night close at the threshold, a foot nudging the mat square and a hand turning the key.

short.hook: A vacuum gets carried back toward its cupboard and the doormat sits directly on the path, so it gets done on the way past rather than as its own job.
short.standalone_note: Name the mat as the one inside the front door and the trigger as putting the vacuum away, because the route is the whole idea.

close.standard_beat: Close on both mats lying dead flat inside their taped outlines, no curled corners, nothing at all on the floor inside the door's swing, and the door latching on the first push, with the standard stated as that floor strip staying empty for good. Lock-up trigger shown: the last person home straightens the mat with a foot before turning the key.
close.next_zone_teaser: That closes the entryway. Next stop in the series is the kitchen, starting at the counter that never stays clear.

shot_list: Overhead arm clamped above the door strip for the loaded against bare floor, the stride test and the taped outline.
Three-quarter tripod outside the threshold holding both mats in one frame.
Floor level close, lens on the boards, for curled corners, toe catches and the mat slide test.
Macro setup for the dark threshold line, grip tape and flattened mat fibres.
Exterior wall or rail with daylight behind the dust for beating the mat.
Locked-off hall frame, mat in foreground, for the vacuum passing on its way to the cupboard.
Night threshold setup, hall practical light only, for the mat nudge and the key turn.
Close on a door hinge with a screwdriver for the hinge tightening beat.
videos.description_hook: A doormat looks perfectly fine long after it has stopped working, and a finished mat quietly sands the finish off every floor it feeds. Here is the 6S reset for the door, mat and floor inside your front door, hands only, no presenter on camera.

rooms.room_note: Shoot across two days on mid morning side light, which is the only light that shows crumbs, grease film, and the dust band at the back of a shelf. Kill the ceiling fixture: its colour will not match the window and it drops a hard tripod shadow across the work surface. All overheads come off one tripod with the centre column inverted or a lateral arm fitted, set outside the walkway so the strip of floor between sink, hob, and refrigerator stays clear. This is a one person shoot, so every overhead is locked off and framed before hands enter, and no shot may need a second operator. Nothing above the wrists enters frame at any point, so sleeves push back and every hand move gets a rehearsal pass. Where a second pair of hands is called for, it is a household member's hands only, wrists down, into a locked off frame. Light cabinet interiors and under sink with a bounce card, never a lamp inside the cabinet, which reads as fake instantly. On set safety is real here: knives and the mandoline are sheathed between takes and never rested on a towel edge, the hob stays cold except where heat is genuinely needed, cleaner bottles in the sink sequence stay capped and are never placed in the basin together, and wet crisper drawers get carried two handed because wet plastic on tile is the fall risk of the day. Record room tone twice, once with everything off and once with the refrigerator running, or the compressor will cut in and out under the voiceover.

videos.title: How to Reset a Kitchen Prep Counter with 6S
videos.cold_open_problem: Overhead on the best stretch of counter in the house, given over to the appliance you love and rarely use: the mixer, the bread machine, the espresso setup. Beside it a cutting board balanced half off the edge because there is nowhere flat left. Name the problem: the surface you are meant to cut on has been handed to machines, and the call this zone turns on is the stand mixer, judged on uses last month rather than on what you meant to bake.

segments.covers: Only three things earn this surface: what you cut on, what you cut with, what you season with.
beats: Sweep the whole counter onto the dining table in one continuous move so the true width of the run being argued over is visible.
Return items one at a time against the three item test, making the point that the count is fixed before sorting starts rather than discovered afterwards.
Handle each stray in turn, the vitamins, the second board, the bread bag, the receipts, each getting a home elsewhere or leaving, never a spot at the back.
Work the stand mixer call on camera: count real uses over the past month, under a couple of times a week goes to a low cabinet, untouched for a year leaves the kitchen.
shots: Overhead, loaded counter before anything moves
Three-quarter, hands loading a carry tray
Overhead, bare run with a board laid across to show its width
Macro, hands setting board, knife block, and salt back down one at a time
on_screen_text: Cut on. Cut with. Season with.

short.hook: Overhead: a fully loaded prep counter clears to bare surface in one unbroken sweep, then exactly three objects come back.
short.standalone_note: Re-establish that this is the prep run only, not every counter in the kitchen, and name the three item test before the first object returns.

segments.covers: The board goes where you already stand, and knives, oil, and salt are built outward from it.
beats: Mark the spot where hands land when chopping starts, then set the board there rather than where the counter looks tidiest.
Move the knives to a wall strip or block on the dominant side, showing the reach that decision saves mid cut.
Shift the oil and the salt from beside the board to behind it, making the point that beside the board is really on the board once you are working.
Open the cabinet directly underneath and lift a mixing bowl without turning around, which is the reason the board sits here and not two steps along.
shots: Overhead, hands sweeping the reach arc around the board
Close, a knife going onto the magnetic strip
Three-quarter, oil and salt moving from beside the board to behind it
Low three-quarter, cabinet below opening and a bowl coming up in one motion
on_screen_text: Behind the board, not beside it

short.hook: Two takes of the same reach for a mixing bowl under a cutting board, one with a turn and a step, one without, cut side by side.
short.standalone_note: Say this is the prep counter and that the board's position is decided by where your hands land, not by how the run looks.

segments.covers: Clean to inspect: lift the toaster and the kettle instead of wiping around them.
beats: Lift the toaster and the kettle straight up off the counter to reveal the crumb ring under the feet, and make the point that wiping around them has never moved it.
Run a damp cloth along the counter to backsplash seam, showing what comes off a joint that looks clean from standing height.
Pull the toaster crumb tray and empty it over the bin, noting that this is a tray most people have never opened.
shots: Macro, appliance feet lifted to reveal the crumb ring
Close, cloth drawn along the backsplash seam in raking light
Close, crumb tray sliding out and emptying over the bin

short.hook: Macro on a toaster lifted straight up off a counter, revealing a crumb outline of its own feet.
short.standalone_note: Establish that this is the prep counter and that lifting every appliance is the pass itself, not a bonus step.

segments.covers: Blades get a home and the kettle and toaster cords stay off the wet side. This is the 4th S.
beats: Show the two ways a blade hides on this run: knives lying loose behind the board under a tea towel, and one left blade-up in the rack at the end of the counter.
Move every loose blade into the block, the magnetic strip, or a bladed sleeve in the drawer, one at a time on camera.
Trace the kettle and toaster cords away from the sink end of the counter, naming this as water and electricity meeting on a wet hand.
Slide the toaster out from under the low cabinet and away from the paper towel roll, so heat has somewhere to go.
shots: Close, a knife blade-up in the rack, then removed and sheathed
Macro, blade sliding into a sleeve in the drawer
Three-quarter, cord being routed away from the sink end
Overhead, toaster repositioned clear of the cabinet and the paper roll

short.hook: A knife is pulled blade-up out of a drying rack, held still for a beat, then sheathed and given a fixed home.
short.standalone_note: State that Safety is the fourth of six passes, so the Short does not read as a five step system, and name the zone as the prep counter.

segments.covers: The clear run stops being a matter of opinion once it has an edge you can see.
beats: Run a short strip of tape under the counter lip to mark where the clear prep run starts and ends.
Show the alternative for anyone who does not want tape on the lip, an outline traced around the board's own footprint.
Explain what the mark decides: board, knife block, and salt inside it, the mixer and the bread bag outside it, settled without anyone being reminded. Cross-reference Chapter 14, visual controls.
shots: Close, tape being pressed along the counter lip
Overhead, marked run seen from above with the board inside it
Macro, edge of the mark where the clear run ends
on_screen_text: Mark it, do not mention it

short.hook: A strip of tape goes under a counter lip, and the line decides on the spot which side of it the bread machine lives on.
short.standalone_note: Re-establish the standard being marked, one board, one knife block, one seasoning, nothing parked, before the tape goes down.

segments.covers: The trigger already exists in the house: the dishwasher start button.
beats: Press start on the dishwasher, then clear the counter and set the board down onto bare surface, in that order, as one linked action.
Show the board refusing to sit flat because something has arrived under it, and treat the wobble as the signal rather than a nuisance.
Make the point that the trigger is tied to a thing that already happens every night, not to a reminder or an app.
shots: Close, hand pressing the dishwasher start button
Overhead, counter clearing and the board coming down flat
Macro, board rocking on an object that does not live here
on_screen_text: If it will not sit flat, something arrived

short.hook: A cutting board set down on a counter rocks once on something underneath it, and that wobble is the entire check.
short.standalone_note: Name the trigger, the dishwasher going on, and the one board standard in the first few seconds, since neither carries over.

close.standard_beat: Final overhead of the finished run in the same frame as the opening shot: one board, one knife block or strip, one seasoning within reach, nothing parked overnight. Then the trigger shown once more, the dishwasher start button pressed and the counter clearing behind it, so the standard and the moment that holds it land together.
close.next_zone_teaser: One step to the left, to the burners, where the hood filter has been quietly giving up.

shot_list: Overhead locked off on the full counter run, used for before and after
Three-quarter tripod at counter height for placement and reach moves
Macro on appliance feet, crumb tray, and the counter to backsplash seam
Close on knife handling: rack, strip, block, and sleeve
Low three-quarter on the cabinet directly under the board
Close on tape being laid under the counter lip
Insert on the dishwasher start button
Overhead on the board set down flat, and again rocking
videos.description_hook: The prep counter is the surface your kitchen loses first, because it is flat and it accepts anything. Six passes, Sort through Sustain, to get one clear run back and keep it.

videos.title: 6S for the Cooking Zone: Hob, Hood Filter, Spices, and the Utensil Crock
videos.cold_open_problem: Close on the spice rack, jars opened one at a time over the bin, several smelling of dust rather than of themselves. Then the crock beside the hob with a dozen handles sticking out of it. Name the problem: both are full and neither is readable, and the call this zone turns on is which utensils earn a place beside the heat, decided by what your hand reached for during a week of ordinary cooking.

segments.covers: The crock earns its contents over a week of real cooking, not over one afternoon of guessing.
beats: Empty the whole utensil crock into a box and set the box out of easy reach, making clear that the week is the test and nothing is thrown yet.
Cook normally for the week, returning to the crock only what a hand actually reached for, filmed as single inserts across the days.
Open the box at the end of the week: the warped plastic turner, the corn holders, and the third pair of tongs never moved, which is the answer.
State the cap plainly, no more than six tools in the crock, every one used this month.
shots: Overhead, crock tipped into a box in one motion
Close, a single tool taken from the box mid week and dropped into the crock
Overhead, day one and day seven of the box from the same marked tripod position
Macro, six tools going back into an empty crock
on_screen_text: Empty it, then cook for a week
Six tools, all used this month

short.hook: A utensil crock is emptied into a box beside the hob, and seven days later the box still holds three tongs and a warped turner.
short.standalone_note: Explain the week long test and the six tool cap up front, since the Short compresses a real week into a few seconds.

segments.covers: Arrange by the moment of need, with hands busy and heat already on.
beats: Place the oil, the salt, and the turner within one reach of the burner, demonstrating the reach with a pan already on the hob.
Move the spices into a shallow drawer or a tiered rack so the lids are read from above instead of jars being shuffled front to back.
Store the pans on the side you plate from, and show the walk that placement removes mid cook.
Give the pot holders a hook that can be found without looking, which only matters when both hands are already carrying something hot.
shots: Three-quarter, one reach from burner to oil and salt
Overhead, spice lids read from above in a shallow drawer
Close, pan lifted from storage and set down on the plating side
Macro, hand finding the pot holder hook without the eyes following
on_screen_text: Within one reach of the burner

short.hook: Overhead on a spice drawer where every lid is readable at a glance, cut against the same jars being shuffled front to back on a rack.
short.standalone_note: Say this is the cooking zone and that placement is decided by the moment of need, hands busy and heat already on.

segments.covers: Degrease before you disinfect, and the hood filter is the piece nobody has touched.
beats: Lift the burner grates off and set them to soak, making the point that this is slow work and the soak buys the time.
Wash the splash wall and the underside of the hood with warm water and dish soap first, because disinfectant cannot reach through a film of cooking oil.
Take the hood filter out and run it through hot soapy water, showing what comes off, and explain that a saturated filter stops pulling steam and starts dripping it back down.
Return the grates only once the surfaces behind them are done.
shots: Close, grates lifted off and lowered into a soak
Macro, raking light on the underside of the hood before and after
Close, filter sliding out of its clip and going into hot soapy water
Overhead, the water in the sink after the filter has been washed

short.hook: A metal hood filter unclips from above a hob for what is plainly the first time, and the water it goes into changes colour.
short.standalone_note: Show where the filter lives and how the clip releases, since most viewers do not know it comes out at all.

segments.covers: Handles in, cloth and paper away from the burner, and the blanket found before anything is smoking. This is the 4th S.
beats: Turn every pan handle inward and give the two reasons on camera: a sleeve catching it, and a small hand reaching up.
Move the tea towel, the paper roll, and the oil bottle off the burner side of the hob, framing this as the burn and fire question.

Show where the fire blanket or extinguisher lives and clear the route to it, the point being that it is found before a pan is smoking rather than during. Cross-reference Chapter 22, prevent and prepare.
Keep the landing space beside the hob clear and wide enough to set a hot pan straight down.
shots: Overhead, a handle turned from out over the edge to inward
Low angle at a small child's eye line on the protruding handle, no person in frame
Close, tea towel and paper roll relocated away from the burner side
Close, hand on the fire blanket in its mounted position
on_screen_text: Handles in. Cloth away. Blanket found.

short.hook: A camera set at toddler height looks straight up at a pan handle hanging out over the front edge of a lit hob.
short.standalone_note: State that Safety is the fourth of six passes, and name the landing space beside the hob as part of the same pass.

segments.covers: Ready becomes a picture of this hob that anyone can match.
beats: Set the hob and one step of surround into its ready state, grates on, crock at six tools, oil and salt in place, and photograph it from the angle you actually stand at.
Tape the photo inside the nearest cabinet door, then have a household member's hands match the hob to the picture, filmed wrists down in a locked off frame.
Make the shift explicit: ready stops living in one person's head, so the spice jar and the loose spoon have an answer without anyone being asked. Cross-reference Chapter 25, the ideal-state photo.
shots: Overhead, hob and surround set to ready state
Close, the printed photo being taped inside a cabinet door
Three-quarter, cabinet door open with the photo visible and the matching hob behind it

short.hook: A photo of a hob in its ready state gets taped inside the cabinet door directly above it, and the two are held in one frame.
short.standalone_note: Show what ready looks like in this zone, oil and salt placed, six tools in the crock, before the photo appears, or the picture means nothing.

segments.covers: The trigger is heat: every time a pan goes on.
beats: Put a pan on to heat, and while it comes up to temperature return the spice just used to the front of the rack and the loose utensil to the crock.
Make the case for this trigger, that it happens every single time you cook and it uses time already being spent waiting.
Show the zone at the end of a cooked meal, still holding its standard, having never been reset as a separate job.
shots: Close, pan set on the burner and the flame or element coming up
Overhead, spice jar returning to the front of the rack during the wait
Macro, utensil dropped back into the crock
Wide overhead, the zone after cooking, still in ready state

short.hook: The thirty seconds spent waiting for a pan to heat are used to put the spice back and drop the spoon in the crock, and nothing is left over afterwards.
short.standalone_note: Name the trigger, a pan going on to heat, in the opening line, since the reset is invisible without it.

close.standard_beat: Hold the finished zone: oil, salt, and the turner within one reach of the burner, six tools in the crock, handles turned in, clear landing space beside the hob, clean filter back in its clip. Then the trigger shown once, a pan going on to heat and the small reset happening in the wait, so the standard is seen being held rather than described.
close.next_zone_teaser: Follow the dirty grates to the sink, where the whole kitchen resets from, and where the cleaners under the cabinet have been multiplying.

shot_list: Overhead locked off on hob and one step of surround, for before and after
Three-quarter at hob height for reach and handle moves
Macro on hood underside and filter in raking light
Close on the grate soak and the sink water after the filter wash
Low angle at child eye line for the handle hazard, no person in frame
Close on the fire blanket or extinguisher in its mounted position
Insert on the ready state photo being taped inside the cabinet door
Overhead on the spice drawer, lids read from above
videos.description_hook: The cooking zone is judged with your hands busy and the heat already on, which is why it gets arranged by the moment of need. Six passes, Sort through Sustain, including the hood filter nobody has taken out.

videos.title: The Empty Sink Standard: 6S for the Sink and Dishwashing Zone
videos.cold_open_problem: Close on one pan sitting in the basin under grey water, then a second dish joining it, then a third. Name the problem: soaking is the word a kitchen uses for postponing, and one soaking pan gives every other dish permission to join it. The call this zone turns on is not what to keep, it is whether the basin is allowed to be a staging area, and what deadline a pan actually gets.

segments.covers: Everything comes out from under the sink, because that cabinet has been collecting what does not belong in a damp space.
beats: Pull every bottle and box out from under the sink and line them up on the floor where they can be counted.
Combine the three half empty bottles of the same spray into one, and bin what has separated or lost its label.
Move out anything that is not dish, sink, or plumbing related, the spare bulbs, the paper goods, the vase, on the grounds that a damp cabinet under a working trap is the wrong home for them.
End on one tray holding dish soap, dishwasher tablets, and one all-purpose cleaner, with the pipes visible around it.
shots: Three-quarter, cabinet doors open on the full contents
Overhead, everything lined up on the floor on a towel
Close, two matching sprays combined into one bottle
Three-quarter, the single tray going back with the pipes visible behind it

short.hook: The cabinet under a kitchen sink is emptied onto the floor, and three half empty bottles of the same spray line up next to each other.
short.standalone_note: Say this is the under sink cabinet and that damp storage next to the pipes is why the category rule is this narrow.

segments.covers: Everything at this basin has to work for one wet hand.
beats: Put the soap and the brush in a caddy that lifts with one wet hand, and wipe the counter underneath in the same motion.
Move the dishwasher tablets into a container beside the machine rather than across the room in a cupboard.
Fit a towel bar within reach of somebody already standing at the basin with wet hands, showing the reach from that standing position.
shots: Close, caddy lifted with one wet hand and the surface wiped beneath
Three-quarter, tablet container placed beside the dishwasher
Close, hand reaching the towel without stepping away from the basin

short.hook: A soap caddy at a kitchen sink lifts with one wet hand and the counter under it gets wiped in the same motion.
short.standalone_note: Establish the sink zone and the one wet hand test, which is the only rule this Short needs.

segments.covers: The sponge and the dishwasher filter, which is why the glasses come out gritty.
beats: Wring the sponge out and stand it on edge, noting that it only dries on edge and that it retires the day it smells while dry.
Scrub the drain flange and wipe the rubber seal all the way around the dishwasher door, into the folds.
Twist the dishwasher filter out of the machine floor and rinse it, showing what comes off a filter that has never been removed since fitting.
Wipe the basin dry at the end so the finished state is visible, not merely clean.
shots: Macro, sponge wrung and stood on edge in a drainer
Close, brush working the drain flange
Close, filter twisted out of the dishwasher floor and rinsed under the tap
Overhead, basin wiped dry and holding nothing
on_screen_text: Pull the filter, it comes out

short.hook: A cylinder twists out of the floor of a dishwasher, and what rinses off it explains why the glasses have been coming out gritty.
short.standalone_note: Show where the filter sits and how it releases, since many viewers do not know their machine has one.

segments.covers: Bleach and ammonia never share this cabinet or this basin, and this is the kitchen cabinet that earns a latch. This is the 4th S.
beats: Separate the bleach from any ammonia or toilet cleaner, capping both and turning the labels out, and name the gas that will drive you out of the room if they meet in the basin.
Give each a fixed position at opposite ends of the tray so the separation is visible rather than remembered.
Move the kettle, the socket adapter, and any charging phone back out of splash distance of the basin, as this zone's water and electricity question.
Fit a latch if small children live here or visit, and make the point that this is the one kitchen cabinet that genuinely earns one. Cross-reference Chapter 21, the hazard hunt.
shots: Close, two bottles moved apart on the tray with labels turned out
Macro, capped lids and the gap between them
Three-quarter, charging phone and kettle moved back from the basin edge
Close, latch fitted and tested on the cabinet door

short.hook: Two cleaning bottles are walked to opposite ends of a tray under a sink, and the reason is a gas, not tidiness.
short.standalone_note: State that Safety is the fourth of six passes and name the two product types, bleach and ammonia, plainly at the start.

segments.covers: The empty sink standard gets written down where the zone can see it.
beats: Write the standard on a card by hand: dishes in the machine or washed, basin wiped, brush standing, towel hung.
Tape the card inside the cabinet door and check the zone against it line by line on camera.
Land the frozen line as the card goes up, that a standard is the best way you know today, written down. Cross-reference Chapter 23.
shots: Macro, the card being written by hand
Close, card taped inside the cabinet door
Overhead, zone matching the card line by line
on_screen_text: A standard is the best way you know today

short.hook: Four lines get written on a card and taped inside the cabinet door under a sink: dishes done, basin wiped, brush standing, towel hung.
short.standalone_note: Read the four items of the standard on screen, since the Short cannot rely on anything shown earlier.

segments.covers: Two moments hold this zone: the last light off at night, and the coffee brewing in the morning.
beats: At the end of the night, empty the basin and wipe it dry before the kitchen light goes off, shot as one linked sequence ending on the switch.
In the morning, while the coffee brews, check and clear the sink, using time that is already being spent waiting.
Show why the soaking deadline works: it names a moment, the end of the current wash cycle or the next time you leave the room, and moments arrive on their own.
shots: Close, basin wiped dry, then the light switch
Close, coffee brewing with the sink in the same frame
Overhead, an empty dry basin in morning light

short.hook: The last two actions before a kitchen light goes off at night: the basin emptied, then wiped dry.
short.standalone_note: Name both triggers up front, the light going off and the coffee brewing, since the pairing is the whole idea.

close.standard_beat: Hold the finished zone: empty sink, dry basin, one brush and one sponge standing, cleaners on a single tray with the plumbing visible behind them, bleach and ammonia at opposite ends. Then the trigger, coffee brewing while the sink is checked and cleared, so the standard is shown being kept rather than achieved once.
close.next_zone_teaser: Look up from the drying rack to the cabinets above it, and to the mug count nobody in the house wants to do.

shot_list: Overhead locked off on the basin, for before and after
Three-quarter at sink height for caddy, towel, and reach moves
Wide three-quarter on the open under-sink cabinet, bounce card lit
Overhead on the floor lay-out of everything from under the sink
Macro on sponge, drain flange, and door gasket folds
Close on the dishwasher filter twisting out and rinsing
Macro on the standard card being written and taped
Close on the coffee brewing with the sink in frame
videos.description_hook: A sink you can see the bottom of makes every other kitchen decision obvious. Six passes, Sort through Sustain, plus an honest deadline for how long a pan is allowed to soak.

videos.title: 6S for Upper Kitchen Cabinets: Mugs, Plates, and the Second Set of Dishes
videos.cold_open_problem: Overhead on two sets of dishes sharing the same eye level shelf, the everyday one and the good one, or the one from before you moved. Name the problem: both sets are being stored at the height you reach into daily, and then the cabinet gets blamed for being full. The call this zone turns on is the second set, and it is decided by whether anyone has actually eaten off it.

segments.covers: Count the mugs, then count the people who drink from them.
beats: Take every mug in the house out and line them up in a grid, then line up one mug per person who actually drinks from them in a second row beneath.
Pull the conference giveaway, the chipped one, and the one nobody ever chooses, using the chips and crazed glaze as the easy calls that shorten the argument about the rest.
Move to the second set of dishes and size one everyday set to the people who eat here plus two.

Make the second set call on camera. Not on a table in two years and nobody has asked to inherit it, it goes now, whole, somewhere it will be used. Genuinely inherited, then sentiment keeps the objects but not the daily shelf: boxed, labelled, stored outside the kitchen.
shots: Overhead, every mug lined up in a grid on the counter
Overhead, second row showing one mug per drinker
Macro, a chip and a crazed glaze line under raking light
Three-quarter, the second set boxed and labelled
on_screen_text: Everyday set, people here plus two

short.hook: Every mug in a house comes out onto the counter in a grid, then a second row underneath shows one mug per person who drinks from them.
short.standalone_note: Set up the two row comparison in the first seconds, since the grid means nothing without the row underneath.

segments.covers: Daily dishes live between shoulder and eye height, and height is decided by frequency.
beats: Put the dinner plates and everyday bowls at eye level on the side nearest the dishwasher or the table, with the glasses beside them.
Cap plate stacks at about six high and check that every mug lifts without moving another mug, demonstrating both.
Send the serving platters and the punch bowl to the top shelf, treating a step stool once a year as an honest cost.
Keep one category per stack, which is what makes the shelf readable from the doorway.
shots: Three-quarter, plates going to eye level on the dishwasher side
Close, a mug lifted cleanly without disturbing its neighbour
High three-quarter from a raised tripod, platters going onto the top shelf
Close, a plate stack counted to its cap

short.hook: A mug is lifted out of a packed cabinet row without touching a single one beside it, which is the whole test for the shelf.
short.standalone_note: Explain the shoulder to eye height rule and the one mug lift test before the lift, or it looks arbitrary.

segments.covers: Take the shelf completely empty first, because the dust band behind the plates is the finding.
beats: Empty a shelf entirely rather than sliding the stacks aside, then show the band of dust at the back in raking light and what it says about the last time it was cleared.
Wipe the shelf front to back and lift the liner, then clean the ring where a mug has been standing in one spot and the sticky patch on the shelf edge.
Wipe the underside of the cabinet nearest the hob, showing the greasy film that only appears when you look up at it from an angle.
shots: Close, shelf emptied and the dust band revealed at the back
Macro, cloth pass across the dust band and a mug ring on the liner
Low angle from below, greasy film on the cabinet underside in raking light
on_screen_text: Empty the shelf, do not slide
Look at it from an angle

short.hook: A cabinet shelf is emptied instead of shuffled, and a clean line of dust at the back shows exactly where the plates have been sitting.
short.standalone_note: Say which cabinet this is and that emptying completely is the pass itself, not a preference.

segments.covers: Heavy and breakable do not belong above head height, and the step stool is not optional. This is the 4th S.
beats: Bring the casserole stack or the cast iron lid down from overhead with two hands, naming it as the fall, cut, or crush question, and rehome it low.
Move the glassware out of any position at or above head height, since it fails onto a hard floor and onto whoever opened the door.

Show the three improvised standing surfaces this cabinet invites, a chair edge, the counter lip, and an open drawer front, filmed on feet and edges only, then replace all three with a real step stool.
Store the step stool where it can be reached in one move, because a stool that is awkward to get out is a stool nobody uses.
shots: Three-quarter, heavy dish lowered from overhead with two hands, wrists down only
Close, glassware relocated from head height to a low shelf
Close on a chair edge and an open drawer front, framed below the ankles, then a proper stool in their place
Three-quarter, step stool in its storage position
on_screen_text: Never a chair, never a drawer front

short.hook: A cast iron lid comes down from a shelf above head height with two hands, and the weight of it tells the story on its own.
short.standalone_note: State that Safety is the fourth of six passes and give the height rule, nothing heavy above head, before the lift.

segments.covers: Label the shelf edge, not the contents, so anyone can put away correctly without asking.
beats: Write four shelf edge labels, plates, bowls, glasses, mugs, and fix them to the edge rather than to any item.
Have a household member's hands unload a clean dishwasher against those labels, filmed wrists down in a locked off frame, with nothing asked.
Draw the difference: labelling contents describes what happens to be there, labelling the edge decides what belongs there. Cross-reference Chapter 14, visual controls.
shots: Macro, label being written and pressed onto the shelf edge
Three-quarter, cabinet open with all four edges labelled
Close, a second pair of hands putting a plate away without hesitation, wrists down only
on_screen_text: Label the edge, not the item

short.hook: Four labels go onto four shelf edges in one cabinet: plates, bowls, glasses, mugs.
short.standalone_note: Show all four categories on screen, since the labels are the entire content of this Short.

segments.covers: Emptying the dishwasher is the check, and a homeless clean plate is the signal.
beats: Empty a clean dishwasher and put everything away against the labelled edges as the routine check.
Hold a clean plate that has nowhere obvious to go, and read it as the shelf being over its limit rather than as a storage problem.
Make the point that this adds no step, because the dishwasher already gets emptied every day.
shots: Three-quarter, dishwasher opened and unloading begins
Close, a plate hovering with no space to go into
Overhead, the shelf at its limit
on_screen_text: Nowhere to put it means over the limit
Every time the dishwasher gets emptied
