beats: Set one power strip on a hard surface and assign one slot per device, with the owner's name going on the slot.
Coil each cable to the length that just reaches its slot and clip the excess, so the ends stay up on the surface instead of hanging toward the floor.
Walk the room and unplug every other charger, bringing them all in, so this station is genuinely the only charging point.
Leave the empty slots visible during the day, which is what lets anyone read the station in one glance from the doorway.
shots: Tripod at table height on the strip being placed on a hard surface and squared up
Macro on a cable being coiled to length and clipped
Close on cable ends resting up on the surface rather than hanging over the edge
Wide of the room as hands collect chargers from two other sockets

short.hook: A charging cable hangs off a side table almost to the floor, then a clip takes up the slack in one motion.
short.standalone_note: Say this is a family charging station and that cables are cut to just-reach length. Name the hanging loop as the reason in one beat so the clip reads as a fix rather than tidiness.

segments.covers: Inspect the cable ends where the sheath cracks first, and clear the lint out of the charging ports.
beats: Wipe each cable end and inspect the last few centimetres near the plug, where the sheath splits first, and treat a crack there as the finding.
Brush the lint out of the charging ports, since packed lint is why a plug stops seating long before the cable is actually broken.
Show a port before and after and the plug seating fully with no gap, which is the test that says the port was the problem.
shots: Macro on the last few centimetres of a cable near the plug, sheath cracked
Macro into a charging port packed with grey lint
Macro on a soft brush drawing the lint out
Close on the plug seating fully with no gap
on_screen_text: The sheath cracks nearest the plug

short.hook: Macro straight into a phone charging port that is completely packed with grey lint.
short.standalone_note: Establish it is a charging port and state the misdiagnosis in the first line, that people buy a new cable when the port is the problem. The brush-out and the fully seated plug close it.

segments.covers: Nothing charges on soft material, swollen or hot packs come off immediately, cables stay short, and drinks stay off this surface.
beats: State the rule first and clear each thing it names, a tablet off a cushion, a pack out from under a blanket, a phone off a stack of paper, framed as the burn or fire question.
Lay a hand flat on every device on the station once during this pass, since lithium batteries need air and heat is the thing a hand finds first.
Use a clearly labeled stand-in pack to show what stop now looks like, bulging at the seam, and take it off the strip so it does not go back on.

Take the poison, choke, or strangle question to the cable long enough to hang to the floor and loop at a toddler's neck height, then clip it flat, and move the glasses off a surface that holds a live strip.
shots: Overhead on a tablet charging on a cushion, then the same tablet on a hard surface
Close on a hand laid flat across each device on the station in turn
Macro on the labeled stand-in pack with a bulged seam, on-screen note that it is a stand-in
Low camera on a hanging cable loop at toddler height, then the same cable clipped flat
Close on a glass being lifted off the charging table

short.hook: A tablet lies face down charging on a sofa cushion, and a hand lifts it to show the warm hollow underneath.
short.standalone_note: Name the burn or fire question and the rule immediately, nothing charges on soft material. Include the swollen and too hot to hold signs, since a viewer may only ever see this Short.

segments.covers: Names on the slots rather than only on the cables, and the strip left in open view.
beats: Write name labels for the slots themselves rather than for the cables, so an empty slot reads as a missing device rather than as free space.
Show that reading happening, a mid-morning station with two named slots empty and the names answering whose phones are out of the house.

Keep the strip in open view instead of pushed behind furniture, because a scorched socket or a chewed cable behind a sofa goes unnoticed. Point to Chapter 21, the hazard hunt, and to the line, find it, and fix it now.
shots: Macro on name labels being written and placed at each slot on the surface
Overhead on the station mid-morning with two named slots empty
Tripod at table height showing the strip in open view rather than tucked behind furniture
on_screen_text: Name the slot, not just the cable

short.hook: Two slots on a charging station sit empty, and the labels underneath say exactly whose phones are not home.
short.standalone_note: Establish the station and the naming rule in one beat. The insight, that an empty slot reads as a missing device, is the whole Short, so land it on the labels.

segments.covers: Devices come to the station when the dishwasher is started for the night and stay until morning.
beats: Show the dishwasher door closing and the cycle starting, and hang the habit there, because it is the last thing anyone does in this house before phones would otherwise walk to bedrooms.
Bring every device to the station in one trip rather than announcing a rule, and show them staying there until morning.
End on every named slot filled, the strip in view on a hard surface, and nothing charging anywhere else in the room.
shots: Close on a dishwasher door closing and the cycle button being pressed
Tripod at table height on hands carrying phones and a tablet to the station in one trip
Overhead on every named slot filled
Wide of the room at night with the station lit and in view

short.hook: A dishwasher cycle button is pressed, and the next shot is three phones landing on their named slots.
short.standalone_note: Name the room and the trigger in the first beat. The one-trip carry is the demonstration and the full station is the payoff, so both must be in the Short.

close.standard_beat: Hold the station and read the standard against what is visible: one strip on a hard surface, one named slot per device, one labeled bag of spare connectors, no charger plugged in anywhere else in the room, and nothing charging on soft material. Then show the trigger once, the dishwasher started and the devices coming to the station for the night.
close.next_zone_teaser: The table where the glass could not go is next, and something on it has been half finished for months.

shot_list: Overhead arm on a table for the cable line-up, the device matching, and the recycling sweep
Macro handheld for plug sheaths, ports, lint, and slot labels
Tripod at table height on the strip for placement and the nightly fill
Low camera at toddler height for the hanging cable loop and the clipped fix
Cushion and hard surface pair setup for the charging comparison, with the labeled stand-in pack
Kitchen setup on the dishwasher for the trigger, cut to the station in the same evening light
Night wide of the room with the station in open view
videos.description_hook: One charging station for the whole house, on a surface that can take the heat: named slots so an empty one means a missing phone, cables shortened to just reach, and nothing charging on a cushion. Hands only, no presenter.

videos.title: Bins Named for What They Make: Resetting a Family Craft Corner
videos.cold_open_problem: Open on a bag holding something started with real enthusiasm and abandoned in the middle, sitting on the good end of the work surface with dust along its top edge. Set out why it stays: clearing it feels like quitting, so nothing else gets started on that surface. Establish the test the video runs on, naming the very next physical action and the day you will do it, and make clear that failing to produce both halves is itself the answer.

segments.covers: Every marker is tested on a scrap, dried and separated supplies go, and the abandoned project either gets a next action and a date or gets broken down.
beats: Draw every marker across one scrap sheet, because the cap tells you nothing and the sheet tells you everything, and let the gaps build in the row.
Bin the dried glue sticks and the paint that has separated, showing the stir attempt failing so the judgement is visible rather than asserted.
Search once for the missing instruction sheet on camera, and discard the kit only after the search fails.

Work the call on the abandoned project: name the very next physical action and the day, not the goal, and when it stalls, break the project down, good materials back into the paper, drawing, and glue bins, the partly worked piece to somebody who will finish it or out.
shots: Overhead on a row of markers drawn one after another across a single scrap sheet
Close on a stir stick lifting separated paint that will not recombine
Overhead on a kit box with no instruction sheet, phone beside it mid-search
Overhead on the abandoned project being unpacked and its materials sorted back into the bins
on_screen_text: Materials go back to the bins

short.hook: Overhead: a row of markers drawn one after another across a single scrap sheet, and several leave nothing behind at all.
short.standalone_note: Establish this is a family craft supply sort and give the rule in the first line, a cap tells you nothing. Hold on the finished scrap sheet with its gaps as the payoff.

segments.covers: Four lidded bins packed by what gets made, each one liftable to the table and back in one hand.
beats: Pack each bin by what gets made rather than by material, with the drawing bin taking paper, pencils, and the sharpener together.
Show what that avoids by walking the shelves the old way first, three stops to start one drawing.
Set the four bins, paper and card, drawing, glue and tape, kits in progress, and lift each one out to the table one-handed.
Carry the same bin back to its slot the same way, so the trip works in both directions and a child can make it too.
shots: Overhead on the drawing bin being packed with paper, pencils, and the sharpener together
Close on the four labeled bins in a row on the shelf
Tripod at table height on one bin lifted one-handed and carried to the table
Tripod at table height on the same bin going back into its shelf slot

short.hook: A hand takes paper off one shelf, pencils off another, and the sharpener off a third, then cuts to all three sitting in one bin.
short.standalone_note: Say this is a family craft shelf and give the principle in one line, pack by what gets made rather than by material. The one-handed carry closes it.

segments.covers: Scrape the surface before wiping, clear the glitter out of the seams, and dry brushes bristle up.
beats: Scrape dried glue and paint off the work surface with a plastic scraper before any cloth touches it, and show what wiping first would have smeared.
Get into the table seams where glitter sits, showing the tool that actually reaches into them.
Stand the brushes bristle up to dry and put a bent head next to a straight one, so the cost of drying them the other way is visible.
shots: Macro on a plastic scraper lifting dried glue off the work surface in one pass
Macro along a table seam packed with glitter, before and after
Close on brushes standing bristle up in a jar
Macro comparing a bent bristle head against a straight one

short.hook: Macro: a plastic scraper takes a long ribbon of dried glue off a craft table in one unbroken pass.
short.standalone_note: Establish the craft work surface and the order in the first line, scrape before you wipe. Use the brush drying comparison as a fast second half.

segments.covers: The glue gun is the real hazard here, and knives, beads, and solvents go up high rather than into a floor-level bin.
beats: Name the glue gun as the hazard and show why, framed as the burn or fire question: no obvious off signal, a tip that stays hot long after the last bead, and a plug left in on a surface a child reaches.
Give it a fixed cooling spot on a hard tile and pull the plug before the clean-up starts, demonstrated in that order rather than described.
Take the fall, cut, or crush question to craft knives and sharp-point scissors, and turn the scissors point down in the cup instead of blade up.
Take the poison, choke, or strangle question to seed beads, googly eyes, and pompoms in a room a crawling child shares, and move them with the glue and the solvent based markers to a high shelf.
shots: Close on a glue gun tip with a bead still forming, then the plug being pulled at the wall
Tripod at table height on the gun placed on its hard tile in a marked spot
Macro on scissors turned point down into a cup
Overhead on seed beads, googly eyes, and pompoms being lidded and moved to a high shelf
Low camera confirming that shelf is above the youngest child's reach mark

short.hook: A glue gun sits on a tile with a bead still hanging from the tip, and a hand pulls its plug at the wall without touching the gun.
short.standalone_note: Establish that this is a craft table children use and name the specific danger, no off signal and a tip that stays hot. Give the fixed cooling tile as the fix so the Short ends with a setup, not a scare.

segments.covers: One project out at a time, and each lidded bin labeled with what it makes rather than what it holds.
beats: Set the rule, one project bin out at a time, and show what it protects, a work surface that otherwise fills from both ends.
Write two candidate labels for the same bin, one naming the material and one naming what it makes, and choose on camera.
Hold the state the rule produces, one clear work surface with exactly one bin on it and the other three lidded and named on the shelf.
shots: Macro on two candidate labels side by side, one naming a material and one naming what it makes
Close on the chosen label going onto the bin front
Overhead on the clear work surface with exactly one bin on it
Tripod at table height on the shelf with the other three bins lidded and named
on_screen_text: One project out at a time

short.hook: Two labels for the same craft bin sit side by side, one naming the contents and one naming what it makes, and a hand picks up the second.
short.standalone_note: Establish this is a craft bin and let the two labels carry the idea without needing the parent video. Close on the clear surface with one bin out so the rule has a visible result.

segments.covers: When the table is being set for dinner, the open project bin closes and goes back whatever state the project is in.
beats: Show placemats and cutlery landing on the far end of the same surface the project bin is on, since dinner and craft compete for this one table every evening.
Press the lid onto a genuinely mid-project bin and put it back on the shelf, because that resistance is the whole habit.
End on the clear surface with the table set beside it, which is what makes tomorrow's restart one motion instead of an excavation.
shots: Close on placemats and cutlery entering frame at the edge of the work surface
Overhead on a half-worked project having its lid pressed on
Tripod at table height on the bin going back to its named shelf slot
Overhead on the clear surface with the table set beside it
on_screen_text: Table gets set, bin gets closed

short.hook: A lid presses down on a craft project that is visibly half finished, and it goes back on the shelf anyway.
short.standalone_note: Name the trigger in the opening beat, the table being set for dinner in a room where craft and dinner share one surface. The resistance is the lesson, so the lid closing on unfinished work is the hook.

close.standard_beat: Hold the finished corner and read the standard against it: four lidded bins labeled by what they make, one project bin out on a clear surface, the glue gun unplugged on its tile, and knives, beads, and solvents above the youngest child's reach. Then run the trigger once in real use, the table being set and the open bin closing and going back whatever state the project is in.
close.next_zone_teaser: That is all six zones in this room, and the next room starts at the door everybody comes in through.

shot_list: Overhead arm fixed above the craft work surface for marker testing, bin packing, and the dinner trigger
Macro handheld for scraping, glitter seams, brush bristles, labels, and the glue gun tip
Tripod at table height for the one-handed bin carries to and from the shelf
Low camera at child reach height for the high shelf confirmation
Shelf-face setup for the four labeled bins and the scissors cup
Glue gun station on its hard tile with the wall socket in frame, gun cold and unplugged between takes
Dinner setup with placemats entering the edge of the work surface in the same light
videos.description_hook: A family room craft corner where a project starts in one motion and the surface clears just as fast: four lidded bins named for what they make, scissors point down, and the glue gun on a fixed cooling tile. Hands only, no presenter.

rooms.room_note: One person, one tripod, window light. Shoot on a clear morning with the curtains fully open and the overhead light off, because the bedroom ceiling fitting sits directly above the bed and throws a hard shadow of the camera into every overhead frame. Bounce a white board off the wall opposite the window to lift the shadow side of the bed. Two positions carry the whole room: a low three-quarter at the foot of the bed for wide work, and an overhead arm clamped to a stand for drawer, nightstand and dresser tops, set up on the side of the bed away from the door so the walking strip stays clear for the Safety frames. Everything is locked off. There are no tracking, following or handheld travel shots in this room, so movement is carried by hands entering and leaving a static frame. Strip and remake the bed yourself before you start rolling so the linen reads clean. Take the closet door off its hinges rather than squeezing a tripod into the opening. Save the two darkened passes, the bedside floor strip and the closet floor, for last: close the curtains, shoot both, then stop for the day rather than trying to get daylight back. On-set safety: the dresser anti-tip strap and the closet rod brackets are filmed as real fixes, so have a stud finder, the correct fixings and a driver on hand. Never stage a loaded chest with two drawers open as an unanchored tip demonstration; the strap goes in first and the shot shows it taking the load. Extinguish the candle before filming the sleeve pass. Keep your own lamp and camera cables out of the same floor strip the video tells viewers to keep bare.

videos.title: Bed and Bedding: Two Sheet Sets and a Clear Floor
videos.cold_open_problem: Open on a linen shelf with four or five sets stacked on it, hands lifting each one out in turn: the wedding gift, the new set that turns out to be scratchy, the good set still in its wrapper. Name the honest number the manual gives, two per bed, one on and one clean, and name the one condition that earns a third, which is a child or a pet who actually sleeps here and a bed you have stripped in the middle of the night within the last year. Land the specific discomfort that the good set has never been slept on, and promise the video ends with it on the bed.

segments.covers: Stripping the bed and pulling out everything underneath it, and knowing which linen is genuinely finished rather than demoted to a spare.
beats: Strip the bed completely and pull out what is actually under it: the wrapping paper, the shoe boxes, the box of paperwork nobody filed, none of which belongs to sleep and all of which is here because the door usually stays shut.
Show the three retirement tests on real items: a sheet worn thin at the hip held up to the window, a blanket gone pilled and scratchy under the hand, a pillow bent in half that stays folded.
Explain that these leave as rags or textile recycling and not as spares for a guest who never comes, and bag them on camera.
Count the surviving sets against the two per bed standard and set the good one aside for tonight.
shots: Three-quarter wide from the foot of the bed, hands pulling the fitted sheet off the corners.
Overhead of the floor filling with bins, shoe boxes and wrapping paper coming out from under the bed.
Backlit close on a sheet held to the window so the thin patch at the hip reads on camera.
Macro on a pillow folded in half by two hands and staying folded when released.
on_screen_text: Strip it, then look under it

short.hook: A pillow bent in half by two hands that just stays folded, with the retirement test named in the first seconds.
short.standalone_note: Re-establish that this is a bed and bedding reset and that the pillow is being tested, not played with, because the folded-pillow shot is meaningless without the test being named up front.

segments.covers: Storing each set folded inside one of its own pillowcases, keeping this bed's linen off the guest and kid shelves, and putting the good set on tonight.
beats: Fold a full set flat on the bare mattress and slide the whole bundle into one of its own pillowcases.
Explain that this stops the flat sheet and the fitted sheet travelling separately, which is the actual failure it fixes.
Show the linen shelf reorganised so this bed's two sets sit on one shelf rather than stacked in with guest doubles and kid singles.
Make the bed with the good set, the one that has never been slept on, because a sheet saved for an occasion is a sheet nobody ever uses.
shots: Overhead of the fold sequence on the bare mattress, hands only, single continuous framing.
Close on the bundle sliding into the pillowcase and the case being squared off.
Three-quarter of the linen shelf before and after, matched framing on a locked tripod.
Close on the good set coming out of its wrapper and the fitted sheet going onto the first corner.
on_screen_text: This bed gets its own shelf
The good set goes on tonight

short.hook: A whole sheet set disappearing into its own pillowcase in one motion, overhead.
short.standalone_note: Say what the bundle contains and which bed it belongs to, since the fold shot alone reads as a folding tip rather than a storage rule.

segments.covers: Cleaning the mattress and behind the headboard while the bed is bare, which is the only moment either is reachable.
beats: With the mattress bare, vacuum the whole surface and then work the seam where the protector tucks under.
Feed the vacuum head down behind the headboard and show the dust and hair packed against the wall there, which is cleaning to inspect rather than to impress.
Note that the cases get washed constantly and the pillows inside them almost never do, and put the pillows themselves through the machine as the seasons turn.
shots: Overhead of the vacuum head crossing the bare mattress in overlapping passes.
Macro on the protector seam being lifted and the nozzle going into it.
Low three-quarter from beside the bed, hands feeding the vacuum head down the gap behind the headboard.
Close on the pillows going into the machine drum.
on_screen_text: Wash the pillows, not just the cases

short.hook: The vacuum head going down the gap behind the headboard, into a space the viewer has never cleaned.
short.standalone_note: Establish that the bed is stripped and that this gap is only reachable now, or the shot reads as ordinary vacuuming.

segments.covers: The floor strip you cross in the dark, and the weight sitting above a sleeping head.
beats: Frame the first hazard as fall: hold a locked low frame on the strip of floor between the bed and the door with a storage bin corner, a shoe and a charging cable sitting in it.
Clear the strip on camera and set the rule that nothing goes under the bed that sticks out into it, so the under-bed bins sit flat and fully back.
Frame the second hazard as fall, cut or crush: framed pictures, a speaker and a stack of books on a headboard ledge sitting directly over a sleeping head.
Show the two acceptable outcomes, moving them off entirely or fixing them into the wall properly, and drive a fixing into the wall on camera.
shots: Locked low frame along the bare floor strip from bedside to door, curtains closed to read as night.
Close on a bin corner and a coiled cable being lifted out of the strip.
Three-quarter from the side of the bed looking up at the headboard ledge with the pillow in frame beneath it.
Close on hands driving a fixing into the wall behind a frame.

short.hook: A darkened floor between a bed and a bedroom door with a bin corner and a cable lying in it, framed as what your foot finds at three in the morning.
short.standalone_note: Name the room and the moment in the first line, because the darkened floor strip is unreadable without knowing it is a bedside walking route at night.

segments.covers: Writing down what a made bed means in this house, precisely enough that it looks the same whoever does it.
beats: Make the bed to the agreed state and hold the wide as the reference frame.
Show the standard being written down to the pillow count and whether the duvet is folded back or pulled flat, because those two details are what drift between people.
Leave the written standard where the linen lives, and quote the frozen rule line that a standard is the best way you know today, written down.
Photograph the finished bed and point to Chapter 25 and the ideal-state photo as why the photo goes on the linen shelf.
shots: Locked three-quarter wide of the finished made bed, held long enough to work as a reference frame.
Overhead close on the standard being written out by hand.
Close on a phone photographing the made bed and the photo being tucked onto the linen shelf.

short.hook: Two beds cut back to back that differ only in pillow count and duvet fold, showing what an unwritten standard costs a household.
short.standalone_note: State in the opening seconds that both beds were made by different people in the same house on different mornings, which is the entire point of the comparison.

segments.covers: Making the bed before you leave the room, and using the sheet wash as the trigger to look underneath.
beats: Show the one-pull version, duvet still thrown back, done in the moment before leaving the room.
Contrast with the ten o'clock version where yesterday's clothes have to come off the bed first, which is why the habit is placed where it is and not later.
Attach the under-bed check to stripping the sheets for the wash, so the space under the bed gets seen every time the linen cycles.
shots: Three-quarter of hands pulling the duvet up in a single motion beside a still-warm bed.
Matched shot later in the day with clothing piled on the cover, hands clearing it first.
Overhead of a stripped bed with hands sweeping under it before the clean set goes on.

short.hook: The same bed made twice in one clip, once in a single pull and once after a pile of clothes has to come off it first.
short.standalone_note: Establish that the only difference between the two is the time of day, not the person and not the bed.

close.standard_beat: Return to the finished wide: two sets for this bed each folded inside its own pillowcase, the agreed pillow count on the cover and nothing else, the good set actually on the bed, and a bare floor strip on both sides. Show the trigger as a physical sequence, sheets coming off for the wash and hands going under the bed before the clean set goes back on.
close.next_zone_teaser: Next, the smallest zone in this room and the one you look at last thing and first thing, your own nightstand.

shot_list: Locked three-quarter wide from the foot of the bed, used for the made-bed reference and every before and after pair.
Overhead arm over the mattress for the strip, the vacuum passes and the fold sequence.
Locked low frame along the bedside floor strip, curtains closed, shot last with the closet floor pass.
Close on hands at the mattress protector seam and behind the headboard.
Backlit close at the window for the worn sheet and the folded pillow tests.
Three-quarter on the linen shelf, matched before and after.
Close on hands writing the made-bed standard and photographing the finished bed.
Close on hands fixing a frame into the wall above the headboard.
videos.description_hook: Two sheet sets per bed, one on and one clean, and a floor strip you can cross barefoot in the dark. This is the bed and bedding zone from the Micro Zone Manual, worked start to finish through all six S's.

videos.title: Your Nightstand: Five Things or Fewer, and the Phone Charger Decision
videos.cold_open_problem: Open overhead on a nightstand top with the phone charging on it, and name the trade the manual names: you know the phone should not sleep here and you have kept it because it is your alarm. Show that as one job a small clock already does. Set up the two honest routes the video makes you pick between, moving the charger across the room to the dresser or keeping it face down and taking something else off the top so you are still at five, and say plainly that the option gone is calling the current arrangement temporary.

segments.covers: Emptying the drawer onto the bed, clearing the four books you started, and settling the phone charger one way or the other.
beats: Tip the whole drawer out onto the bed in one movement and let the volume land before sorting starts.
Work the four named categories on camera: dead pens tested on paper, chargers for phones nobody owns any more, hotel earplugs still in their wrappers, and the started-and-abandoned books.
Apply the book rule as the manual states it, that a book you are not reading this week belongs on the shelf and not beside your head, and carry three of the four out.

Settle the charger on camera rather than deferring it: the clock goes onto the top and the charger is carried to the dresser across the room, with the honest alternative shown as a second option, charger stays, phone face down, and something else leaves the top.
Count the remaining items on the top with a finger to land on five or fewer.
shots: Overhead of the drawer inverting onto the bedspread, single take.
Close on hands scribbling each pen on a pad and dropping the dead ones into a pot.
Close on a stack of four part-read books, hands lifting all but one out of frame.
Close on the charger being unplugged from the nightstand and set down on the dresser across the room, with the clock going into its place.
Overhead of the cleared top with the remaining items counted by a finger.

short.hook: A whole nightstand drawer tipped onto a bed in one motion, with the five things or fewer target named before the pile lands.
short.standalone_note: Name the zone and the target number immediately, so the pile has a destination and the Short is not just a shot of mess.

segments.covers: Dividing the drawer into named sections and getting every cord off the surface.
beats: Fit dividers so glasses, lip balm and earplugs each get their own section instead of sliding into one heap.
Apply the test from the manual, naming what is in each section with the drawer still shut and then opening it to check.
Clip the lamp and clock cords down the back leg so nothing loops across the top, and hold a surface-level frame with no cable crossing it.
shots: Overhead of dividers going into the empty drawer and each section being filled.
Overhead of the drawer shut, then opening to confirm the three named sections.
Low three-quarter behind the nightstand, hands running clips down the back leg.
Close along the bare top at surface level, no cable in the frame.

short.hook: Three drawer sections named on screen while the drawer is still shut, then the drawer opens to prove the names right.
short.standalone_note: Set the naming up as a test of the storage before performing it, or it reads as somebody listing objects.

segments.covers: The water ring on the top, and the lampshade and bulb that have been quietly dimming your reading light.
beats: Lift everything off and wipe the top, working at the ring the water glass has been leaving.
Wash the lampshade and the bulb, which is what gets your reading light back to the brightness you paid for.
Cut a before and after of the lamp switched on in identical conditions, showing the difference without claiming a number.
shots: Overhead of the bare top with hands working the water ring in one continuous pass.
Close on the shade being lifted off and washed, and the cooled bulb being wiped.
Locked three-quarter of the lamp lit before and after, identical framing and exposure.
on_screen_text: Wash the shade and the bulb

short.hook: A bedside lamp switched on before and after its shade and bulb are washed, in one locked frame.
short.standalone_note: State that framing and exposure are unchanged between the two, because a brightness comparison is worthless if the viewer suspects the camera did it.

segments.covers: Water and electricity sharing one small surface, and open flame at bedding height.
beats: Frame the first hazard as water and electricity: an open glass beside the lamp base, a charger and a power strip all crowded onto one small top, one knocked elbow from a problem.
Perform both fixes on camera, the power strip moving down to the floor behind the nightstand and the open glass being swapped for a bottle with a lid.
Frame the second as burn or fire: a candle sitting level with the bedding and directly in the path your sleeve takes reaching for the lamp.
Move the candle to the dresser and set the rule that if you want one burning at night it burns there.
shots: Low surface-level three-quarter showing glass, lamp base, charger and strip crowded in one plane.
Close on hands lifting the power strip down behind the nightstand and dressing the cable.
Close on the open glass being replaced by a lidded bottle on the same coaster.
Side-on close of a sleeve passing directly over a candle at bedding height, flame extinguished before the pass is filmed.

short.hook: A sleeve passing straight over a bedside candle at bedding height on the reach to the lamp, shot side on.
short.standalone_note: Establish that this is a nightstand and a nightly reaching motion, and say plainly that the flame is out for the filmed pass.

segments.covers: Five things or fewer, countable from the doorway, and knowing what the sixth item usually is.
beats: Put the camera at the doorway and count the top from there, showing the standard is checkable without walking over.
Name the manual's observation that the sixth item is almost always a finished book or an empty glass, and show the sixth appearing.
Route both on camera, the finished book going to the shelf and the empty glass going to the kitchen that night.
shots: Doorway-height three-quarter of the nightstand across the room, items countable in frame.
Overhead close as a sixth item lands on the top and is picked up.
Locked close on a shelf as the book arrives, and on the bedroom door as the glass leaves frame.
on_screen_text: The sixth is a book or a glass

short.hook: Counting a nightstand top from the bedroom doorway without walking over or touching anything.
short.standalone_note: Give the number and the reason for counting from a distance, so the shot reads as a daily check and not as a camera position.

segments.covers: Using the reach for the lamp switch as the moment the top goes back to five.
beats: Show the habit exactly where the manual puts it, in the reach across to switch off the lamp, with the hand putting the sixth thing back before it returns.
Show that the reset finishes inside the reach itself, with the lamp off and no second trip made and nothing to remember tomorrow.
Cut to the same top the next morning to show what waking to a clear surface actually looks like.
shots: Low three-quarter from pillow height, a hand reaching across, resetting an item and returning.
Close on the lamp switch under the same hand in the same motion.
Overhead of the top in morning light, unchanged from the night before.
on_screen_text: Reset on the way to the switch

short.hook: One hand reaching for a bedside lamp switch, putting the nightstand top back to five things on the way, and never making a second trip.
short.standalone_note: Name the trigger as the lamp reach and the target as five in the opening line, since the motion is small and easily missed.

close.standard_beat: Finish on the overhead: lamp, lidded bottle on its coaster, one book, a small dish with your glasses, five or fewer and no cable crossing the surface. Open the drawer to show three named sections with room left in each. Show the trigger as the physical reach for the lamp switch, with the top going back to five inside that movement.
close.next_zone_teaser: Next, the other side of the bed, and the one zone in this room that is not yours to decide about.

shot_list: Overhead arm locked over the nightstand top, the spine of the whole video.
Overhead of the drawer inverted onto the bed and of the dividers going in.
Low surface-level three-quarter for the crowded-top hazard and the candle pass.
Doorway-height three-quarter across the room for the countable-from-the-doorway check.
Locked three-quarter of the lit lamp, matched before and after the shade wash.
Behind-the-nightstand close for cord clipping and the power strip relocation.
Close on the charger leaving the nightstand and landing on the dresser.
Pillow-height low three-quarter of the hand reaching for the lamp switch.
Morning overhead of the untouched top.
videos.description_hook: Five things or fewer on the top, countable from the doorway, and a drawer where every section has a name. The nightstand zone from the Micro Zone Manual, including the phone charger decision made on camera.

videos.title: The Shared Bedroom Nightstand: You Clean, They Cull
videos.cold_open_problem: Open on two nightstands in one frame, one finished and one untouched, and name the fight the manual names: you want to fix that side because you can see it from yours, and every argument about tidiness in a shared bedroom starts right here. State the rule that settles it, that you may wipe, vacuum and straighten anything on that side and may not remove a single object from it, and flag the one exception the video ends up handling out loud, which is out of date medication, because that is a safety question and not a taste question.

segments.covers: The sort you do not do, and how the offer gets made instead.
beats: Carry a bin liner and a box in and set them down beside the other nightstand, unopened, so the offer has something to point at.
Show your own side already finished to standard, because finishing first is the only argument you are allowed to make.
Show only what gets handed over going into the liner, one item at a time, with the drawer never being tipped out and no pile ever being made.
Hold on the closed drawer and the untouched top to land the discipline, that what they keep stays and you say nothing about it.
shots: Wide three-quarter holding both nightstands, one finished and one untouched.
Close on a bin liner and box set down on the floor beside the untouched side, lids closed.
Close on a single item entering frame from the far side of the bed and going into the liner.
Overhead of the closed drawer with hands resting on the top and not opening it.

short.hook: A hand resting on a closed bedside drawer in a shared bedroom and deliberately not opening it, with the rule that stops it stated out loud.
short.standalone_note: Establish that this is a shared bedroom and the other sleeper's side within the first line, or the restraint has no meaning at all.

segments.covers: Agreeing only on the shared edge, the floor and the cord, and leaving the drawer entirely alone.
beats: Define the shared edge on camera, the floor beside this nightstand that you both walk past.
Clear that floor and run the lamp cord down the leg, and explain that both qualify because they affect the person who does not sleep on this side.
Open the drawer once, show that its contents are entirely their business, and close it again without a hand going in.
shots: Low overhead of the shared floor beside the nightstand, before and after clearing.
Close on hands dressing the lamp cord down the back leg to the skirting.
Close on the drawer opened briefly and closed, no hand entering it.

short.hook: Drawing the line in a shared bedroom between the floor beside the bed, which you may fix, and the bedside drawer, which you may not.
short.standalone_note: State the shared bedroom setup and that there are two owners, because the whole distinction collapses without it.

segments.covers: Cleaning is the part you are fully allowed to do, including the slot neither of you looks into.
beats: Dust the top and wipe the lamp base and the switch, working around objects rather than clearing them off their spots.
Vacuum the slot between the nightstand and the bed frame where tissues, hairbands and dust collect, and tip out what comes back.
Land that this is the clean half of you clean, they cull, and that it happens without a word about what is on the top.
shots: Overhead of a cloth working around objects rather than clearing them off.
Macro on the lamp switch and base being wiped.
Low three-quarter with a crevice tool going into the slot between nightstand and bed frame.
Close on what the vacuum brings out, tipped onto a sheet of paper.

short.hook: A crevice tool going into the gap between a bed frame and a nightstand, and the tissues and hairbands that come back out.
short.standalone_note: Name the gap and why nobody ever cleans it, since the shot is visually narrow and hard to place without context.

segments.covers: Medication, the one exception where you are allowed to raise the subject out loud.
beats: Frame this as poison, choke or strangle and show why: sleep aids and prescription bottles loose in an open bedside drawer sit at the height a toddler or a dog reaches from the mattress.
Show the check as a joint job rather than a raid, dates read off the bottles and caps screwed down properly.
Move tablets from the open drawer into a closed box, under the manual's condition that this applies where a child or a dog gets up onto this bed.
Handle the fall question on this side too, taking the lamp cord out of the walking strip and running it down the leg and along the wall.
shots: Bed-height close from the mattress looking into an open drawer, showing the reach line.
Close on bottles turned to the light and dates read off the caps.
Close on caps screwed down and bottles going into a closed box.
Low overhead of the walking strip with the cord relocated to the skirting.
on_screen_text: Ch 21: find it, and fix it now

short.hook: The view from mattress height into an open bedside drawer full of loose pill bottles, at exactly the reach of a small child or a dog climbing onto the bed.
short.standalone_note: Establish the camera height as mattress level and the room as a bedroom, because the framing is carrying the entire point.

segments.covers: Matching the standard rather than the contents, so two different drawers can both be correct.
beats: Put both tops in one frame and show the same item count and the same lidded drink rule holding on each.
Show both drawers open with contents that match at nothing, and land why that is completely fine under this standard.

Write the shared standard down and leave it where both sleepers see it, and quote the frozen line from Chapter 27, that an audit checks the home, not the household, and what it finds is always a system to fix, never a person to blame.
shots: Wide locked frame holding both nightstand tops, counts matching.
Two matched overheads of each drawer open, paired in the edit to sit side by side.
Close on the shared standard written down and left where both can see it.
on_screen_text: Match the standard, not the drawer

short.hook: Two bedside drawers in the same room, obviously nothing alike inside, both passing the same written standard.
short.standalone_note: State the standard being matched before the reveal, or the clip reads as two untidy drawers and nothing else.

segments.covers: Tying both tops to the sheet wash so one side cannot quietly drift while the other holds.
beats: Show the sheets coming off and both tops being cleared and wiped inside that same job.
Land why pairing them works, that the wash happens to the whole bed and not to one person, so neither side gets a turn skipped.
Finish the pass with both tops wiped, both lamps back, and the same count standing on each.
shots: Wide three-quarter of the bed being stripped with both nightstands in frame.
Matched close on each top being cleared and wiped in turn.
Final wide with both tops reset and the clean set going on.

short.hook: Sheets coming off a bed triggering both bedside tops getting cleared, not just the tidy one.
short.standalone_note: Say this is a shared bedroom and that pairing the two sides to one job is the whole reason the trigger works.

close.standard_beat: Finish on the pair: matching item counts on both tops, the same lidded drink rule, a lamp cord running down the leg instead of across the floor, medication in date and closed away, and drawer contents belonging to whoever sleeps on that side. Show the trigger physically, sheets going into the wash and both tops cleared and wiped in the same pass.
close.next_zone_teaser: Next, the surface where your pockets land at the end of the day, and the perfume you were given and never wear.

shot_list: Wide locked three-quarter holding both nightstands, the reference frame for every comparison.
Overhead over the second nightstand top and drawer.

Wide of the bed being stripped with both nightstands in shot.
videos.description_hook: You clean, they cull. The one nightstand in the house you are not allowed to empty, and the single exception where you get to raise it out loud.

videos.title: Dresser Top: One Tray, an Anti-Tip Strap, and the Perfume You Never Wear
videos.cold_open_problem: Open overhead on three or four fragrance bottles standing on a dresser top, hands lifting each in turn. Name the honest count from the manual, that you wear one of them, and name why the others are still standing there: they were gifts, or they were expensive, or they were who you were five years ago. Set up the test the video applies, that fragrance turns, and a bottle that has stood open for years smells sharper and flatter than the one you were handed.

segments.covers: Working through pocket sediment, applying the fragrance test, and moving the jewellery that never gets put on.
beats: Show what has actually accumulated here, the loose change, the receipts, the single earrings and snapped chains, swept into one working pile.
Route each category on camera, coins into a jar that lives in another room, receipts binned or photographed, broken jewellery into one small bag.
Set the condition on that bag out loud, that it goes to a repair counter this month or it goes, so it does not quietly become permanent storage.

Apply the fragrance test to the bottles from the cold open: the one you wear stays, the one you honestly alternate to stays, and the rest leave, because whoever gave it to you wanted you to smell good and not to store glass.
Move jewellery you love but never put on to a box in the closet rather than back onto this top.
shots: Overhead of the loaded dresser top before anything is touched.
Close on coins going into a jar and the jar leaving frame toward another room.
Macro on single earrings and a snapped chain going into one small bag.
Close on the fragrance bottles worked one by one, two set back on the dish and the rest lifted out of frame.
Close on the closet jewellery box receiving the loved but unworn pieces.

short.hook: Four perfume bottles on a dresser worked down to the one you actually wear, with the reason each of the others is still standing there named as it goes.
short.standalone_note: Say up front that fragrance turns over years, since without that the clip reads as somebody throwing away expensive gifts for no reason.

segments.covers: One tray for daily carry, a dish for fragrance, and nothing else living on the wood.
beats: Place one valet tray and show keys, wallet, watch and rings all landing inside it.
Group the surviving fragrance on its own small dish so the bottles stop wandering across the top.
Set the rule that folded clothes never rest here on the way to the drawer, and carry a stack straight past the dresser into the drawer instead.
shots: Overhead of the tray being set down and filled item by item.
Close on bottles gathered onto the dish and set back from the edge.
Locked close on the dresser top as a stack of folded laundry passes over it without landing, then a matched frame of it going into the open drawer.

short.hook: A stack of folded laundry travelling over a dresser top without ever touching it and going straight into the drawer below.
short.standalone_note: Name the rule being demonstrated in the first line, because a clip of laundry being put away is otherwise completely unremarkable.

segments.covers: The sticky ring under the fragrance, and the handles that get touched every day.
beats: Take the tray and the bottles off completely and wipe the bare top.
Work at the sticky ring where the sprayer has been misting the wood for years, showing it takes a second pass and does not lift with the first wipe.
Wipe the drawer fronts and the handles while the top is bare, which is the only easy moment to reach them.
shots: Overhead of the fully bare dresser top before the first wipe.
Macro across the sticky ring with the window light coming in low and grazing, so the residue reads on camera.
Close on the second pass working the ring, with the finish coming back.
Close on drawer handles and fronts being wiped.

short.hook: Low grazing light across a dresser top revealing the sticky halo a perfume sprayer has misted into the finish over years.
short.standalone_note: Explain what caused the ring within the first seconds, or the macro shot is an unidentifiable smear on some wood.

segments.covers: Anchoring the chest so it cannot tip, and getting glass back from the edge.
beats: Frame this as fall, cut or crush and show the mechanism: a loaded drawer open puts the weight forward, and a child leaning on it does the rest, on a chest heavy enough to pin someone underneath.
Fit an anti-tip strap into a stud on camera, finding the stud first rather than driving into plasterboard alone.
Reload the drawers with the heaviest clothes at the bottom so the weight sits low, and say why that order is part of the same fix.
Set the glass bottles back from the front edge onto the dish, above a floor you walk to the bed on barefoot.
shots: Low three-quarter of the chest with a loaded drawer open, weight visibly forward of the base.
Close on a stud finder crossing the wall and the mark being made.
Close on the strap being driven into the stud and tensioned at the dresser end.
Overhead of bottles moved from the front edge back onto the dish.

short.hook: A stud finder crossing the wall behind a bedroom dresser, then the anti-tip strap going in, start to finish in one clip.
short.standalone_note: State what the strap prevents and why it must reach a stud rather than plasterboard, so the fix is understood and not just copied.

segments.covers: The tray as the physical edge, and what to do when the day's carry will not sit in it.
beats: Show the tray holding keys, wallet, watch and rings flat, with the rule that anything which will not sit in it does not live on this dresser.
Show the failure state, the same four items stacking on top of each other rather than lying flat.
Apply the two allowed responses, thinning the keyring or moving a ring to the closet jewellery box, and rule out the third by sweeping a second pile back into the tray.
Point to Chapter 14 and visual controls, since the tray outline is doing exactly that job.
shots: Overhead of the tray holding the full daily carry flat, nothing stacked.
Overhead of the same tray overloaded and stacking, matched framing for contrast.
Close on a keyring being thinned and a ring going into the closet box.
Overhead of a second pile forming beside the tray, then being swept back in.

short.hook: A valet tray holding keys, wallet, watch and rings until it cannot, and the two fixes that are allowed when it starts stacking.
short.standalone_note: Establish that the tray is the written standard and not just a dish, and that starting another pile beside it is the failure, since the whole clip hangs on the boundary idea.

segments.covers: Emptying your pockets into the tray at night, with nothing landing beside it.
beats: Show the end of day empty in real motion, keys, wallet, watch and rings going into the tray in one movement.
Land that the tray is the entire instruction, so there is no sorting step and nothing extra to remember at the end of a long day.
Cut to the same top in morning light, bare wood all around a full tray.
shots: Overhead of hands emptying pockets directly into the tray, single take.
Close along the bare wood beside the tray at surface level, nothing on it.
Overhead of the dresser top in morning light with the tray holding the watch and rings.
on_screen_text: Into the tray, not beside it

short.hook: Pockets emptied straight into one tray at the end of the day, with the bare wood beside it staying bare.
short.standalone_note: Name the one tray rule up front so the clip reads as a standard being held rather than somebody putting their keys down.

close.standard_beat: Finish on the overhead: one valet tray holding keys, wallet, watch and rings with nothing outside it, the surviving fragrance grouped on a dish and set back from the front edge, no folded laundry, no receipts, no loose coins on the wood, and the anti-tip strap running from the back of the dresser into the wall. Show the trigger as the nightly pocket empty, everything going into the tray in one motion.
close.next_zone_teaser: Next, the drawers under this top, and the two of them holding clothes that do not fit today.

shot_list: Overhead arm locked over the dresser top, the spine of the video.
Macro on the bare top with the window light coming in low and grazing, for the fragrance ring.
Low three-quarter of the chest with a loaded drawer open, for the forward weight line.
Close on stud finder, strap fixing and tensioning.
Macro on jewellery sorting and the small repair bag.
Close on the fragrance bottles being worked down to the ones that stay.
Locked pair from dresser top to open drawer for the laundry pass-through.
Surface-level close along the bare wood beside the tray.
Morning overhead of the finished top.
videos.description_hook: One valet tray, an anti-tip strap into a stud, and an honest answer about the perfume you were given and never wear. The dresser top zone, worked through all six S's.

videos.title: Dresser Drawers: One Category Each, Folded to Stand Up
videos.cold_open_problem: Open on two drawers being pulled out, part filled with clothes that do not fit today. Name the cost the manual names, that every morning starts with a small unpleasant reminder instead of a clean choice. Set up the decision the video makes on camera: one box, not two, today's date written on the lid, stored somewhere else in the house, and if it is still sealed a year from now it leaves sealed and unopened. Land the reframe, that these drawers dress the body you have this morning, and that this is not giving up on anything.

segments.covers: One drawer at a time onto the bed, the dated box for the wrong size, and knowing what becomes a rag rather than a donation.
beats: Tip one drawer onto the bed and set the rule that you work one drawer at a time, because that is what keeps a job this size finishable.

Work the named categories on camera: socks whose partners never turned up, waistbands that have given up, the six workout tops sitting behind the two that get worn, and the t-shirts from events nobody thinks about now.
Demonstrate the waistband test physically, stretched and released, rather than describing it.
Pack the wrong-size clothes into one box, write today's date on the lid, tape it shut and carry it out of the bedroom entirely, without a second box being started.
Split the disposal, anything stained or holed into textile recycling rather than a donation somebody else has to bin, with the two bags filling separately on camera.
shots: Overhead of one drawer inverting onto the bedspread, single take.
Close on a waistband stretched and released, not returning.
Overhead of unmatched socks laid out in a row with no partners.
Close on today's date written on a box lid, the tape going across and the box leaving frame through the bedroom door.
Close on two labelled bags, textile recycling and donation, filling separately.

short.hook: A waistband stretched and released that stays stretched, deciding the garment on the spot with no second guess.
short.standalone_note: Name the test and say these are dresser drawers being emptied, because the shot is fast and reads as fidgeting without the framing.

segments.covers: Folding so the drawer reads like a row of files, and putting the heavy categories at the bottom.
beats: Teach the upright fold on the bed, repeated until it is legible, so each item stands on its own edge.
Show the difference from above, a drawer you read in one look against a stack you have to excavate.
Add dividers for socks and underwear so the small things stop sliding under the folded rows.
Move jeans and knitwear into the bottom drawers so the weight sits low, which is the same fix the Safety segment is about to test.
shots: Overhead close of the fold sequence on the bed, hands only, one continuous take.
Overhead of the finished drawer open, every item standing on edge and readable.
Overhead of a stacked drawer beside it for contrast, matched framing.
Three-quarter of heavy knitwear being loaded into a bottom drawer.

short.hook: The same dresser drawer shown stacked and then filed upright, from directly above, with one cut between them.
short.standalone_note: State that it is the same drawer holding the same clothes, which is the only thing that makes the comparison land.

segments.covers: Emptying each drawer completely to reach the runners and corners, and fixing what you find there.
beats: Take one drawer fully out and vacuum the corners, the runners and the carcass behind it.
Wipe the base and let it dry fully before anything goes back in, because folded cotton and a damp drawer base do not mix.
Check the runners while the drawer is out and tighten any screw that has worked loose, which is cleaning to inspect rather than to impress.
shots: Three-quarter of a drawer being lifted fully clear of the carcass.
Close inside the empty carcass with the vacuum nozzle in the back corners.
Macro on a runner with a driver tightening a loose screw.
Overhead of the wiped base drying with nothing in it.

short.hook: A dresser drawer pulled completely out and the vacuum going into the carcass behind it, a space most people have never once seen.
short.standalone_note: Explain that the drawer has been fully removed and this is the cavity behind it, since the bare interior is hard to read on its own.

segments.covers: One drawer open at a time, and the loose cedar and mothballs at toddler height.
beats: Frame this as fall, cut or crush and show the mechanism with the anti-tip strap already fitted from the dresser top video: two loaded drawers out together and the strap visibly pulling taut, which is the load that would otherwise go forward with nothing holding it.
Show the faster version of the same failure, a child using the open drawers as steps, staged with a weighted object rather than a person.
Set the working rule as a filmed rhythm, one drawer closed before the next is opened, heaviest clothes lowest, strap fitted.

Frame the second hazard as poison, choke or strangle: mothballs and cedar blocks rolling loose in a sock drawer look like sweets at the eye level of a toddler standing at an open bottom drawer, and fix it with a mesh bag hung at the back or by leaving them out entirely.
shots: Low three-quarter of two loaded drawers open together with the anti-tip strap pulling taut in frame.
Close on a hand closing one drawer before opening the next, repeated as a rhythm.
Toddler-height close looking into an open bottom drawer with loose cedar blocks rolling in it.
Close on cedar going into a mesh bag and the bag being hung at the back of the drawer.
on_screen_text: Cedar in a bag, hung at the back

short.hook: Two loaded dresser drawers opened at once and an anti-tip strap snapping taut behind the chest, showing exactly what the strap is holding back.
short.standalone_note: Say the drawers are fully loaded and the strap is already anchored into a stud, so the tension is understood as the fix working rather than a stunt.

segments.covers: One category per drawer, a hand's width of free space as the fill line, and the same-day rule when it fails.
beats: Open each drawer in turn showing exactly one category in each, underwear and socks, sleepwear, t-shirts, workout clothes.
Demonstrate the fill line with a flat hand laid into the free space, which makes the standard checkable in a second without measuring anything.
Show the failure signal, a drawer that needs pressing to close, and apply the rule that one item comes out the same day rather than at the weekend.
Tie the drawer order to Chapter 13 and a home chosen by how it is used, with underwear and socks in the drawer you open every single morning and the jeans and knitwear down at the bottom.
shots: Overhead sequence opening each drawer in turn, one category visible per drawer.
Overhead close of a flat hand laid into the free space at the front of a drawer.
Close on a drawer being pressed shut and springing back open.
Close on a single item being removed and the drawer sliding shut cleanly.
on_screen_text: A hand's width of free space
Pressing to close means one comes out

short.hook: A flat hand laid into a dresser drawer as the fill line, turning a vague standard into something you can check in one second.
short.standalone_note: Name the standard and what happens the moment it fails, or the hand gesture reads as absolutely nothing.

segments.covers: Folding the clean laundry into the drawers before the empty basket goes down.
beats: Show the basket arriving in the bedroom and being worked immediately rather than parked on the floor.
Fold upright and load into the drawers in the same pass, with the empty basket only set down at the end.
Contrast with the alternative the manual names, the stack living on the dresser top until the weekend, and show what that top looks like a few days in.
shots: Three-quarter of the basket arriving and being set on the bed rather than the floor.
Overhead of the fold and load running continuously into an open drawer.
Close on the empty basket being set down last.
Matched overhead of a dresser top carrying an unfolded stack, for contrast.

short.hook: A laundry basket that does not get put down until it is empty and every item is standing upright in a drawer.
short.standalone_note: State the trigger as the basket arriving in the bedroom, since the whole rule is about sequence and needs its starting point named.

close.standard_beat: Open each drawer in turn on the finished state: one category each, everything folded to stand upright so the whole drawer reads from above, a hand's width of free space, and every drawer sliding shut without anything being pressed down. Show the trigger as the laundry basket coming up to the bedroom and being emptied into the drawers before it gets put down.
close.next_zone_teaser: Next, the biggest job in this room, and the one expensive thing hanging in it that does not fit your life.

shot_list: Overhead arm over the bed for every tip-out and fold sequence.
Overhead arm over the open drawer for the filed rows and the fill line.
Low three-quarter of the chest for the two-drawers-open strap tension shot.
Toddler-height close into the open bottom drawer.
Three-quarter of a drawer removed fully from the carcass.
Macro on runners, screws and the driver.
Close on the waistband and unmatched-sock sorting tests.
Close on the dated box being taped and leaving through the bedroom door.
Locked frames of the laundry basket at the bed and at the open drawer.
Matched overhead pair of a stacked drawer and a filed drawer.
videos.description_hook: One category per drawer, folded to stand upright, and a hand's width of free space as the fill line. Plus the dated box for the size you are not right now, packed and carried out of the room on camera.

videos.title: Primary Closet: One Hanger Style and Two Fingers of Space
videos.cold_open_problem: Open on a single garment sliding out on its hanger, the one that cost real money and does not fit your life: the suit for the job you left, the coat that is beautiful and far too warm, the shoes that turn on you after twenty minutes. Name why it is still hanging there, that letting it go makes the money real, and answer it the way the manual does, that the money left the day you bought it and the garment brings back none of it while taking a hanger you need. Set the deadline the video actually carries out on camera: photograph it, list it, thirty days.

segments.covers: Pulling the unworn and the unrepaired off the rod, listing the expensive mistake, and moving the wrong season out.
beats: Work the rod end to end pulling anything not worn in a year, with the decision happening at the hanger rather than in a pile on the floor, and flag honestly that the try-on pile runs longer than anyone plans for.
Pull everything waiting on a repair you are never going to make, and be direct that an intention is not the same thing as a plan.
Carry out the cold open decision: the expensive mistake photographed against a plain wall, listed for sale, and the thirty day deadline written on the tag so it does not quietly go back on the rod.
Strip out every wire hanger and dry cleaner's plastic sheath, which also sets up the suffocation hazard handled in Safety.
Move winter coats and heavy knits into a labelled bin or the guest wardrobe so the rod carries only what this month asks for.
shots: Three-quarter down the length of the loaded rod before anything moves.
Close on hands sliding one hanger out at a time and the row opening up behind it.
Close on the expensive garment photographed against a plain wall and a thirty day date written onto its tag.
Close on a growing bundle of wire hangers and plastic sheaths.
Three-quarter of a labelled bin being filled with winter coats and lidded.
on_screen_text: The repair you will not make

short.hook: Every wire hanger and dry cleaner's plastic sheath pulled out of a closet in one bundle, and how much rod that alone gives back.
short.standalone_note: Establish that this is a clothes closet and that the bundle is packaging rather than garments, since a heap of wire and plastic is visually confusing on its own.

segments.covers: One hanger style, grouped by type then shade, and opening the floor under the short items.
beats: Swap to one hanger style across the whole rod so everything hangs at the same depth and the row reads flat.
Group by type and then by shade, and turn every hook the same way so the row is scannable in one look.
Hang the short items together, show the floor space that opens up beneath them, and slide the shoe rack into it.
Stand the bags upright on the shelf rather than nesting them, since nesting is exactly how you forget the inner three.

rooms.room_note: Shoot all five zones on one daylight day, ideally under overcast sky, because this room usually has a single window and hard sun through a blind puts stripes across every overhead frame. Overhead shots are made with the tripod centre column reversed or a horizontal arm clamped over the bed, set once at the start of the day and left in place, since four of the five zones empty their contents onto the bed and that frame becomes the series signature. Keep the second tripod at three quarter height in the doorway corner for matching wide before and after plates, and tape its feet so every zone's wide lines up. The room is narrow, so plan to move the tripod between setups rather than walk backward past loaded bins. No presenter, no face, nothing above the wrists in any frame, so every beat has to be readable as hands, overhead or detail. On set safety: the anti-tip strap fixing, the closet top shelf and the folding luggage rack all put real weight over hands, so load test the rack and the top shelf bins before rolling, keep the extension lead off the walking line even in the shots where the lead is the subject, and never stage a cord loop near the bed for the camera. Voiceover is recorded separately, off set, so the room stays silent and the window can stay open for the airing shots.

The hard decision this video settles is stated up front, that guest linen is not the linen you stopped wanting, and a shelf holding six tired sets is a backlog rather than a decision.

Each fitted sheet tried on the actual mattress, with the pass and fail explained: a corner that pops off while the bed is being made makes it a rag, not a spare.
Each pillow folded in half and released, and the verdict shown rather than argued, since a pillow that stays folded has stopped doing its job.
The rule that settles the whole zone landed plainly, that anything you would not sleep on yourself for a week is cleaning cloth and not guest linen.
Two keepers separated from the rest, with the honest consequence named, that stopping at two may mean buying a set.

videos.title: Guest Dresser: Emptying Two Drawers and Keeping Them Empty
videos.cold_open_problem: Hands pull open a guest dresser drawer packed with off season jumpers, a bin of cables, wrapping paper and ribbon, and a bag of outgrown baby clothes. The reasoning that put them there gets named honestly, that the room stands empty most of the year so the space felt free, followed by what it actually costs, which is the entire point of the room. The decision this video settles is set out at the start: these two drawers belong to the guest and are never available, not for a week, not for the box you are about to sort properly.

The easy ones routed in frame, jumpers to your own wardrobe, cables to the drawer that already holds cables.
The hard one sat with rather than skipped, the baby clothes, and the point made that the decision happens today rather than after another year of storage.
The rule that governs the zone landed: when something needs a home and this dresser is the only candidate, that is a signal you have not decided about the thing, not a reason to take the drawer.

videos.title: Guest Room Desk: Sharing a Room With Its Second Job
videos.cold_open_problem: A desk in a guest room buried under gift wrap, an ironing pile, a printer nobody has switched on this year, and somebody's paperwork. The truth the video is built on gets said early, that almost every guest room is also something else, the home office, the sewing room, the place the exercise bike ended up, and that this is exactly why hosting takes an afternoon: you are not tidying, you are relocating a whole activity under time pressure. The test the video runs is set up in the same breath, whether that second job clears into one bin or one cupboard, in a single trip, without unplugging anything.

Each pile routed in frame, ironing back to the wardrobe it came from, paperwork into the file it was always headed for.
The printer decision made live, it either earns a desk somewhere it gets used or it leaves the house.
The second job test run: the room's other activity named out loud, then its whole footprint gathered to see whether it clears into one bin or one cupboard in a single trip with nothing unplugged.
The verdict taken honestly, share the room and set the boundary in tape, or accept that the second job is too big for this room and something moves out for good.

videos.description_hook: Hosting takes an afternoon because you are not tidying the guest room, you are relocating a whole second activity out of it under time pressure. Here is the test that decides whether the room can honestly share.

rooms.room_note: Shoot this room in daylight with the curtains fully open and the ceiling light off, because a child's room has low surfaces and an overhead bulb throws hand shadows straight down onto everything you are filming. Window light only, one operator, no lighting kit. Access is the real constraint: floor work, under bed work and closet floor work all need a low tripod, so plan on a tabletop tripod plus a taller one and expect to work kneeling. Set the overhead shots on a horizontal arm clamped to a heavy stand beside the bed, never over the bed frame, so nothing hangs above where a child sleeps. There is no slider and no second operator, so every floor level move is a locked off before and a locked off after rather than a tracking shot. Keep the child out of frame at all times: every keep or go call is filmed as adult hands with the child's choices already made off camera, and every child height shot means the camera is at that height, not the child. On set safety while filming: the anti tip strap, the blind cord cleat and the socket work are real fixes, so make them properly on camera and leave them made rather than staging and undoing them. Bag small parts and button batteries into a labelled tub the moment they leave a bin, and never leave a loose blind cord looped for a shot.

videos.title: 6S the Kids Bed and Sleep Zone: Thin the Stuffed Animals, Cleat the Blind Cord, Make It in One Pull
videos.cold_open_problem: Open overhead on the bed lost under stuffed animals, hands lifting them off one at a time until the pillow finally shows. Frame the decision this room has been dodging: the two or three that genuinely get slept with are already known, and the avoided part is not thinning the rest, it is whether you are allowed to do it without the child standing there. Set up that this video answers that with a dated lidded box and a six week wait, and that nothing leaves the house the same day it leaves the bed.

beats: Hands pull every stuffed animal out of the bed and lay them in one row across the carpet, so the actual count is visible for the first time.
Set out the split that makes this workable: the child picks the sleepers off camera, you handle the drift, and nothing leaves the house the day it leaves the bed.

Show the lidded box going onto the wardrobe shelf with a date written on the end, and give the six week rule complete: no request and the box goes quietly, one asked for by name and that one comes back while the rest still go.
Return three or four to the bed and set an open basket at the foot for the ones that stay visible rather than boxed.

videos.title: 6S the Toy Storage Zone: Six Open Bins, No Lids, and a Six Week Rotation Box Test
videos.cold_open_problem: Open overhead on the set every kids room has, the forty small figures or the enormous block set, emptied across the carpet with nothing built and the room empty. Name why it is still here: it was expensive, or the person who gave it asks after it. Set up that this video swaps that feeling for a test, half the set into a dated rotation box on the top shelf for six weeks, and shows exactly what to watch for on the afternoon it comes back down.

segments.covers: Every bin comes out onto the carpet and gets sorted into toy families before anything goes back, and the outs leave during the sort rather than into a pile to be decided later.
beats: Tip every bin onto the carpet, all of them, so the true volume is on the floor at once before a single keep or go call is made.
Sort into families first, blocks with blocks, figures with figures, vehicles with vehicles, and set out why families have to come before keep or go.
Broken toys, orphan puzzle pieces and party bag plastic go straight into the out bag during the sort, with the reason stated plainly: a decide later pile becomes a seventh bin.
Introduce the rotation box on the set that always gets abandoned: half of it goes up dated for six weeks, and what happens with it on the afternoon it comes back down is the answer.
