short.hook: The same toy put away twice from the same angle: once into a lidded bin, once into an open one, and only one of them takes two hands.
short.standalone_note: Establish in the first line that the person putting this toy away is five, since the whole case against lids is that one extra step is why it lands on the carpet instead of in the bin.

segments.covers: Washing the hard plastic and checking the bins themselves, because Shine here inspects the containers you are about to trust a child to carry.
beats: Run the hard plastic through a sink of warm soapy water in batches and lay it on a towel to dry.
Vacuum the skirting corners where small parts migrate, and show what actually comes out of them.
Turn every empty bin over and flex the base for splits before refilling, with the reason stated: a split bin gives way while it is being carried full.
Refill only once everything is dry, so nothing goes back damp into a closed corner of the room.
shots: Overhead of the sink with plastic toys in soapy water
Overhead of the drying towel laid out with sorted pieces on it
Macro of the vacuum nozzle in a skirting corner, small parts visible
Close on hands flexing an upturned bin base, the split running along it
on_screen_text: Check the bin, not just the toys

short.hook: An empty toy bin gets turned over and flexed, and a split runs the whole length of the base.
short.standalone_note: Frame it as cleaning in order to inspect rather than a cleaning tip, and give the consequence in the first line: this bin gives way while a child is carrying it full across the room.

segments.covers: The fourth S here is small parts and button batteries, sized against a toilet roll tube and checked hatch by hatch.
beats: Run the tube test hands only: anything that drops through a toilet roll tube is a choke risk for a younger sibling and belongs in a bin they cannot reach.
Move the small part families up to the high shelf and show the height gap against the low bins.
Work through the battery toys hatch by hatch, naming button batteries as the serious one.
Any toy whose battery cover has lost its screw goes out, and it leaves in the out bag on camera rather than back into a bin.
shots: Macro of small figures dropped through a toilet roll tube one after another
Three quarter showing the high shelf against the child height bins
Close on a screwdriver checking a battery hatch screw
Macro on a button battery in its open hatch, then the toy going into the out bag
on_screen_text: Fits the tube, goes up high

short.hook: Toy after toy gets dropped through a toilet roll tube, and the ones that pass straight through pile up underneath.
short.standalone_note: Name the risk as choking for a younger sibling in the opening line, and include the battery hatch rule before the end, because the tube test on its own misses the button battery, which is the serious one.

segments.covers: A photo of the contents taped to the front face of every bin, never the lid, at the height the child actually looks from.
beats: Photograph the contents of each bin from above, one shot per family.
Tape each photo to the front face of its bin and set out why the front face is the surface a child sees on the way past.
Drop the camera to child eye height and check every label reads from there.
Reference Chapter 14, visual controls, and land the point that a picture of six blocks works long before reading does.
shots: Overhead of blocks laid out being photographed for the label
Close on hands taping a photo to a bin front face
Camera at child eye height panning the labelled bin row
Macro on one photo label with the matching contents visible over the bin rim

short.hook: A row of toy bins seen from a child's eye height, every one carrying a photograph of exactly what lives inside it.
short.standalone_note: Say in the first line that the child using these bins cannot read yet, which is the entire reason the labels are photographs and sit on the front face rather than on a lid.

segments.covers: Pickup happens while the bedtime story is being chosen, not after it, because the story is the thing worth clearing the carpet for.
beats: Show the trigger in order: the book comes off the shelf, the floor gets cleared, then the story starts.
Set out why the story has to come after the pickup, and what happens to the habit the first time that order gets flipped.
Show the pickup finishing inside the time a child's attention actually lasts, which is why the bins are open and the labels are pictures.
Land the clear carpet as the light goes off, with the dated rotation box on the top shelf as the loop still open.
shots: Close on a bedtime book being pulled off the shelf
Overhead of the carpet clearing into the bins, hands only, one continuous take
Three quarter of the last toy dropped into its labelled bin
Overhead wide of clear carpet from the bed side as the light goes off

short.hook: The bedtime book comes off the shelf first and the carpet clears before it opens, in that order and not the other way round.
short.standalone_note: State the order rule explicitly at the top, pickup before the story rather than after it, because the ordering is the whole idea and without it this is an ordinary tidy up clip.

close.standard_beat: Show the standard holding: every toy family in one open, photo labelled bin at child height, none above the shoulder, and carpet clear enough to lie down on when the light goes off. Fire the trigger once, floor cleared while the bedtime story is being chosen, and end on the dated rotation box up on the top shelf with the test still running.
close.next_zone_teaser: Pan off the clear carpet to the desk in the corner, where the pile that never gets decided on is paper rather than plastic.

videos.description_hook: Six open bins, no lids, photo labels a child can read before they can read, and a six week rotation box that finally settles the set that gets tipped out and abandoned. Zone two of six in the Kids Bedroom.

videos.title: 6S the Study Desk: One Tray for Live Work, One Box per School Year, One Strip in One Socket
videos.cold_open_problem: Open on the stack of finished schoolwork being lifted from one end of the desk to the other, exercise books, paintings, a folder of worksheets. Name the block honestly: binning any of it feels like saying you did not care, so the pile gets moved instead of decided on. Set up that this video takes the judgement out of the moment and hands it to a box with a fixed size, so the call is not being made at nine on a Tuesday, and rebuilds the surface so homework gets started rather than avoided.

segments.covers: Paper first, every sheet to exactly one of three places, with a fixed size memory box making the hard call for you.
beats: Clear every sheet off the desk into one stack, then set out three destinations on the floor: the live work tray, the memory box, recycling.
Work the stack sheet by sheet and state the rule that hurts, that a worksheet from a finished term is recycling even when the marking was good.

Introduce the box that makes the call: one lidded box per child per school year, fixed size, on the wardrobe top, where full means full and room is made by taking something out rather than by getting a second box.
Photograph the oversized art flat on the floor and let the paper go, keeping the pieces where their hand is visibly getting better.
shots: Overhead of the whole desk stack lifted into one pile
Overhead three way layout of tray, memory box and recycling with hands feeding all three
Close on the memory box lid closing with the school year written on the end
Overhead of a large painting flat on the floor being photographed on a phone

short.hook: One stack of a child's finished schoolwork, three destinations laid out on the floor, and every sheet lands in one of them without a pause.
short.standalone_note: Re-establish in the first line that this is finished schoolwork and why it never gets decided on, then give the fixed size box rule complete, because the box is what makes sorting possible at all.

segments.covers: The surface stays a work surface, with pens inside one reach of the writing hand and books up on the shelf above.
beats: Stand pens and pencils in a cup within a hand's reach of the writing hand, and show the reach it replaces, the one that crosses the desk and takes the water bottle with it.
Move books and folders up onto the shelf, with the rule stated: anything stacked on the surface is the surface no longer being a work surface.
Set the final layout, lamp, pen cup, one tray of live work, and nothing else on the wood.
Show the chair pulled in and empty, because a chair holding a bag is a desk nobody sits down at.
shots: Overhead of the reach arc from the writing hand to the pen cup, marked on the desk
Close on hands lifting a book stack from the desk up onto the shelf
Overhead of the finished layout: lamp, pen cup, tray
Three quarter of the empty chair pulled in to the clear desk
on_screen_text: Books go up, surface stays clear

short.hook: Trace the reach from the writing hand to the pen cup, then run the version where the reach crosses the desk and catches a full water bottle.
short.standalone_note: Say up front that this is a child's homework desk and the point is getting started rather than looking tidy, so the reach argument reads as function and not as styling.

segments.covers: Down to bare wood, then into the drawer runners and the lamp shade, which are the two places dirt here is actually costing something.
beats: Clear the desk completely to bare wood and wipe the surface in one pass.
Open the drawer and get the pencil sharpener dust and dried glue out of the runners, showing what has been binding it.
Wipe the lamp shade with the lamp lit and show the direct payoff, that a dusty shade is a dimmer desk.
Return only the three things that live on this surface.
shots: Overhead of the bare desk mid wipe, cloth crossing the whole surface
Macro into the drawer runner with sharpener dust and dried glue visible
Close on the lamp shade being wiped, lamp lit, before and after
Overhead of the three items returning to the bare surface
on_screen_text: A dusty lamp is a dimmer lamp

short.hook: Macro into a desk drawer runner packed solid with pencil sharpener dust and dried glue, then the same drawer sliding shut with one finger.
short.standalone_note: Establish in the first line that this drawer had been sticking, since the runner clean only lands once the viewer knows which problem it just solved.

segments.covers: The fourth S here is what is chained together under the desk and what is standing point up in the pen cup.
beats: Get the camera under the desk and count the plugs, finding the strip plugged into another strip feeding a lamp, a charger and a console.
Bring it back to one strip in one wall socket on camera, name the risk as water and electricity, and move the water bottle off that end of the desk.
Turn the pen cup out and show scissors and a craft knife standing point up where a hand goes in blind, then reset them point down.
Blades go into a closed drawer if a younger child comes into this room, and close on the rule, find it and fix it now.
shots: Low under desk shot of the chained strips and the plug tangle
Close on hands unplugging the second strip and consolidating to one socket
Macro into the pen cup interior, the blade edge visible point up
Close on the craft knife going into a closed drawer

short.hook: The camera goes under a child's desk and finds a strip plugged into another strip, and the count of what hangs off it keeps climbing.
short.standalone_note: Name the hazard as water and electricity in the opening line and finish on the single consolidated strip, so the Short delivers the fix and not only the problem.

segments.covers: The tray is the standard: if it does not fit in the tray, it is not live work.
beats: Set the tray on the desk and state what it enforces, that anything which does not fit goes to the shelf, the memory box or the recycling.
Show the tray turned out on the same evening the backpack gets emptied, so the emptying has a rhythm and the tray never quietly becomes a second pile.
Name the failure this prevents, a tray that fills up and then stops meaning anything at all.
Reference Chapter 24, the checklist, schedule and name: the tray is the name, and the backpack evening is the schedule.
shots: Overhead of the tray with live work in it, the tray edges clearly the limit
Close on the tray tipped out beside the emptied backpack
Overhead of the sorted result feeding shelf, memory box and recycling
Three quarter of the tray back on the clear desk holding only live work
on_screen_text: If it does not fit, it is not live
Turn it out with the backpack

short.hook: Live work goes into a tray until the next sheet will not fit, and that sheet gets sent somewhere else on the spot instead of stacked on top.
short.standalone_note: Explain that the tray has a fixed size on purpose and pair it with the turn out evening, because a tray with no emptying rhythm is just a neater version of the pile.

segments.covers: The desk gets cleared when the laptop lid closes at the end of homework, not the next morning.
beats: Show the trigger: the laptop lid closes and the clear down starts in the same movement.
Clear back to the photographed state, lamp, pen cup, tray, and thread the charger through the clip on the desk edge so the plug never drops behind the desk again.
Set out why the next morning fails as a trigger and why the lid closing does not.
Land on the empty chair and the bare wood, a desk ready to be started at rather than cleared first.
shots: Close on the laptop lid closing
Overhead of the surface clearing in one continuous take
Macro on the charger threaded through the desk edge clip
Three quarter of the finished desk with the chair empty

short.hook: A laptop lid shuts at the end of homework and the desk clears in the same motion, one unbroken overhead take.
short.standalone_note: Name the trigger as the lid closing and contrast it with leaving the desk until morning, or this reads as a satisfying clean up clip with no rule behind it.

close.standard_beat: Show the finished surface holding the current task, the lamp, the pen cup and one tray, with the tray holding only work that is still live. Fire the trigger once, the desk clearing the moment the laptop lid closes, and end on the memory box on the wardrobe top with the school year written on the end.
close.next_zone_teaser: Open the closet door on the rod, where the pile nobody decides on is clothes, and a good part of it fits nobody in this house.

videos.description_hook: One tray decides what counts as live work, one fixed size box per school year decides what you keep, and the chained extension strips under the desk come back to one socket. Zone three of six in the Kids Bedroom.

videos.title: 6S the Kids Clothing Closet: Lower the Rod, Run the Size Test, Reverse Every Hanger
videos.cold_open_problem: Open on a rod packed so tight the hangers will not slide, and hands pulling out garment after garment that fits nobody in the house. Name why it is here: it is being kept for a younger sibling, a cousin, or a second child who is currently hypothetical. Set up the test this video applies, name the child and name the season they will fit it, and what it means when you cannot say both out loud.

segments.covers: Children's clothes fail in one direction only, too small, so the size test is fast and physical.
beats: Take everything off the rod onto the bed and run the three part size test garment by garment: sleeves above the wrist bone, waistbands that leave a mark, shoes where the toe is already touching.
Apply the keeping for someone test to the pile that fits nobody, name the child and name the season, and state what it means when you cannot say both: it is not being stored, it is being deferred.
Show one sealed labelled box per next size, with the rule that when the box is full the overflow goes now rather than after one more sort.
Name the cost of deferring, that clothes kept for nobody in particular arrive at the right size stained, dated and unworn anyway.
shots: Overhead of the emptied rod with everything laid across the bed
Macro on a sleeve ending above the wrist bone, then on a waistband mark
Close on shoes with the toe already touching the end
Close on a next size box being sealed and labelled in large numbers
on_screen_text: Fails one way only, too small
Name the child, name the season
Full box means it goes now

short.hook: Three fast physical tests on a child's clothes, sleeve above the wrist bone, waistband mark, toe touching the shoe end, and the reject pile builds in seconds.
short.standalone_note: Say in the first line that children's clothes only ever fail by getting too small, which is why the test can be this quick, then finish on the name the child and name the season rule so the Short carries the hard part too.

segments.covers: Lowering the rod is one bracket move, and it changes who is capable of using this closet at all.
beats: Measure the child's reach against the current rod and mark the new height on the closet wall.
Move the bracket, drop the rod, and take a hanger down from the new height with no stool anywhere in frame.
Group by type and then by colour inside each type, shirts together, dresses together, jackets together, with a hand's width gap between groups so a row can be read rather than dug through.
Set shoes in pairs on the floor rack and the backpack on its own low hook.
shots: Three quarter of the reach measured and marked against the old rod height
Close on hands moving the bracket and seating the lowered rod
Hands taking a hanger down from the new height, camera at child height, no stool in frame
Overhead along the rod showing grouped rows and the gaps between them

short.hook: A child's reach gets marked on a closet wall, one bracket moves, and the rod comes down to meet the mark.
short.standalone_note: Establish in the opening line that nobody under adult height could reach this rod before, since the entire result of the move is a child dressing themselves from it.

segments.covers: The closet floor and the top shelf, the two surfaces in this room nobody has looked at in a year.
beats: Empty the closet floor completely and vacuum it corner to corner, showing what was living under the shoe pile.
Wipe the rod where hangers have left a grey line along it, and show the cloth afterwards.
Check the top shelf for the dust that has been settling all year, and connect it directly to the clothes boxed up there.
Refill the floor with shoes in pairs on the rack only, so the floor stays a surface you can see.
shots: Low overhead of the empty closet floor mid vacuum
Macro on the grey hanger line along the rod, before and after the cloth
Close on a hand drawn across the top shelf, the dust line visible
Three quarter of shoes going back in pairs on the floor rack
on_screen_text: The grey line on the rod

short.hook: A closet floor gets emptied to bare carpet and the vacuum goes in on everything that had been living under the shoe pile.
short.standalone_note: Frame it as cleaning in order to inspect, and connect the top shelf dust to the next size clothes boxed up there, so it is not just a satisfying vacuum clip.

segments.covers: The fourth S here is the rod itself and the weight stored above a child's head.
beats: Hang everything back on and give the loaded rod one hard downward pull before trusting it, with the plastic end brackets carrying the load in frame.
Name the risk as fall, cut, or crush: an overloaded rod on plastic brackets comes down onto a child's head.
Move the heavy things, sports kit and boots and skates, down to the closet floor, because the top shelf is where a child pulls weight onto themselves reaching for something else.
Clear the closet floor, since a stool or a storage box used as a step on a cluttered floor is the second fall in this zone.
shots: Macro on a plastic rod end bracket under full load
Close on hands giving the loaded rod one hard downward pull
Three quarter of boots and sports kit coming off the top shelf down to the closet floor
Low shot of the clear closet floor with the storage box taken out of step duty
on_screen_text: Pull test before you trust it

short.hook: A closet rod loaded full, then one hard downward pull on it, with the plastic end bracket held in macro throughout.
short.standalone_note: Name the fall, cut, or crush risk in the opening line and include the heavy things live low rule, because the pull test alone leaves the boots on the top shelf exactly where they were.

segments.covers: One hanger style, box numbers readable from the doorway, and every hanger turned backwards at the start of the season.
beats: Swap the mixed hangers for one style throughout and show what a uniform rod does to how fast a row reads.
Label the next size box in numbers big enough to read from the doorway, then prove it by shooting from the doorway.
Turn every hanger backwards at the start of the season and set out the record it creates, that the ones still reversed at the end are the things not being worn.
Reference Chapter 22, prevent and prepare, because the reversed hangers do next season's sorting before you get there.
shots: Overhead of mixed hangers replaced one by one with a single style
Doorway wide with the box label legible at that distance
Close on hands reversing a row of hangers along the rod
Macro on one reversed hook against forward facing neighbours

short.hook: Every hanger on a child's rod gets turned backwards in one pass, and whatever is still facing backwards in three months is a garment nobody wore.
short.standalone_note: Give the full loop inside the Short, reversed at the season start and still reversed means unworn, because half the explanation makes the trick meaningless.

segments.covers: The hanger gets flipped forward as the garment comes off the drying rack, so the record keeps itself.
beats: Show the trigger: a shirt comes off the drying rack, onto its hanger, and back onto the rod facing forward.
Set out why this works, that nobody has to remember anything because the record rides on laundry that already happens.
Show the rod part way through a season with forward and reversed hooks mixed, and read what it is telling you about what gets worn.
Land the finished closet, only clothes that fit today, grouped by type, one hanger style, at a height reachable without a stool.
shots: Close on a shirt lifted off the drying rack
Macro on the hanger hook turning forward as it goes onto the rod
Overhead along the rod mid season with the hook directions mixed
Wide of the finished closet with the door open, camera at child height
on_screen_text: Flip it as it goes back

short.hook: A backwards hanger means nobody has worn that shirt yet, so watch the hook turn forward the moment the shirt comes off the drying rack.
short.standalone_note: State what a reversed hanger means before the flip happens, otherwise the movement is just a hanger being turned round and carries nothing.

close.standard_beat: Show the finished closet against the standard: only clothes that fit today on the rod, grouped by type, one hanger style, at a height reachable without a stool, with the next size box sealed and labelled on the top shelf. Fire the trigger once, a hanger flipped forward as the shirt comes off the drying rack.
close.next_zone_teaser: Turn from the closet to the dresser, where the problem is not what fits, it is eleven shirts in a drawer that only closes if you lean on it.

Drying rack setup for the flip trigger sequence
videos.description_hook: Lower the rod so a child can dress themselves, run the sleeve and waistband size test, and settle the clothes you are keeping for a sibling who may never exist. Zone four of six in the Kids Bedroom.

videos.title: 6S the Kids Dresser: File Fold Upright, Set the Number by Arithmetic, Strap It to the Wall
videos.cold_open_problem: Open on a drawer that only shuts when a hand presses down on it, then the same hand pulling the whole stack out to find one shirt. Name the real problem, that this is not a folding problem, it is eleven shirts in a drawer built for fewer. Set up that this video sets the number by arithmetic rather than garment by garment feeling, and ends on the mechanical test that settles it without an argument: if it does not close with one push, the sort is not finished.

segments.covers: One drawer at a time onto the bed, with the quantity set by counting days between washes rather than by judging each garment.
beats: Tip one drawer onto the bed and state the rule for the whole pass, that the next drawer stays shut until this one is back in.
Take out the single socks with no pair, the underwear with dead elastic, and the pyjama bottoms that now stop above the ankle.
Run the arithmetic on camera: days between washes, add two, and that is the number for socks, underwear and shirts.
Everything above the number goes, starting with whatever you would not choose on a normal morning, and the test stays mechanical enough to run without an argument.
shots: Overhead of one drawer tipped onto the bed with the empty drawer in frame
Macro on dead elastic being stretched, then a single unmatched sock held flat
Close on hands counting shirts into a row up to the calculated number
Overhead of the surplus pile beside the counted keep pile

short.hook: Count the days between washes, add two, and lay out exactly that many shirts while everything above the number goes into a pile beside them.
short.standalone_note: State in the first line that this is a child's drawer that will not close, and give the arithmetic complete, since the number is the whole point and useless as a half rule.

segments.covers: File folding upright turns this drawer into something a child reads from above instead of excavating.
beats: Demonstrate the fold hands only and slowly on a single shirt, then stand it upright in the drawer.
Fill a row upright so the drawer reads like a card index, cut against the flat stack it replaced.
Add dividers, or two shoebox lids, so the rows do not fall sideways the first time the drawer gets yanked.
Check the drawer closes with one push and no pressing down, which is the test that says the sort was finished.
shots: Overhead close on one shirt file folded, unbroken take
Overhead of the drawer half flat stacked and half upright for the cut
Macro of socks standing in a row with every pair visible from above
Close on the drawer closing with one push, the hand leaving the front

short.hook: Half a drawer stacked flat, half filed upright, shot from directly above so the difference needs no explaining at all.
short.standalone_note: Say who opens this drawer, a child getting themselves dressed alone, so the upright fold reads as findability rather than as an aesthetic choice.

segments.covers: Pull the drawers right out, because the grit in the frame is where the sticking drawer, and then the slammed drawer, comes from.
beats: Lift each drawer clear of the carcass and set it aside, leaving the empty frame open to the camera.
Vacuum the inside of the frame and wipe the runners, showing what comes off them.
Follow the chain from grit to sticking drawer to slammed drawer, and land it as a safety point rather than a cleaning one.
Refit the drawers and test the slide with one finger before anything goes back in.
shots: Three quarter of a drawer being lifted clear of the carcass
Low overhead into the empty frame, vacuum nozzle working the back corners
Macro along a runner before and after the wipe
Close on the refitted drawer sliding shut with one finger

short.hook: A dresser drawer comes all the way out of the carcass and the camera goes into the empty frame after what has been collecting in the back corners.
short.standalone_note: Connect the grit to the slammed drawer in the opening line, because the reason to pull drawers out is not tidiness, it is that a jammed drawer pulls a child off balance when it gives.

segments.covers: The fourth S here is the anti tip strap, because a chest with two drawers open is a climbing frame.
beats: Open two drawers and shoot the shape from low down, then name what it is to a small child, a ladder that tips forward onto whoever climbs it.
Find the wall stud, fit the anti tip bracket properly on camera, and show the strap taut rather than slack.
Take the tablet and the toy off the dresser top, because anything a child wants up there is an invitation to climb for it.
Cover the second hazard, the jammed drawer that needs a hard yank and pulls a child backwards when it gives, and tie it back to the runners you just cleaned.
shots: Three quarter of the dresser with two drawers open, camera low
Close on a stud finder against the wall, then the bracket going in
Macro on the strap pulled taut between dresser and wall
Overhead of the dresser top going bare, tablet and toy removed
on_screen_text: Two open drawers is a ladder
Nothing on top worth climbing for

short.hook: Two drawers open on an unanchored chest, filmed from the height of a small child, and the shape it makes is a ladder.
short.standalone_note: Name the fall, cut, or crush risk immediately and finish on the strap fitted to a stud and the top cleared, so the Short ends on a fix rather than on a warning.

segments.covers: A picture label on each drawer front so a child finds and returns without reading, and the same category stays in the same drawer forever.
beats: Photograph the contents of each drawer and fix a picture label to each front, socks on the socks drawer.
Show the labelled fronts from child eye height and set out that the label serves the return trip as much as the finding trip.
State the rule that costs something: same category in the same drawer forever, even when that leaves one drawer half empty.
Reference Chapter 21, the hazard hunt, because the taut strap fitted in the last pass is part of the finished state, not a one off job.
shots: Overhead of socks laid out being photographed for the label
Close on hands fixing a picture label to a drawer front
Wide of five labelled drawer fronts, camera at child eye height
Overhead of one deliberately half empty drawer with the category intact

short.hook: Five drawer fronts, five photographs of what is inside them, filmed from the eye height of whoever has to put the clothes back.
short.standalone_note: Explain in the first line that the label exists for putting clothes away rather than only for finding them, which is what makes the same category forever rule worth a half empty drawer.

segments.covers: Refolding happens straight out of the laundry basket into the drawer standing up, never stacked flat on the bed for later.
beats: Show the trigger: the basket lands beside the open drawer and each item is folded upright and goes straight in.
Show the alternative it replaces, the flat stack left on the bed to be dealt with, and name that stack as the exact point where the system fails.
Close each drawer with one push in sequence and confirm the quantities are still holding.
Land the finished dresser: one category per drawer, upright rows, strapped to the wall, bare on top.
shots: Three quarter of the laundry basket set down beside the open drawer
Overhead of one item folded and placed upright, continuous take

Three quarter wide of the finished dresser, top bare, strap visible behind

short.hook: Laundry goes basket to drawer with nothing landing on the bed in between, filmed as one unbroken overhead take.
short.standalone_note: Name the failure being avoided in the opening line, the flat stack on the bed for later, since the value of the trigger is only visible against the thing it replaces.

close.standard_beat: Show the standard holding: one category per drawer, file folded upright, quantities set by the wash rhythm, and every drawer closing with a single push and no leaning. Fire the trigger once, clothes folded upright straight out of the basket, and hold on the taut anti tip strap and the bare dresser top.
close.next_zone_teaser: Move to the square metre by the bedroom door, where tomorrow morning either gets assembled tonight or gets argued about at seven.

videos.description_hook: Set the shirt count by arithmetic instead of argument, file fold so a child can read the drawer from above, and strap the dresser to a wall stud before it gets climbed. Zone five of six in the Kids Bedroom.

videos.title: 6S the School Launch Zone: A Five Line List, One Hook Each, and Handing the Packing Over
videos.cold_open_problem: Open on adult hands packing a child's backpack at speed, zipping it, hanging it on the hook. Name the decision hiding inside that competence: you pack it because they are slow and you are not, and every rushed morning proves you right again. Set up that this is the one worth reversing, and that the video gives the five line list, the handover, and the rule that holds it, that you never silently repack the bag afterwards.

segments.covers: The backpack gets turned fully upside down every Friday, so nothing lives in it by accident for another week.
beats: Invert the backpack over a bin and empty every pocket, turning out the leftover lunch, the dead permission slip and the newsletter from three weeks ago.
Set out why complete emptying beats a look inside, that the things which survive are the things nobody ever sees.
Send the sports kit to the wash basket rather than back into the bag damp, and name damp kit as what actually makes the bag smell.
Fix the rhythm plainly, this is a Friday job, so the weekend never starts with last week's bag.
shots: Overhead of the backpack inverted over a bin, contents falling out
Close on each pocket held open and turned out in turn
Overhead of the contents laid on the floor, split into out and back in
Three quarter of damp sports kit dropping into the wash basket
on_screen_text: Damp kit never goes back in

short.hook: A school backpack gets held upside down over a bin and emptied pocket by pocket, and what falls out has been in there for weeks.
short.standalone_note: Establish in the first line that this is a full weekly empty rather than a tidy up, and say what survives when you only look inside, since that contrast is the entire reason for inverting it.

segments.covers: Hook, then shoes, then bag along the wall in the order they get grabbed, with the lunchbox on its own hook doing the telling.
beats: Set the hook at child height and hang the packed bag, then place the shoes side by side directly underneath it.
Stand the instrument case upright against the wall where it cannot be trodden on, and put the sports bag on the second hook.
Give the lunchbox its own small hook and set out what it reports, that an empty hook at bedtime means the box is still in the bag with yesterday's sandwich in it.
Show the floor completely clear, which is the state this whole zone exists to hold.
shots: Three quarter of the hook rail at child height with the packed bag hung
Overhead down onto shoes placed directly under the bag
Close on the instrument case standing upright against the wall
Macro on the empty lunchbox hook, then the lunchbox hanging on it
on_screen_text: An empty hook is a message

short.hook: One small empty hook by a bedroom door at bedtime means a lunchbox is still shut inside a school bag with yesterday's sandwich in it.
short.standalone_note: State the pairing at the top, that this hook belongs to the lunchbox and nothing else, because the hook only reads as a signal once you know what is meant to be hanging there.

segments.covers: Seals, lids and the base of the bag, which is where the growth and the old spill actually are.
beats: Wipe the lunchbox seal groove and take the water bottle lid apart, showing the inside of the lid where the mould actually grows.
Turn the backpack over a bin and shake it out, then wipe the base where the drink leaked back in March.
While the bag is empty, check the base seam and the zip pulls, since a failing zip is what strands the bag on a Monday.
Everything dries fully before it goes back on the hook.
shots: Macro on the water bottle lid taken apart with the inner seal visible
Close on the lunchbox seal groove being wiped out
Overhead of the backpack shaken out over a bin
Macro on the stained bag base and the zip pulls, before and after
on_screen_text: Check the seam and the zips

short.hook: A kid's water bottle gets washed every day and the lid almost never comes apart, so here is the macro lens on the inside of that seal.
short.standalone_note: Say in the first line that the bottle gets washed but the lid does not come apart, which is exactly why the seal is the thing worth showing.

segments.covers: The fourth S here is a clear doorway at seven in the morning, and one named pocket for the thing that must never be forgotten.
beats: Shoot the doorway low with the bag and the instrument case lying across it, and name the risk as a fall in the line everyone walks at seven in the morning.
Set the rule that fixes it, everything hangs and nothing rests on the floor, then repeat the identical low frame with the floor clear.
Cover the second hazard as poison, choke, or strangle: loose medication in a backpack pocket, reachable by a younger sibling and easy to forget entirely.
Give the inhaler, the epipen or the dose one named pocket that is checked at packing rather than remembered at the school gate.
shots: Locked off low doorway frame with bags and a case across the walking line
The identical locked off doorway frame with everything hung and the floor clear
Close on hands labelling one named pocket on the backpack
Macro on medication going into the named pocket and the zip closing over it
on_screen_text: Checked at packing, not at the gate

short.hook: Camera on the floor of a bedroom doorway at bag height, with a school bag and an instrument case lying exactly where feet go at seven in the morning.
short.standalone_note: Name the fall risk and the seven in the morning walking line at the top, and include the named medication pocket before the end, because the doorway fix alone leaves the more serious hazard standing.

segments.covers: Five lines taped beside the hook at the child's eye level, in pictures for a younger one and words for an older one.
beats: Write the list on camera, five lines and no more: bag, shoes, lunch, form, kit.
Tape it beside the hook at the child's eye level, checked with the camera down at that height.
Set out the constraint that matters, that a longer list gets skipped, so a missing item means you swap a line rather than add a sixth.
Reference Chapter 27, the friendly audit, and quote it: an audit checks the home, not the household. What it finds is always a system to fix, never a person to blame.
shots: Overhead of the five line list being written out
Close on the list taped to the wall beside the hook
Camera at child eye height showing the list sitting level with it
Macro across the five lines, each one legible in frame

short.hook: A packing list for a school bag stops dead at five lines, and the reason line six never gets added is the whole point.
short.standalone_note: State that the list belongs to the child and hangs beside the hook at their eye level, so the five line limit reads as a deliberate design constraint rather than laziness.

segments.covers: The bag gets packed while the bath is running, and the packing is genuinely handed over rather than supervised.
beats: Show the trigger: the bath taps go on, and the packing starts in the bedroom while the water runs.
Set out why this window works, that it happens before anyone is tired enough to argue, and it ends when the bath is full.
Show the handover as a rule rather than a performance: the packing is done off camera, and what is filmed is a finger running down the five line list instead of going into the bag.
Give the rule that makes the handover real, never silently repack it, and the honest cost, a few genuinely bad weeks bought back on every school morning after.

Wide of the finished launch zone, floor clear, bag hung and zipped
on_screen_text: Check the list, not the bag

short.hook: A finger runs down a five line packing list and stops there, without once going into the school bag underneath it.
short.standalone_note: Set up in the first line that the adult used to pack this bag and now only checks the list, and include the never silently repack rule, because that rule is the only thing that makes the handover real.

close.standard_beat: Show the standard in place: bag on the hook, shoes directly underneath, forms in the front pocket, and the five line list taped beside the hook at the child's eye level. Fire the trigger once, the bag packed and hung while the bath is running, and hold on the completely clear doorway floor.
close.next_zone_teaser: Pull back to the whole room with all six zones standing at once, then point at the next room in the series, where the same six passes meet a much smaller occupant.

videos.description_hook: Empty the backpack upside down every Friday, hang everything so the doorway is clear at seven in the morning, and hand the packing over to a five line list you check instead of the bag. Zone six of six in the Kids Bedroom.

rooms.room_note: Shoot the whole room in daylight with the blind up and no overhead bulb, because the nursery reads warm and soft on camera and hard top light flattens the pale surfaces the room is made of. No baby, no doll and no person above the wrists appears in any frame at any point, so every demonstration is built from hands, overhead angles and detail shots, and any beat that looks like it needs a body gets solved with an empty pad or an empty crib instead. Treat every crib frame as if it will be screenshotted on its own, which means the crib is never filmed holding bedding except in the deliberate before shots at the top of that video. The tripod lives in two places: a horizontal centre column over the crib and the changing pad for the locked overhead angles, and a three quarter stand at dresser height for drawer and shelf work. Crib slats eat light, so bounce a white card from the window side rather than adding a lamp, and shoot the two low light beats at dusk using the night light already in the room. Real hazards get demonstrated at rest and never in motion: cords are shown slack and then shortened, the anchor bracket goes on the wall before the chest goes back, and any kettle or sterilizer is filmed cold and unplugged. Wipe the changing pad between takes on camera, since that is the standard the room is teaching. Keep a spare fitted sheet and a second set of clean bottle parts on hand so resets between takes do not cost a wash cycle.

videos.title: Crib Reset: One Fitted Sheet and Nothing Else (6S Nursery)
videos.cold_open_problem: Open overhead on the loaded crib: the handmade quilt folded over the rail, the plush pile, the bumper, the wedge, the muslin stack. Name the hard call this zone forces, that the bedding was made for this crib by somebody who loves you, took them weeks, and still cannot go inside the rails. Hands lift each item out and set it on the floor until the mattress is bare. Frame the problem as a decision about a gift and about who you now have to tell, not as clutter.

segments.covers: Everything comes out of the crib in one armful, and exactly one thing goes back in.
beats: Hands lift the quilt, the plush, the bumper, the wedge and the muslin stack out and lay them on the floor as a single spread, small enough to prove this is one armful of work rather than a project.
Each item is walked to its actual destination on camera: plush to the toy basket, muslins to the changing station, quilt to the keepsake box.
Explain that the crib is the one zone in this room with a number instead of a judgement call, and that the number is one.
One fitted sheet goes back onto the bare mattress and nothing follows it over the rail.
shots: Overhead of the loaded crib before anything is touched
Overhead of the floor spread, every item separated and readable
Close on hands folding the quilt into the keepsake box and closing the lid
Overhead of the bare mattress with the single fitted sheet going on

short.hook: Overhead of a crib packed with quilt, bumper, wedge and plush, swept out by hands in one continuous move down to a bare mattress.
short.standalone_note: Open by naming the nursery crib and stating the one fitted sheet standard as a flat rule, since nobody watching has seen the rest of the video.

segments.covers: Spares live where your hand finds them in the dark, because the sheet change happens at 3 a.m.
beats: The top dresser drawer is emptied to its bare base, then two fitted sheets and one spare sleep sack go in and nothing else.
Explain the test being applied: one drawer, one motion, no ceiling light.
A hand opens the drawer in a dark room and comes out with a fitted sheet without looking down, shot at dusk on the room's own night light with no added fixture.
Explain what fails if the spares live in the airing cupboard down the hall, which is a walk you will not make with a wet mattress and a crying baby.
shots: Three-quarter of the top drawer emptied to its bare base
Close on hands folding two fitted sheets and a sleep sack into the drawer
Close on a hand opening the drawer and lifting a sheet out blind, lit by the room's night light

short.hook: A hand in a dark nursery opens one drawer and comes out holding a fitted sheet without looking down.
short.standalone_note: Say in the first line that this is the crib zone and that the drawer holds sleep spares only, or the shot reads as a generic drawer tip.

segments.covers: Cleaning the crib is the inspection that catches loose frame bolts.
beats: Sheet comes off to a hot wash, the mattress is lifted out and stood against the wall, leaving the frame empty and reachable on all sides.
Hands wipe the mattress cover and every rail, holding on the top rail where hands and gums end up.

A palm runs down each slat, then a spanner goes onto the frame bolts. Explain that crib hardware works loose over months of being leaned on, which is why the check belongs to cleaning day rather than to a worry in the middle of the night.
Mattress goes back and the fresh sheet is pulled tight to all four corners.
shots: Close on a cloth working along the top rail
Close on a palm sliding down a slat
Close on a spanner seating on a frame bolt and turning
Overhead of the sheet pulled tight, corner by corner
on_screen_text: Check the bolts while it is empty

short.hook: Close on a spanner seating on a crib frame bolt and taking up a quarter turn of slack that was already there.
short.standalone_note: Explain in the first line that the crib is empty because the sheet is in the wash, so the bolt check reads as routine rather than an emergency.

segments.covers: A cord reachable through the slats and a mattress left high are the two things in this zone that hurt a baby.
beats: Frame it as poison, choke, or strangle. The blind cord, the lamp flex and the monitor cable are shown in turn, then a hand comes through the slats to test which of the three can actually be reached, framed tight so nothing above the wrist enters.
The reachable cord is shortened and clipped high on the wall and the crib is slid clear. Explain that reachable from inside the rails means it comes down or gets shortened today.
Frame the second hazard as a fall. The mattress bracket is unhooked and dropped to its lowest setting.
Name the trigger for that drop as the day your baby can push up onto hands and knees, because pulling to stand is what they learn next.
shots: Close on a hand between the slats reaching toward a hanging cord
Close on the cord being shortened and clipped high, well back from the rails
Three-quarter of the mattress bracket being unhooked and reset low
Overhead of the monitor mounted on the wall with its cable clipped an arm's length back
on_screen_text: Find it, and fix it now

short.hook: A hand comes through the crib slats and closes on a blind cord that should never have been in reach.
short.standalone_note: Name Safety as the fourth S and state both hazards plainly, since a viewer arriving cold needs the rule and not just the demonstration.

segments.covers: A photograph of the correct crib means nobody has to ask you what goes in it.
beats: Shoot the overhead frame of the finished crib, bare mattress and one sheet, as the reference image itself.
The printed picture is taped inside the closet door. Explain that a visiting grandparent putting your baby down can now see the right state without asking you.
The quilt is hung on the wall above the crib in the same frame as the taped photo, which closes the cold open decision and gives you the thing you say to the giver.
shots: Overhead reference frame of the crib, held long and clean
Close on hands taping the printed photo inside the closet door

short.hook: An overhead photo of a bare crib mattress with one fitted sheet gets printed and taped inside a nursery closet door.
short.standalone_note: Say what the photo shows and who it is for, because the picture means nothing without its contents and its audience.

segments.covers: The wash is the trigger, so the crib rebuilds itself to standard every time.
beats: The sheet is stripped for the wash, then the crib is remade with a sheet and nothing else.
Explain that the crib is already empty at this exact moment, which is why the rebuild costs nothing extra and needs no reminder attached to it.
Close on the live crib matching the taped photo.
shots: Close on hands stripping the sheet in one motion
Overhead of the crib remade, sheet only
Match cut between the taped photo and the live crib
on_screen_text: Trigger: when the sheet comes off

short.hook: A crib sheet stripped for the wash, then the same crib remade with one sheet and nothing else.
short.standalone_note: State the trigger and the full standard in the first two lines, since this Short is the whole habit compressed.

close.standard_beat: Hold the finished crib beside the taped photo and give the standard as the room's rule: the crib holds a fitted sheet, a sleep sack, and your baby, and nothing else crosses the rail. Show the trigger once more as the sheet comes off for the wash, and point to Chapter 25, the ideal-state photo.
close.next_zone_teaser: Next, the changing station, where the whole design question is what one arm can reach with the other hand still on your baby.

videos.description_hook: The crib is the one surface in the house where your baby is left alone, which is why the standard is a fitted sheet and nothing more. This is the full 6S reset, including the hard conversation about the quilt somebody made you.

videos.title: Changing Station Setup: Everything Inside One Arm's Sweep
videos.cold_open_problem: Open on the half-built changing setup on the living room floor, a wipe pack and no diapers. Name the decision this zone forces: you built a second spot downstairs because carrying the baby up eight times a day is unbearable, and the half-stocked version is the one that fails you. A hand reaches for a diaper that is not there. Name the rule the video settles, that you run it as a full station or you do not run it at all.

segments.covers: Only what your hand touches during a real change earns a place on the dresser top.
beats: The entire dresser top is cleared onto a towel on the floor, and the count of what was living up there is left on screen long enough to register.
Explain the single test for getting back: does your hand touch this during an actual change.
Diapers, wipes, cream and a burp cloth go back one at a time, each named as it lands.
The lamp, the framed scan photo and the unopened lotion leave the surface entirely, and the shot follows each to where it now lives.

Overhead of the towel spread with every item laid out separately

segments.covers: The reach arc defines the station, and the dominant hand decides which side of it holds diapers.
beats: Hands pin a length of string at the pad and swing it across the dresser top to mark the limit of a planted reach, laying tape along the arc it draws. Shot overhead and framed tight to hands and string.
Explain the split the tape creates: inside the arc is the station, outside the arc is storage.
Diapers go on the side the dominant hand lands, wipes beside them, cream where a thumb can flip the cap without looking.
The lined pail is set within one step and two spare outfits go into the drawer directly beneath the pad.

short.standalone_note: Say in the first line that the other hand never leaves the baby, since that is the entire reason the arc exists.

segments.covers: The pad is the surface bare skin touches most in this house, so it gets wiped every change.
beats: The pad is wiped on camera, and the beat explains why this one alone does not wait for the weekly reset.
The pad cover comes off for a hot wash, noted as weekly rather than monthly.
The drawer under the pad is pulled right out and upended, showing the crusted cream lids and dried wipes that collect underneath the spare outfits where nothing ever disturbs them.

videos.title: Baby Clothes: One Size Per Drawer, and Outgrown Leaves Today
videos.cold_open_problem: Open on a newborn outfit with the tags still attached, held against a drawer of clothes three sizes bigger. Name the decision: it came from somebody who mattered, it was never once worn, and keeping it feels like keeping the gift while giving it away feels like a small betrayal. The outgoing bag hangs empty on the door hook behind it. Say plainly that this video settles that call with a rule rather than a mood.

segments.covers: Read the label, compare it to today's size, and accept that there are only two destinations.
beats: A drawer is emptied onto the bed and every garment laid flat in a single layer, dropped into rough size order as it goes down so the spread of sizes living in one drawer is visible at a glance.
A label is read between two fingers, and the beat explains why reading beats judging by eye on baby clothing, where the same garment shape runs across four sizes.
Each garment is checked against the size your baby is wearing today, and anything smaller leaves the drawer now.
The two destinations are shown physically, the outgoing bag on the hook and the keepsake box, and the beat explains that a third pile is exactly what stalls this zone.
The cold open rule is applied on camera: two garments per size, chosen by what your baby actually lived in, and the unworn gift goes out while it is still new enough to delight somebody.

short.standalone_note: State the two-per-size rule and both destinations inside the first ten seconds, because without them the shot is just a sad object.

segments.covers: One size per drawer, filed upright, so a half-asleep hand cannot pick wrong.

segments.covers: Empty to the base, and deal with set stains before they ever reach the drawer.

Hand-me-downs are turned to the window and inspected for stains that have set, and washed before they go in rather than after you have pulled one out at 6 a.m.

segments.covers: An unanchored chest is a ladder and a crush risk, and old trims come off in a mouth.
beats: Frame it as fall, cut, or crush. Two drawers are opened at once and the weight is shown carrying forward, turning the chest into a ladder for a climbing child.
The wall anchor is fitted on camera and the chest is fixed to it before it goes back against the wall.
The working rule is demonstrated as a repeated hand motion, each drawer closing before the next one opens.
Frame the second hazard as poison, choke, or strangle. Decorative buttons, ribbon ties and a hood drawstring on a hand-me-down cardigan are cut off before the garment ever enters a drawer.

videos.title: Feeding Station: A Clean Bottle in Your Hands at 2 a.m.
videos.cold_open_problem: Open on three bottle brands lined up on the surface with spare teats and mismatched collars scattered between them. Name the decision: the first bottle was refused, everybody swore the second one worked for them, and you now wash, sterilize, store and match parts for three systems in order to use one. A hand hunts through the pile for a collar that fits the teat it is holding. Point out that every one of those steps happens at 2 a.m.

segments.covers: Lay out every part at once, then bin the failed ones and remove the brands you have stopped using.

Every part belonging to a brand or pump you have stopped using is gathered and the whole system leaves, box and spares included.

Explain the three-feed test from the cold open: a new teat gets three honest feeds across a week, offered when your baby is calm and hungry rather than already crying, and then it either stays or the system leaves the house.

beats: Two bins in clearly different colors are set down, one for clean and ready, one for used and waiting.
Bottles come out of the sterilizer and are assembled fully, teat and collar seated, before they are allowed into the clean bin.
Explain the payoff: the middle of the night becomes a grab rather than a hunt for a matching collar in the dark.

The kettle or sterilizer is descaled, filmed cold and unplugged, and noted as monthly.

rooms.room_note: Smallest room in the series and the hardest to shoot headless, because a mirror faces almost every angle. Scout the tripod position first with the camera running and check the mirror, the shower glass, the chrome faucet, and the tap spout for reflections of the operator, then mask or reposition before a single take. Best light is a single window mid morning with the overhead off; if the room is windowless, bounce one soft source off the ceiling so the mirror does not throw a hotspot. Overhead work needs a low tripod with a side arm over the counter, the drawer, or the open cabinet, with the camera dressed in a lens cloth so a bare hand never enters frame while adjusting. Shoot the shower and tub with the lens protected against spray and the enclosure door held open by a wedge rather than a hand. Real chemistry on set means real rules: only ever open one cleaning product per take, never film bleach and bowl cleaner within reach of each other even as a prop, keep the extractor fan on for every cleaning setup, and unplug any heat tool at the wall between takes rather than leaving it live for the shot. Medicine cabinet takes should use the household's own boxes with any patient name and prescription label covered before rolling.

beats: Hands lay a towel on the floor or the closed toilet lid and clear the entire counter onto it in one sweep, basin to wall, nothing left standing.

Show the three piles this room always produces, travel bottles, sample sachets, and the hair tie graveyard, and explain that these route to a drawer or out of the room entirely rather than back to the stone.
Count the survivors on camera against the ceiling of four daily products plus soap and the toothbrush holder.

beats: Hands set the tray down on the reach side and load the daily set into it, explaining that the side is chosen by which hand actually reaches, not by which side looks balanced.
Demonstrate the lift test, one hand under the tray, raising it clear of the counter to show the whole daily set moves as a single unit for cleaning.
Route the heat tool cord behind the basin on the far side from the tap and set the tool on its heat-safe rest, explaining that the cord path is a placement decision, not a tidiness one.
shots: Overhead of the empty tray landing on the counter, then filling item by item
Three-quarter of one hand lifting the loaded tray clear of the stone
Close on the cord being drawn behind the basin, tap in the same frame for reference
Macro on the heat tool settling onto its metal rest

short.hook: Open on the one-hand lift test, the entire morning routine rising off the counter on a single tray.
short.standalone_note: State up front that the tray holds the daily set and that lifting it in one hand is the test the counter has to pass.

segments.covers: Clean in order, tray, counter beneath it, faucet base, then mirror and the light switch plate.
beats: Wipe the tray first with it lifted away, then the counter underneath, explaining why the order stops you cleaning around an object twice.
Work the base of the faucet where toothpaste dries into a crust, showing the cloth getting into the joint rather than passing over it.
Finish on the mirror and then the light switch plate, calling out the plate as the surface in this room nobody ever wipes and the one that shows it.
Explain cleaning to inspect here, that wiping the faucet base is also how you notice a drip or a loose escutcheon.
shots: Overhead of the tray lifted off, counter shown mid wipe with the clean line visible
Macro on the faucet base, dried toothpaste before and clean joint after
Three-quarter of the mirror being worked, camera angled off axis so no reflection of the rig
Macro on the light switch plate, cloth passing over it

short.hook: Macro on the crust at the base of the faucet, then the cloth going into the joint and the joint coming up clean.
short.standalone_note: Name the faucet base and the switch plate as the two surfaces that get skipped, so the Short teaches a rule rather than showing a wipe.

segments.covers: Water and electricity share one small surface here, so the cord stays clear of the basin and the plug comes out at the wall the moment the tool goes down.
beats: Show the hazard plainly, a plugged-in heat tool within cord reach of a full basin, then show the correction, unplugged at the wall with water standing in the bowl.
Explain the timing rule, that the plug comes out when you set the tool down, not once your hair is finished, because the gap between those two moments is the whole risk.
Cover the burn hazard, a hot iron cooling on a towel or a cosmetic bag, and give it the metal or ceramic rest it returns to in the same spot every time.
Move glass bottles from the counter edge to the back row against the mirror, or show decanting into something that does not shatter on tile.
shots: Close on the cord lying between tap and basin, then the same frame with it rerouted
Macro on a hand pulling the plug at the wall socket
Three-quarter of the hot tool being set on its rest instead of on fabric
Overhead of glass bottles moving from the front edge to the back row
on_screen_text: Unplug when you set it down
Glass goes to the back row

short.hook: Hold on a live cord draped across a full basin, then a hand pulling the plug at the wall, with no other action in the frame.
short.standalone_note: Say that this is a bathroom counter where a heat tool and a basin share one surface, and give the set-it-down-unplug-it rule in full.

segments.covers: The four-product limit gets written down and the cleared counter gets photographed, so a fifth bottle has something to argue with.
beats: Hands write the four-product limit on a strip of tape and stick it to the underside of the tray, explaining that a written limit is the best way you know today, written down.
Take the ideal-state photo of the cleared counter, print or tape it inside the vanity door, and show it in place with the door open.
Demonstrate the standard working, a fifth bottle arriving at the counter and being held against the taped limit before it lands.
shots: Macro on the pen writing the limit on tape
Close on the tape being pressed to the underside of the tray, tray then flipped upright
Three-quarter of the vanity door swinging open with the photo taped inside
Overhead of a new bottle hovering over the counter beside the photo

short.hook: Open on the photo of the finished counter taped inside the vanity door, then the real counter matching it exactly.
short.standalone_note: Explain that the photo is the standard for this counter and where it is taped, since the door interior alone reads as ambiguous.

segments.covers: The trigger is the nightly toothbrush rinse, and the tray goes back to match the photo before the light goes off.
beats: Show the trigger as it already happens, the toothbrush going under the tap at night, then hands resetting the tray in the same standing position.
Explain why the trigger is attached to something the house already does rather than to a reminder, and that the photo is what tells you when the reset is finished.
Show the counter at the end of the reset next to the photo, matching, with the light going off.
shots: Close on a toothbrush under running water
Overhead of two or three items returning to the tray, seconds of work
Three-quarter of counter and taped photo in the same frame
Wide low angle of the dark room with the counter bare

short.hook: Toothbrush under the tap, then a ten second counter reset that happens without anyone deciding to do it.
short.standalone_note: Name the toothbrush rinse as the trigger and the taped photo as the finish line, both of which the parent video established.

close.standard_beat: Hold the finished counter beside the taped photo while stating the standard in full, that the counter carries one liftable tray and nothing beside it and anything used less than daily lives behind a door, then show the trigger once more as the toothbrush is rinsed and the tray goes back.
close.next_zone_teaser: The bottles that left the counter went into a drawer, and the drawer is where the dates are hiding, so the vanity drawers are next.

shot_list: Overhead counter setup on a side arm, before state, after state, and every tray sequence
Three-quarter tripod at basin height for sweeps, cord routing, and the tray lift
Macro on the faucet base, the light switch plate, and the tape being written
Close on the wall socket for the plug pull
