short.standalone_note: Re-establish that these are the two laundry machines and that their lids are the surface in question, then state the one rule plainly, that nothing coming off one machine is allowed to land on the other.

segments.covers: The two items that genuinely belong at the machines move to the shelf above, and both lids stay free to open.
beats: A washer lid swinging fully open against a bare surface, cut against the same lid blocked, so the cost of a cluttered top is watched rather than described.
The vent brush and the pack of machine cleaner tablets placed on the shelf above the machines, the two things used at this spot and nowhere else in the room.
The failure this prevents demonstrated once: a loose cap set on a lid, knocked, and rolling down the gap behind the drum where nothing is ever retrieved.
Height established as the actual fix rather than tidiness, since a shelf above the machines cannot be knocked into that gap.
shots: Three-quarter of the washer lid swinging fully open against a bare surface
Close on hands setting the vent brush and tablet pack onto the shelf above
Tripod close, macro framing on a cap rolling off a lid into the gap behind the machine
Overhead of the finished shelf, two items, clearly spaced
on_screen_text: Store it above, not on top

short.hook: A cap is set on a washer lid, nudged with one finger, and rolls straight down the gap behind the drum where it is gone for good.
short.standalone_note: Establish that these are the washer and dryer, then name what does belong within reach of them, the vent brush and the cleaner tablets, and where those two go, the shelf above rather than the lid.

segments.covers: Cleaning to inspect the two places that hold water and grime on a washer, the door gasket and the detergent drawer.
beats: Gloved fingers peeling back the folds of the washer door gasket to reveal what has been living in there, coins, hairpins and grey slime.
The gasket wiped out fold by fold and then wiped dry, with the between loads habit that prevents it, the door left propped ajar so the rubber is never sitting wet.
The detergent drawer pulled right out, carried to the sink and washed, including the residue that comes off the roof of the empty housing it left behind.
A cleaner tablet dropped into the empty drum and a hot cycle started, with the pass framed as inspection, since what matters is what the gasket and the drawer were hiding.
shots: Tripod close, macro framing on gloved fingers lifting a gasket fold, contents revealed
Close on the wipe passing through the fold, dirty and clean sides in one frame
Overhead at the sink of the detergent drawer being scrubbed and rinsed
Three-quarter of the empty drum, tablet dropped in, door closed, cycle started

short.hook: A gloved finger peels back the rubber seal around a washer door and the camera holds on the coins, hairpins and grey slime packed into the fold.
short.standalone_note: Say which part of the machine this is, the rubber gasket around the washer door, and close on the habit that keeps it empty, wiped dry with the door left ajar between loads.

segments.covers: This is the 4th S. Lint plus heat is a fire, and the duct behind the dryer is where the fuel collects.
beats: The burn or fire question opened on the lint screen, pulled and cleared, including the lint that collects on the heating element side of the screen housing.
With the dryer already unplugged and pulled out on camera, the duct disconnected and the soft grey packing eased out of the bend where it builds.
The two duct materials laid side by side in one frame, a crushed foil accordion length against a smooth rigid metal length, with the swap made now rather than promised for next time.

The water and electricity question and the fall, cut or crush question covered in the same pass behind the machine: a rubber fill hose gone hard or bulged at the collar sitting a hand's width from a wall outlet, and an unlevel foot that lets the machine walk on a spin, plus the sharp sheet metal edge underneath when it is tilted back.
shots: Close on the lint screen being pulled and the mat of lint peeled off it
Three-quarter of the disconnected duct end, gloved hands easing out packed grey lint

Tripod close, macro framing on a bulged fill hose collar with a wall outlet behind it
Close on a gloved hand turning a levelling foot, machine steady on the floor
on_screen_text: Lint plus heat is a fire

short.hook: A wad of packed grey lint is pulled out of a length of crushed foil duct, and a smooth rigid metal duct lands beside it on the floor for comparison.
short.standalone_note: State that this is the duct behind a clothes dryer and that the machine is unplugged at the wall before anything is disconnected, then give the whole point in one beat, lint plus heat is a fire and the foil kind traps far more of it.

segments.covers: Turning the duct check into a glance, with the month written on tape stuck to the side of the dryer.
beats: A strip of masking tape torn off, the month written on it, and the tape pressed to the side of the dryer where it reads from the doorway.
Why the month lives on the machine rather than in a diary: the answer has to be available while standing in front of the dryer with the duct question in mind.
The frozen standardize line carried as the card over this segment, "A standard is the best way you know today, written down."
The finished zone read from the doorway so the room reports itself, bare lids, washer door ajar, tape legible from where you stand.
shots: Tripod close, macro framing on a marker writing the month onto masking tape
Close on the tape being pressed onto the dryer side panel
Wide three-quarter from the doorway, tape still readable in frame
on_screen_text: Write the month on the machine

short.hook: A fistful of grey lint from a dryer duct drops into a bin, then a marker writes that month onto masking tape and presses it to the side of the machine.
short.standalone_note: Say what the month refers to, the last time this dryer duct was pulled and cleared, and why it goes on the machine itself rather than into a diary or a phone.

segments.covers: One motion tied to the buzzer, and that motion is the whole machine standard.
beats: The buzzer triggered on camera, with hands going straight to the lint screen before the dryer door has swung shut, so the habit hangs on a sound that already happens.
The full leave behind state reached in one unbroken pass before leaving the room: both drums empty, washer door propped ajar, lint screen cleared and back in its slot.
Why this trigger holds, that you are already standing at the machine when the buzzer sounds, so nothing has to come and find you.
The once a year duct clear separated out as the one part of this zone no everyday sound can carry, which is why it lives on the tape instead.
shots: Close on the dryer door opening and the screen being pulled in one motion
Three-quarter of the washer door propped ajar
Wide from the doorway of the finished zone, both machines clear

short.hook: A dryer buzzer sounds and hands go to the lint screen before the door has even swung shut.
short.standalone_note: Establish that the lint screen is cleared every single load rather than weekly, and show the three part finished state it belongs to, drums empty, washer door ajar, screen clear.

close.standard_beat: Return to the matched doorway frame and read the finished standard off the room itself, both drums empty, washer door ajar, lint screen cleared, before you leave the room, with the trigger shown as the buzzer sounding while hands are still at the machine. The masking tape stays in shot as proof that the once a year duct check now has a home.
close.next_zone_teaser: The machines are ready to take a load, so the shelf beside them is next, and the five half used stain removers standing on it.

Tripod angled down over both machine tops for the Sort clear down
Tripod close, macro framing on the washer door gasket folds, gloved hands

Overhead floor lay of foil duct against rigid duct
Close on fill hose collar with wall outlet behind it
Close on levelling foot and the sheet metal edge underneath
Close on marker, masking tape and the dryer side panel
Close on the lint screen pull, shot twice for Safety and for the buzzer beat
videos.description_hook: If you cannot name the month you last pulled the dryer out and cleared the duct, the machine is not slow, it is blocked. Full washer and dryer reset from the 6S Micro Zone Manual, hands only, no presenter.

videos.title: Laundry Detergent Shelf Reset: One Product Per Job, Dose Line Marked
videos.cold_open_problem: Open on the shelf every laundry room grows: a box of dye grabbing sheets, two spray bottles, a stain stick dried solid in its cap, and something a relative swore by. A hand reaches past all of them for the one bottle that actually gets used. Frame the real problem behind the crowding, that binning a mostly full bottle feels wasteful, so the bottles sit there being wasteful slowly while holding the one arm's reach of shelf next to the open washer lid.

segments.covers: Every container comes down to the floor, and three named disqualifiers decide what earns a place back on the shelf.
beats: Every bottle, stick, spray and pod tub lined up on the floor in a single row, so the true count is visible in one frame instead of estimated on a shelf.
The three disqualifiers applied on camera, one container at a time: crusted shut at the neck, label washed off so the dose cannot be read, bought for one stain that already came out.
Two open jugs of the same detergent resolved into one jug in use and one refill, rather than two half jugs each holding shelf space.

The hardest version of the call landed in frame: the one treatment whose work has actually been watched held beside a tub of oxygen powder, with every remaining spray and stick routed to the disposal pile in the same pass.
shots: Overhead of the full floor row of containers, wide enough to count them
Tripod close, macro framing on a crusted bottle neck and a washed off label
Close on hands decanting one jug into another
Overhead of the keep pile against the leave pile, visibly unequal
on_screen_text: Keep what you have watched work

short.hook: Every bottle, spray, stick and tub from one laundry shelf goes onto the floor in a single row, and the row runs longer than the shelf it came off.
short.standalone_note: Establish that this is the detergent and stain treatment shelf in a laundry room, name the three disqualifiers as containers are picked up, and state the keep rule, one treatment you have watched lift a stain plus a tub of oxygen powder.

segments.covers: Placement set by the open washer lid, with everyday detergent in the reaching spot and pods above the basket test.
beats: The washer lid opened and the arm's reach arc from it traced on camera, then the everyday detergent and its dosing cap set inside that arc.
Bleach and the stain sprays moved onto a tray behind the detergent, second row, still visible but out of the one spot a hand goes to mid load.
The pod tub placed higher than a child reaches on tiptoe from an upturned laundry basket, with the basket in frame as the measuring stick.
The arc tested a second time with a wet hand holding a garment, so placement is settled by how the shelf is used with the drum open rather than by how the bottles look lined up.
shots: Three-quarter from the open washer lid showing the reach arc to the shelf
Close on the detergent and dosing cap landing in the front position

short.hook: A laundry basket is turned upside down under a shelf and used as the measuring stick for how high the detergent pod tub has to go.
short.standalone_note: Explain that a toddler will climb on whatever is in the room, so pod height gets measured from an upturned basket, and that the tub needs a latched lid or a high shelf without exception.

segments.covers: Detergent always drips, so the fix is a wipeable tray under everything rather than more wiping.
beats: The tacky ring under a detergent jug and the dried trail down its spigot shown first, so the problem is visible before anything is cleaned.
The spigot and the shelf beneath it wiped, framed as the last time this shelf gets cleaned this way.
Every container stood on a shallow tray, so the next drip lands on plastic that rinses rather than a shelf that stays tacky for a year.
The tray lifted and rinsed once at the sink, which is now the entire maintenance job for this shelf.
shots: Tripod close, macro framing on the sticky ring left under a jug
Close on a cloth wiping the spigot and the shelf beneath
Overhead of containers being lowered onto the shallow tray
Close of the tray under a running tap

short.hook: A detergent jug is lifted off a shelf and the camera holds on the tacky brown ring it has been sitting in.
short.standalone_note: Say that detergent drips no matter how carefully it is poured and that wiping is not the fix, then show the shallow tray going under every container and being rinsed in one lift.

segments.covers: This is the 4th S. Two chemical hazards specific to this shelf, plus the blind high reach that drops a full jug.
beats: The poison, choke or strangle question opened on a detergent pod, which looks exactly like a sweet to a toddler and bursts in the mouth, so the tub gets a latched lid or a high shelf without exception.

The separation rule enforced on camera with both containers capped throughout: bleach and any ammonia based cleaner moved onto different shelves, never sharing a shelf and never sharing a bucket, because a spill in a small room with the door shut can mix the two into a gas.
The fall, cut or crush question shown as the combination that causes it, a full jug stored above head height, a smooth handle, a wet hand, and a reach made with no line of sight into the shelf.
The same full jug relocated down to the low shelf in frame, so the correction is watched rather than recommended.
shots: Tripod close, macro framing on a detergent pod held in an open palm at sweet scale
Close on bleach and an ammonia based cleaner being separated onto different shelves, both capped throughout
Three-quarter of a blind reach into a high shelf holding a full jug
Close on the same jug being set down on the low shelf

short.hook: A single laundry detergent pod sits in an open palm with nothing else in frame, held long enough for the viewer to see what a toddler sees.
short.standalone_note: Establish that this is a laundry detergent pod and that it bursts in the mouth rather than being swallowed whole, then give the one rule, a latched lid or a high shelf, no exception.

segments.covers: Inking the true dose on the cap and giving every bottle a labeled footprint on the tray.
beats: The moulded cap filled to the dose the household actually uses, with the gap between that level and the top of the cap held in frame.
The true dose line drawn onto the cap in permanent marker, then used on the very next pour so the mark proves itself immediately.
The job written on the tray edge under each bottle, wash, whites, stains, so a returned bottle lands back in its own footprint without a decision.
The frozen standardize line held on screen over the marked cap and the labeled tray, "A standard is the best way you know today, written down."

segments.covers: The empty jug in your hand is the trigger, and it does two jobs before that load starts.
beats: The last dose poured out, then the empty jug going straight to recycling instead of back onto the shelf as a decision for later.
The replacement added to the shopping list before the start button is pressed, both actions happening at the machine inside the same minute.
Why the empty jug works as the trigger, that it is already in your hand and you are already standing at the shelf, so no reminder has to reach you.
The shelf closed out with one clean gap where the jug stood and no orphan empty anywhere on the tray.

close.standard_beat: Show the finished shelf and read the standard off it, one product per job, standing on a tray, with the real dose line marked on the cap. State the trigger as the moment a jug runs empty while it is still in your hand, and hold on the marked cap and the labeled tray edge as the two visual controls doing the work.
close.next_zone_teaser: The chemistry is settled, so the bags that feed the machine come next, starting with the delicates bag that has been a third full for three weeks.

videos.title: Laundry Sorting System: Hampers That Make a Full Load
videos.cold_open_problem: Open on five hampers, one of them a third full, with a hand lifting out the single garment someone has been waiting three weeks to wear, then setting it back where it was. Put the count on screen against the test that decides it, whether any of these bags has run as a full load, by itself, in the last month. Frame the problem as clothes taken out of circulation by a sorting scheme the household never actually honoured.

segments.covers: Every hamper is emptied to see what a real week produces, and the streams that never fill get merged.
beats: All five hampers tipped out into separate floor piles, whites, darks, towels, delicates and work clothes, so the real weekly volume is visible instead of assumed.
The test applied to each pile in turn on camera: a stream earns its own bag only if it has run as a full load, by itself, in the last month.
The failing streams merged into cold and gentle, with a mesh bag loaded and dropped into the drum so the merge is a real method rather than a compromise.
The spare hampers that served those streams carried out of the room, since an empty bag standing in the corner invites the stream straight back.
shots: Overhead of five hampers tipped out into five distinct floor piles
Close on a hand lifting the pile too thin to have made a load in a month
Close on delicates going into a mesh bag and the mesh bag into the drum
Three-quarter of spare hampers being carried out through the door
on_screen_text: What does a real week make
Full load in the last month

short.hook: Five laundry hampers are tipped into five floor piles and one of the piles is visibly too thin to ever fill a machine.
short.standalone_note: State the test in the opening beat, that a sorting stream earns its own bag only if it has run as a full load by itself in the last month, and show the mesh bag in the drum as where the merged items go.

segments.covers: Bags stand where clothes come off, and pocket contents get a dish so they stop reaching the drum.
beats: One bag per surviving stream placed where clothes are actually taken off, cut against where those bags had drifted, which is wherever they happened to fit.
The walking line between the door and the washer shown as bare floor, with every bag standing clear of it.
A small dish added on the shelf for pocket contents, with coins, hair ties and a memory stick landing in it rather than in the drum.
Bag size treated as a placement decision, since a bag that empties before it passes half full is a bag the household keeps using.
shots: Overhead of the floor with the walking line clear and bags set to the sides
Three-quarter of a bag moved from beside the machine to where clothes come off
Tripod close, macro framing on coins, hair ties and a memory stick dropping into the shelf dish
Wide of bare floor in front of the washer door

short.hook: A hamper is dragged out of the path between the door and the washer, and the bare floor it leaves behind is held in frame.
short.standalone_note: Say that laundry bags belong where clothes are taken off rather than where they happen to fit, and show the pocket dish going onto the shelf as the second half of the fix.

segments.covers: Hampers smell because of damp kit rather than dirt, so this pass is emptiness plus air.
beats: Damp gym kit lifted from the bottom of a lined bag with the lid down, named as the cause of the smell rather than dirt.
The stained inside seams of that liner shown, which is what a bag that has been holding wet towels actually looks like when you inspect it.
Each bin wiped out while it is empty, which is the only point in the week it can be done properly.
The alternative shown in the same pass, damp kit laid out or hung until it can go straight into a load, and the bag left standing with its lid open.
shots: Close on a damp towel being lifted out of a lined bag
Tripod close, macro framing on the stained inside seam of a liner
Overhead into an empty bin, cloth passing around the inside wall
Three-quarter of bags standing with lids open
on_screen_text: Wipe it while it is empty

short.hook: A wet towel is pulled from the bottom of a lined hamper and the camera drops straight to the stained seam underneath it.
short.standalone_note: Name the cause in the opening beat, that damp gym kit and not dirt is what makes a hamper smell, and close on the rule, no wet towel spends the night in a lined bag with the lid down.

segments.covers: This is the 4th S. A hamper in the walking line is a fall taken blind, and a work clothes bag can hide a blade.
beats: The fall question staged at floor level: a hamper standing in the walking line between the door and the machines, then the same frame with the leading edge of a carried load blocking the floor where it stands.
A hamper set down on a stair tread and left there while the rest of the load is fetched, held in frame as the version of this hazard that puts people in hospital, then removed.
The load height rule shown as a sightline: hands raise a loaded basket until the top of the pile crosses the lens and the floor disappears, then lower it until the tread edge comes back into view.

The fall, cut or crush question taken to the work clothes bag, where a utility knife, a razor blade or a pocketful of screws came home in a trouser pocket, with the bag tipped out onto a surface instead of reached into.
shots: Low tripod along the floor from door to machines, hamper in the line, then removed
Close on a hamper balanced on a stair tread, staged and struck immediately
Low three-quarter of a loaded basket raised until the floor leaves frame, then lowered
Tripod close, macro framing on a utility knife blade in the bottom of a work clothes bag
Overhead of the same bag tipped out onto a surface
on_screen_text: Tip it out, do not reach in

short.hook: A bag of work clothes is tipped out onto a counter and a utility knife slides out of it among the trousers.
short.standalone_note: Establish that this is the work clothes hamper and that blades and screws come home in trouser pockets, then give the rule, tip it out onto a surface, never reach in blind.

segments.covers: Each bag is labeled by the load it makes rather than the colour it holds, so anyone can start a machine.
beats: A bag labeled darks shown against the machine dial, with no way to tell from that label which setting it wants.
The label replaced with the load it makes, hot towels, cold darks, gentle, and the effect shown immediately as hands set the dial straight off the new label.
Labels fixed where they get read, at standing height on the front of each bag rather than on a lid that flips back out of sight.
The three finished labels shown legible in one frame, so any hand in the house can pick a bag and run it without asking.
shots: Tripod close, macro framing on a colour label being peeled off and a setting label going on
Overhead of three bags, all labels legible in one frame
Close on a hand reading a bag label then turning the machine dial to match
on_screen_text: Label the load, not the colour

short.hook: A label reading darks is peeled off a hamper and replaced with one reading cold darks, and the next shot is a hand turning the machine dial straight off it.
short.standalone_note: Explain that a colour tells nobody which setting the bag wants, and that labeling by the load it makes lets anyone in the house start a machine without asking.

segments.covers: Pockets get checked at the bag as the item goes in, not later at the machine.
beats: The trigger shown exactly as it happens at the end of the day, hands turning a trouser pocket out over the shelf dish before the trousers drop into the bag.
The failure it prevents shown in the same sequence, a lip balm going through a full load, with the dish named as where that stops.
A bag lifted out and emptied before it passes half full, so the standard reads as a rhythm rather than a deadline.
The finished state reached at the end of an ordinary day rather than during a special reset, which is the whole point of tying it to undressing.
shots: Three-quarter of hands turning a pocket out over the shelf dish, then the garment dropping into the bag
Tripod close, macro framing on a lip balm in a palm, then in the dish
Close on a bag at half full being lifted out
Wide of the zone at end of day, bare floor, three bags clear of the walking line

short.hook: A hand turns a trouser pocket inside out over a small dish and a lip balm drops into it before the trousers go in the hamper.
short.standalone_note: Say that pockets get checked as the item goes into the bag rather than later at the machine, and name what the dish is preventing, one forgotten item ruining a whole load.

close.standard_beat: Show three labeled bags standing clear of the walking line, each below half full, the shelf dish holding nothing older than today, and bare floor in front of the washer door. Read the standard off that picture, every bag is a load, labeled by wash setting, and emptied before it passes half full, with the trigger being the moment you undress at the end of the day.
close.next_zone_teaser: The loads go in cleanly now, so the surface where this whole room actually jams comes next, the folding counter.

shot_list: Zone wide three-quarter, as found and as finished, matched framing
Overhead of five hampers tipped into five floor piles
Low floor level along the walking line, door to machines
Close on the mesh bag being loaded and dropped into the drum
Tripod close, macro framing on the shelf dish, pocket contents, and a blade in the bag
Overhead into empty bins for the wipe out
Close on the stair tread hamper, staged and struck immediately
Close on labels being swapped and the dial being set from a label
Three-quarter of the end of day pocket check
videos.description_hook: A delicates bag that has waited three weeks is not sorting, it is clothes you have taken out of circulation. Here is how to build hampers that make a full load, hands only, no presenter.

videos.title: Laundry Folding Counter Reset: Bare, or Holding One Load
videos.cold_open_problem: Open on a folding counter carrying a growing bag of unmatched socks, kept because a partner does occasionally surface, which is exactly why the bag never gets thrown out. A dry load arrives with nowhere to land and goes back in for a second tumble. Frame the problem as a permanent tenant on the one surface in this room that has to stay clear, since the counter is where the whole room jams.

segments.covers: Everything parked on this counter that was never laundry comes off, down to bare surface.
beats: The counter cleared in one continuous pass, each object named as it comes off, the post, the toolbox, the parcel waiting to be returned, the vase from Christmas.
The connection made explicit, that whatever is parked here is why the dry load went back in for a second tumble.
The single sock call handled on camera: loose singles go into one shoebox and nothing larger, and everything already beyond that box goes today.
The end condition set for the box, that when it is full or at the change of season, whichever arrives first, everything still unmatched becomes a cleaning rag or leaves the house.
shots: Overhead of the counter as found, then a continuous clear down to bare surface
Close on each non laundry object being lifted off
Overhead of loose singles going into one shoebox, lid on
Wide of the bare counter held for a beat

short.hook: A bulging bag of unmatched socks is emptied into a single shoebox, the lid goes on, and everything that would not fit is carried out of the room.
short.standalone_note: Establish that this is the laundry folding counter and that the sock bag has been living on it, then give the rule with its end condition, one shoebox only, and at the change of season the rest becomes rags or leaves the house.

segments.covers: One basket per bedroom under the counter, and hangers on a rail rather than in a heap.
beats: One empty basket per person or per bedroom slid under the counter, so folding and delivering become a single motion instead of two separate jobs.
The failure it replaces shown alongside, folded stacks sitting on the counter waiting for someone to work out whose they are.
A tangled heap of hangers unpicked and six of them hung spaced on a rail at the end of the counter, then one lifted off single handed.
Why the heap matters here specifically, that anything needing to be unpicked first will not get used in the middle of folding a load.
shots: Overhead of empty baskets sliding into place under the counter
Three-quarter of a folded stack going straight from counter into a named basket
Close on a tangled hanger heap, then hands unpicking it
Tripod close, macro framing on six spaced hangers, one lifted off with one hand
on_screen_text: Fold and deliver in one motion

short.hook: A knot of tangled hangers is unpicked and six go onto a rail, evenly spaced, and one is lifted off with a single hand.
short.standalone_note: Say that this is the end of a laundry folding counter, and give the reason hangers get a rail, that anything you have to unpick first will not get used mid fold.

segments.covers: Wiping the counter before folding rather than after, because clean clothes pick up what the last load shed.
beats: Raking light run across the counter to reveal the detergent dust and lint the last load left, which looked like nothing a second earlier.
The counter wiped before folding starts, with the reason that afterwards is too late since the clean clothes have already collected it.
A folding board run across the gritty surface and then across the wiped one, so the difference is watched rather than claimed.
The first garment of the load folded on the clean surface to close the pass.
shots: Tripod close, raking light across the counter surface showing dust and lint
Close on the wipe passing across and leaving a clean band
Close on a folding board skating badly, then smoothly
Overhead of the first garment folded on the clean counter

short.hook: Raking light sweeps across a folding counter and reveals a layer of detergent dust and lint that was invisible a second earlier.
short.standalone_note: State that this is the surface clean laundry gets folded on, and give the rule in the opening beat, wipe it before you fold rather than after.

segments.covers: This is the 4th S. The iron that lives on this counter, and what is stacked on it and above it.
beats: The burn or fire question opened on the exact failure, an iron left face down or resting on its cord with clean clothing stacked within reach of the soleplate.
The fix built in frame: one heatproof rest for the iron, and the cord routed behind the counter where no arm can hook through it.
The plug pulled at the wall when the counter is left, stated as the practice instead of trusting the switch or the auto shutoff.

The fall, cut or crush question taken to what sits above and on the counter, a tall stack of baskets broken down, and the heavy backstock in the wall cupboard directly over the folding spot brought down to a low shelf.
shots: Close on an iron face down beside a folded stack, then lifted onto a heatproof rest
Three-quarter of the cord being routed behind the counter
Tripod close, macro framing on the plug being pulled at the wall socket
Overhead of a tall basket stack rocking, then broken down
Three-quarter of heavy items coming down out of the wall cupboard above the folding spot
on_screen_text: One rest, cord behind, unplug at the wall

short.hook: An iron sits face down on a folding counter beside a stack of clean clothes, and a hand lifts it onto a heatproof rest and pulls the plug at the wall.
short.standalone_note: Establish that irons live on laundry folding counters, and give both halves of the rule, one heatproof rest with the cord routed behind, and unplug at the wall rather than trusting the switch or auto shutoff.

segments.covers: Two allowed states only, with a photograph taped inside the cupboard door that settles what clear means.
beats: Both allowed states shown back to back in the same frame, the counter completely empty, then the counter holding exactly one load in progress, with nothing else permitted between them.
The empty counter photographed on a phone and the print taped inside the cupboard door directly above it.
Why a photo beats a written instruction on this surface, that the standard here is a look, and a look is easier to match than a description.
A hand opening the cupboard with the photo and the counter both in frame, and the counter brought back to match without anyone being asked.
shots: Overhead of the bare counter, then the same frame holding one load in progress
Close on a phone photographing the empty counter
Tripod close, macro framing on the print being taped inside the cupboard door
Three-quarter of the cupboard opening, photo and counter both in frame
on_screen_text: Tape the photo inside the door

short.hook: A phone photographs an empty folding counter and the printed picture gets taped inside the cupboard door directly above it.
short.standalone_note: Give the two allowed states in the opening beat, empty or holding one load in progress, and explain that the photo exists so nobody in the house has to guess what clear means.

segments.covers: The dry basket gets tipped out onto the counter, because a full basket set on the floor keeps its clothes another day.
beats: A dry basket tipped out onto the counter in one motion, with that motion named as the trigger for the whole zone.
The alternative staged as a matched pair back to back, the same full basket set down on the floor and still full in the identical frame.
The mechanism explained honestly, that a heap on the counter has to be dealt with before the surface can be used again, so the counter itself does the reminding.
Every basket under the counter shown empty before bed, which is the second half of the standard.
shots: Three-quarter of a dry basket being tipped out onto the counter
Overhead of the same basket set down full on the floor, matched framing
Close on the heap being folded down and carried away in the named baskets
Overhead of empty baskets stacked back under the counter
on_screen_text: Tip it out, do not set it down

short.hook: A full basket of dry laundry is tipped out into a heap on the counter instead of being set down on the floor.
short.standalone_note: Say why the heap is the point, that laundry heaped on the counter has to be dealt with before the surface can be used again, while a full basket on the floor quietly keeps its clothes another day.

close.standard_beat: Show a counter bare enough to roll pastry on, one empty basket per bedroom stacked underneath, six spare hangers on the rail at the end, and no clean clothing anywhere in the room. Read the standard off that picture, the counter is bare or holding one load, and every basket under it is empty before bed, with the trigger being the moment a dry basket gets tipped out onto the counter. Hold on the taped photo inside the cupboard door as the thing keeping the definition honest.
close.next_zone_teaser: Not everything can go in the drum, so the rack is next, and the wool jumper that has been draped over its end rung since spring.

shot_list: Counter wide overhead, as found and as finished, matched framing
Continuous overhead of the clear down
Tripod close, raking light across the counter surface
Close on the shoebox of single socks, lid going on
Under counter three-quarter for basket placement
Close on the hanger rail, six spaced hangers, one lifted single handed
Close on the iron, heatproof rest, cord routing and wall plug
Overhead of the wall cupboard above the folding spot being unloaded
Close on the phone photographing the empty counter and the print taped inside the door
Three-quarter of a dry basket tipped out onto the counter
videos.description_hook: Clean laundry with nowhere to land is why a dry load goes back in for a second tumble. This is the folding counter reset, hands only, no presenter.

videos.title: Indoor Drying Rack Reset: In Use, or Folded Flat
videos.cold_open_problem: Open on a rack half loaded with a wool jumper draped over the end rung since spring, and a hand lifting one hand wash only garment that takes two days to give up its water while everything else waits its turn. Frame the problem as a running cost rather than a neutral care label, and name the resident garment as the thing holding the rack hostage.

segments.covers: The rack is stripped completely, then three destinations decide what comes off it.
beats: The rack stripped right down to bare bars, so its true footprint is visible instead of sorting around garments already hanging.
What came off sorted into three destinations on the floor: still damp goes back on, dry goes to its drawer right now, and the long term resident gets decided.

The call applied to that resident garment, working back through the last three times it was washed and naming the occasion it was worn for each, with the garment leaving when all three cannot be named.
The decision framed as a running cost rather than a sentimental one, since the garment has been charging rack space and drying days the whole time.
shots: Wide three-quarter of the rack fully stripped, bare bars
Overhead of three destination piles on the floor, damp, drawer, decide
Close on the wool jumper being lifted off the end rung it has held since spring
Three-quarter of the dry pile going straight into a drawer rather than into a basket
on_screen_text: Damp back on. Dry goes now.

short.hook: A wool jumper is lifted off the end rung of a drying rack it has occupied since spring, and the clean line it left in the dust stays in frame.
short.standalone_note: Establish that this is an indoor drying rack, then give the test in full, name the occasion you wore it for each of the last three washes, and say what happens to the garment when you cannot.

segments.covers: One spot with a drip tray under it, and rungs assigned by where the air actually moves.
beats: The rack given one spot with a drip tray slid underneath, cut against wherever the last load happened to abandon it.
Bras, wool and swimwear loaded onto the top rungs, where air actually moves around a rack standing in a small room.
The bottom rungs kept for flat items that can take the slower dry, so the assignment is made by airflow rather than by what fits.
The loaded rack shown from the side so the airflow logic reads in a single frame.
shots: Wide of the rack set into its one spot, drip tray sliding underneath
Close on top rungs receiving bras, wool and swimwear
Overhead of flat items laid across the bottom rungs
Side three-quarter of the fully loaded rack

short.hook: A drip tray slides under a drying rack and the rack is set into one marked spot rather than wherever the last load left it.
short.standalone_note: Establish that this is an indoor drying rack, then give both rung rules quickly, bras, wool and swimwear on the top rungs where air moves, flat items on the bottom rungs for the slower dry.

segments.covers: A rack stored damp grows a musty smell and hands it straight to the next load.
beats: The bars wiped dry as the rack is stripped, so drying the rack is part of unloading it rather than a separate job nobody does.
The drip tray wiped out and shown empty, since standing water in the tray is the same problem as wet bars.
The rack folded flat so both faces get air, cut against the failure it prevents, wet metal pressed against wet metal.
The consequence stated plainly, that a musty rack passes the smell to the next load hung on it.
shots: Close on a cloth running the length of a bar as garments come off
Overhead of the drip tray being wiped out and shown dry
Three-quarter of the rack folding flat, faces separating for air
Tripod close, macro framing on two bars pressed wet against each other, then apart
on_screen_text: Dry the bars as you strip it

short.hook: A cloth runs the length of a drying rack bar as the last garment comes off, and the wet trail it leaves is held in frame.
short.standalone_note: Say that a drying rack stored damp grows a musty smell and passes it to the next load hung on it, then show both fixes, wipe the bars dry as you strip it and fold it flat so both faces get air.

segments.covers: This is the 4th S. Water reaching an outlet or a lead, and the wet patch a rack leaves on a hard floor.
beats: The water and electricity question opened on the exact arrangement to avoid, a rack standing over a wall outlet or across an extension lead running along the skirting, with garments dripping beneath.
The rack repositioned clear of both in frame, with the drip tray kept in place as the second layer of the fix.

The fall question shown at floor level, a dry cloth pressed onto the patch under the rack by hand and lifted soaked, which is what a hard laundry floor looks like to someone crossing it in socks carrying a basket they cannot see past.
The drip tray shown catching what would otherwise be that patch, so the placement fix and the safety fix turn out to be the same object.
shots: Low three-quarter of a rack standing over a skirting outlet, then relocated
Tripod close, macro framing on an extension lead beneath a dripping garment, then cleared
Low close on a dry cloth pressed into the wet patch and lifted soaked
Overhead of the drip tray holding water with the floor dry around it
on_screen_text: Never over an outlet or a lead
The tray is the floor's fix

short.hook: A garment on a drying rack drips onto an extension lead running along the skirting, and a hand slides the whole rack clear.
short.standalone_note: Establish that this is an indoor drying rack and name both hazards in the first two beats, water reaching an outlet or a lead, and the wet patch on a hard floor crossed in socks by someone carrying a basket.

segments.covers: Two allowed states, with nothing holding permanent residence on the rungs.
beats: Both allowed states shown in matched frames, in use holding one set of damp items, or folded flat against the wall.
What the rule excludes shown directly, anything with permanent residence on the rungs, with the last example lifted off.
The overnight test added, that no garment starts a second night up there without a reason that can be said out loud, applied to one garment on camera.
The folded flat state against the wall held as the default the room returns to between loads.
shots: Two matched frames, rack loaded in its spot and rack folded flat against the wall
Close on the last permanent resident being lifted off the rungs
Three-quarter of a hand testing a garment for dryness at the end of a day
Wide of the folded rack flat against the wall, floor clear beneath

short.hook: A hand pinches a garment that has already spent one night on the drying rack, finds it dry, and takes it straight off before it can start a second.
short.standalone_note: Give the two allowed states as the opening idea, in use holding one set of damp items or folded flat against the wall, and add the overnight test for anything staying up.

segments.covers: The rack gets cleared before the next load starts, so it is always ready for the load you are about to run.
beats: The trigger shown exactly as it happens, a hand on the washer door about to start the next load, stopping and turning to the rack first.
Anything dry taken off and delivered, then the decision made on the spot whether the rack folds flat or stays up holding what is still damp.
The effect named, that the rack is always ready for the load about to go in, so the next air dry item never waits for space.
The washer started with the rack in one of its two legal states visible behind it.
shots: Three-quarter of a hand on the washer door, then turning to the rack
Close on dry items coming off and going to a drawer
Wide of the rack either folded flat or holding only damp items
Close on the washer start button being pressed, rack visible behind
on_screen_text: Clear the rack, then start the load
Always ready for the next one

short.hook: A hand reaches for the washer door to start a load, stops, and turns to strip the drying rack first.
short.standalone_note: Establish the order plainly, that the indoor drying rack gets cleared before the next wash load starts, and say why, so the rack is always ready for the load about to go in.

close.standard_beat: Show the rack folded flat against the wall with dry bars, its drip tray wiped out and empty, the rail holding six spare hangers, and nothing hanging that was washed before today. Read the standard off that picture, the rack is in use or folded flat, never left standing half loaded, with the trigger being the moment you open the washer to start the next load.
close.next_zone_teaser: Everything in this room has a home now except the tools that clean it, so the last zone gets the handles off the floor and onto the wall.

shot_list: Rack wide three-quarter, as found and as finished, matched framing
Overhead of the three destination piles during the strip down
Close on bars being wiped as garments come off
Side three-quarter of the loaded rack showing the rung assignment
Low floor level for the outlet and extension lead hazard, staged and corrected in the same setup
Overhead of the drip tray, holding water then wiped dry
Two matched frames for the in use and folded flat states
Three-quarter of the washer door and the rack together for the trigger
videos.description_hook: One hand wash only garment can hold a drying rack hostage for two days while everything else waits its turn. Here is the air dry zone reset, hands only, no presenter.

videos.title: Broom, Mop and Bucket Storage: Nothing Leans, Nothing Stores Wet
videos.cold_open_problem: Open on a corner where worn towels, holed T-shirts and a retired set of sheets have quietly become a rag supply large enough to clean a small hotel, with a broom leaning behind the door in the same frame. Name why the pile grew, that turning a worn item into a rag feels like thrift rather than a decision, so nothing is ever discarded, only reclassified. Set the job for the video, handles onto the wall and rags down to one bin.

segments.covers: Every tool stands up in the open at once, and duplicates and orphans leave.
beats: The broom, the mop, the dustpan, the vacuum hose with its attachments and the sack of rags brought out onto open floor where the whole holding can be seen in one frame.
Duplicates resolved on camera, two brooms becoming one broom, with the second carried out rather than kept back as a spare.
The crevice tool that fits no vacuum still in the house test fitted to the hose, refused, and binned, since an attachment with no machine is not a spare part.

The rag rule applied: rags live in one bin and only one bin, nothing new becomes a rag until something old leaves as waste, and a bin that cannot be worked through in a year is cloth being stored rather than saved.
The second vacuum kept for the garage settled by the same test, since one that has not run in a year is a broken machine with an excuse rather than a spare.
shots: Wide overhead of every tool laid out on the open floor
Close on two brooms held side by side, one carried out through the door
Tripod close, macro framing on a crevice tool offered to a hose and not fitting
Overhead of rags packed into a single bin, lid on, surplus bagged for waste
Three-quarter of the second vacuum being wheeled out of the room
on_screen_text: One bin of rags, no more
A year unused is not a spare

short.hook: A mountain of worn towels and holed T-shirts gets pressed down into one bin, and everything that will not fit gets bagged for waste.
short.standalone_note: Explain why a household rag pile grows, that turning a worn item into a rag feels like thrift rather than a decision, then give the rule, one bin only, and nothing new becomes a rag until something old leaves as waste.

segments.covers: Handles onto a wall rail heads uppermost, and every vacuum attachment into one labeled caddy.
beats: A wall rail mounted and the broom, mop and dustpan hung from it with the heads uppermost and clear of the floor.
Why heads up matters shown rather than claimed, a bristle head rested on concrete splaying sideways, then re-soiling the floor it touches.
Every vacuum attachment gathered into one labeled caddy, so a missing one shows instead of being assumed present.
The floor beneath the rail shown completely clear, which is the whole point of the pass in this corner.
shots: Three-quarter of the rail being mounted and the first handle hung
Tripod close, macro framing on bristles splayed against concrete, then the same head hanging clear
Overhead of attachments going into one labeled caddy
Wide of the clear floor beneath the hanging tools

short.hook: A broom head is pressed down onto concrete and the bristles splay sideways, then the same broom hangs head uppermost on a wall rail.
short.standalone_note: Say plainly that bristles left resting on concrete splay and then re-soil the floor they touch, and show the wall rail as the fix, heads uppermost and clear of the floor.

segments.covers: Nothing goes back on the rail wet, and the vacuum canister is emptied before it is stored.
beats: The mop head rinsed until the grey water runs clear, then hung to dry well away from the rail.
The consequence stated directly, that a mop put away wet and grey spreads that water back down the next floor it touches.
The vacuum canister emptied before storage, with what was still sitting in it held in frame as the reason.
The mop head checked by touch at the end, dry to the touch, which is the condition the standard for this corner actually names.
shots: Close on a mop head being rinsed, grey water running off it
Three-quarter of the mop hanging to dry, clear of the rail

videos.description_hook: A broom leaning behind a door is a hazard waiting for someone to open it, and a rag pile is not thrift, it is storage. This is the utility corner reset, hands only, no presenter.

rooms.room_note: Shoot on a bright overcast day with the desk turned so window light rakes across the surface from the side, which is what makes dust, toner film, and forearm grime read on camera. Everything in this room is either paper or electronics, so kill the overheads and bounce daylight off a white card rather than adding a lamp that reflects off screens and scanner glass. No lighting rig, no second operator, no crane, no drone: one person, one tripod, one clamped overhead arm, a beanbag for the positions a tripod leg will not fit. Headless throughout, meaning nothing above the wrists is ever in frame, no faces, no piece to camera, and no second body walking into shot. Two tripod positions cover most of the room: the overhead arm clamped to the desk edge for surface and drawer work, and a three-quarter tripod at seated eye height on the writing-hand side for shelf, printer, and cabinet work. Access is the constraint, not light, because a filing cabinet drawer or a printer back panel leaves no room for a tripod leg, so plan the beanbag for those and shoot them locked off rather than handheld where you can. For the floor spreads, raise the tripod and shoot high angle from the step stool rather than trying to get a true overhead. On-set safety: power everything down before any cleaning shot, spray cleaner onto the cloth off camera and never toward a screen, anchor the bookshelf and the filing cabinet to the wall before you load them for the anchoring shots, lift the fireproof box with two hands at floor level, and use the step stool in frame for every high-shelf reach, never the rolling chair.

videos.title: Home Office Desk Reset: The Full 6S Pass on the Desk Surface
videos.cold_open_problem: Open on the one corner of the desk held by a half-finished project, papers fanned and untouched for weeks, while the rest of the surface gets swept clear around it in a few seconds of the same shot. Establish that this corner is the reason the desk never finishes, because putting it away feels like admitting it is over. Frame the real problem as a naming problem rather than a tidying one: nobody in this house can say out loud what the next physical action on that pile is, so it stays, and the desk grows around it.

segments.covers: Everything comes off the surface and only what the task in front of you needs goes back, plus the inbox tray.
beats: Lift the entire surface onto the floor in one continuous pass, monitor and keyboard aside, so the desk is bare wood before a single decision gets made.
Show why the floor is the holding ground rather than a drawer: a drawer lets an item skip the decision, the floor does not.
Work the return pile item by item against the task actually in front of you today. Dead pens, the second mug, and the fringe of sticky notes around the monitor bezel do not go back up.

Handle the half-finished project corner as the hard case. Say the next physical action in one sentence. If it can be named, that sentence goes on a card clipped to the papers and the whole thing goes into the inbox tray. If it cannot be named, box it, date the lid, shelf it, and set the rule that an unopened box on that date next year leaves unopened.
Set the finished state: the inbox tray holds fewer than a dozen sheets and nothing else claims the surface.
shots: Overhead locked wide of the full desk, one continuous unbroken clearing move from cluttered to bare

Three-quarter on hands writing one short sentence on a card and clipping it to a stack of papers
Overhead of the dated box lid being marked and the box sliding onto a shelf

Also restate the box-and-date fallback in full, because it is the half of the rule that makes the test safe to apply.

segments.covers: Positions on this desk are chosen by how the keyboard, notebook, and mouse are actually reached for, not by symmetry.
beats: Place the keyboard square in front of the monitor and mark the position, establishing that fixed means fixed rather than roughly central.
Put the notebook on the writing-hand side and the phone face down beyond it, following the reach you make most often.
Sweep an arm across the full arc the mouse travels and clear everything inside it, showing a stapler parked in that arc being steered around and then removed.
Compare the finished layout against the tape mark at the keyboard corner, so the viewer can see what fixed position means in practice.

short.standalone_note: Say plainly that the arc is the sweep the mouse travels, and name the three fixed positions again, because without the parent video the tracing move reads as decoration rather than a test.

segments.covers: Cleaning around a live screen safely, and the underside lip where forearms rest.
beats: Power everything down first and show the screen going dark, since the dark screen is what lets you see the film you are about to remove.
Spray cleaner onto the microfiber cloth, never onto the screen, and show why: liquid on glass runs down into the bezel and the electronics behind it.
Move to the desk edge, then to the underside lip where forearms rest, which is the grubbiest surface in the room precisely because it is the one nobody sees.
Show what the wipe turns up on this desk: the cable that has slipped out of its clip under the lip, the monitor arm bolt that has worked loose, the sticky ring where the mug has been parked.

segments.covers: A mug sharing the surface with the power strip, and the trip hazard in the arc the chair rolls through.
beats: Show the mug sitting behind the keyboard on the same surface as the power strip and the laptop charger, and name the hazard as water and electricity.

videos.cold_open_problem: Open on the bag of cables, adapters, and wall bricks being lifted out of the pedestal, heavy and tangled, and set down on the cleared desk. Establish why it has survived every previous attempt: each individual cable is too cheap to think about and too specific to throw away, so the decision gets made one cable at a time and therefore never gets made at all. Frame the fix as emptying the whole lot at once so the decision is made in one sitting rather than a hundred.

Empty the entire cable lot at once. Pick up each cable, name the device it powers, and point at where that device physically is in this house. No device, no keep.
Keep exactly one spare of each connector type still used daily, coil and band it, and bag the rest for electronics recycling this week.

videos.title: File Storage: Sorting Paper Into Keep, Scan, and Shred With a Retention Card
videos.cold_open_problem: Open on a drawer of paper that is neither obviously permanent nor obviously rubbish, a bank statement, a utility bill, a receipt for something long gone, each held up and set back down undecided. Establish that this middle band is why the whole job stalls: the permanent originals are easy and the junk is easy, but most of the drawer sits between them and every sheet reopens the same unanswered question. Frame the video as supplying the rule that ends the question rather than the motivation to keep going.

segments.covers: One drawer at a time into three piles, with the three-way rule that settles the middle band.
beats: Set up three labelled piles on the cleared desk: keep as paper, scan then shred, shred now.
Work one drawer only, since this is hundreds of small calls in a row and a fresh start beats a long finish.
Split permanent originals out first, birth and marriage certificates, deeds, vehicle titles, wills, immigration papers. These leave the cabinet entirely and go to a closed fireproof box.
Give tax paper one folder per year, held for whatever the local retention period is, which gets looked up once and written down.

Apply the test to everything else: if the issuer will reprint it on request, or it already lives inside an online account, it is information rather than a record, and information does not get a folder. Warranties and manuals stay only for machines still in this house.

beats: Open on the new tax paperwork landing on the desk, which is the household event this hangs on.
Pull the oldest year folder that has passed the period written on the card and take it straight to the shred bag.
Drop the new year folder into the gap the old one left, so the one in, one out rhythm reads in a single frame.
Land why the drawer never overflows again: its size is now held by the swap rather than by a clear-out.

Close on the shred bag by the door, filled and tied

close.standard_beat: End on the finished drawer, tabs in one line, the fireproof box closed at floor level, the shred bag by the door. Put the standard on screen, every folder named for the question you would ask, the retention card deciding what stays, then cut to the tax paperwork landing as the trigger that fires it once a year.
close.next_zone_teaser: Paper is settled, which leaves the shelf above it, and the books there are harder to release than any document in that drawer.

videos.title: Home Office Bookshelf Reset: Reference at Eye Level, Weight Low, Unit Anchored
videos.cold_open_problem: Open on the shelf holding textbooks from a degree, the professional library from a job that ended, and a reference set a website now answers faster, each pulled halfway out and pushed back. Establish that these are the hardest books in the house to release, because they stand for a version of you that has not been formally retired. Frame the coming decision as a question about when you last took one down rather than about whether you might one day.

segments.covers: Every shelf empties in one go, and the display test settles the books that stand for who you used to be.
beats: Take every book, binder, and manual off the shelves in one continuous pass rather than shelf by shelf, since partial emptying is what makes this job slow.
Clear the easy categories in one sweep: appliance manuals for machines that left the house, superseded editions with a year in the title, binders from finished projects.
Apply the call to the hard shelf. Ask when you last took it down since it arrived on this shelf, not whether you might one day.

If no specific occasion can be named and the book could be borrowed or reordered inside a week, it is no longer reference, it is display, and it goes into open competition for a display slot with everything else.
Handle manuals with the simpler blade: model still in the house, keep it, model gone, it goes today.
shots: Locked wide from the tripod facing the unit, shelves emptying in one continuous sweep to bare boards
Macro on a copyright year on a title page and the book going to the out pile
Close on a hand lifting a textbook, holding it, and setting it into the display competition row
High angle from the step stool on the display competition row laid out on the floor, more books than slots
on_screen_text: When did you last take it down?

short.hook: A row of books laid out on the floor beside a shelf that has visibly fewer slots than there are books.
short.standalone_note: Ask the when-did-you-last-take-it-down question out loud in the opening beat and name the borrow-or-reorder-in-a-week condition, because the display competition only makes sense once both halves of the test are on the table.

segments.covers: Height on this unit is set by the desk chair, mapped to how often you reach and how heavy the item is.
beats: Mark seated eye level on the shelf upright with the tape held at the height of the desk chair, since that height is defined by where you actually sit rather than by the shelf spacing.
Load working reference at that mark, occasional reading at standing height, archive boxes highest, heavy binders lowest.
Show one rule doing two jobs at once, easy reach and low weight, which is why it survives contact with a real room.
Frame the finished unit from the chair position, the angle it was loaded for.
shots: Three-quarter at seated chair height with a tape mark going onto the shelf upright
Locked wide facing the unit, books loading in bands, low to high
Close on heavy binders sliding onto the bottom two shelves
Locked three-quarter final from the chair position, no hands in frame

short.hook: A strip of tape goes onto a shelf upright at the height of the desk chair rather than at standing height, and the shelf gets loaded around it.
short.standalone_note: Explain that the height is taken from the working chair, not while standing, since that is the entire difference between this and ordinary shelving advice.

segments.covers: Dust from the top down, including the top edges of the books themselves.
beats: Work top shelf downward with a dry cloth, since anything knocked loose lands on shelves not done yet.
Wipe the front edge of every shelf, which is the line the eye reads when it scans the unit.
Vacuum the top edges of the books with a brush head, because that is where the dust in this room actually settles rather than on the shelf boards.
Act on what the pass turns up, a shelf pin that has worked loose or a board that has bowed under the binders, before the shelf goes back on.
shots: Three-quarter of a dry cloth running the top shelf, dust visible in raking light
Locked close at shelf-front height, cloth travelling through a static frame, repositioned shelf by shelf
Macro on a brush vacuum head crossing the top edges of a row of books
Close on a shelf pin being checked and seated

short.hook: A brush vacuum head runs along the top edges of a row of books, and the dust line is visible where it has already passed.
short.standalone_note: State that book top edges, not shelf boards, are where the dust in an office settles, because that claim is the reason to watch, and say to work top shelf downward.

segments.covers: An unanchored unit standing above the desk chair, with the weight loaded high.
beats: Show the unit standing over the desk chair with binders and box files on the top shelf, and name the hazard as fall, cut, or crush.
Find the wall studs and screw the unit in on camera, showing the bracket and the fixing rather than describing them.
Move box files, binders, and any framed glass award off the high shelf that sits above head height at the working position.
Close on the finished sightline from the chair, so the proof is the shot rather than a claim.
shots: Low three-quarter looking up at the loaded top shelf with the chair beneath it
Close on a stud finder crossing the wall and a pencil mark going down
Macro on the bracket and screw driving into the stud
Upward point of view from seated height, top shelf now light and clear

short.hook: A camera at desk chair height looks straight up at a tall shelf unit loaded with box files, and the unit is fixed to nothing.
short.standalone_note: End on the anchor going into the stud and the top shelf cleared, and name the hazard plainly, so the clip resolves rather than only alarming.

segments.covers: A bookend and a hand's width of slack turn a full shelf into a visible signal.
beats: Set a bookend closing every group and show the groups reading as separate blocks from across the room.
Leave a hand's width of empty shelf at the end of every row and measure it with an actual hand, so the standard needs no ruler.
Land the signal: when a shelf has no slack left, that is the visible sign a book has to leave, not that you need another shelf.
Point to Chapter 14, visual controls, where the shelf itself does the telling rather than a list.
shots: Three-quarter wide of bookends closing each group across the unit
Close on a hand set flat in the gap at the end of a row as the measure
Locked close on two shelves in one frame, one packed solid, one with a hand's width at the end

short.hook: A flat hand is placed in the gap at the end of a shelf row of books, and it just fits.
short.standalone_note: Say the rule that a shelf with no slack means a book leaves rather than that you buy another shelf, because that inversion is the whole idea, and show the hand as the only measure needed.

segments.covers: Finishing a book or closing a project binder is the moment the keep-or-go question gets asked.
beats: Open on a book being finished and a project binder being closed out, the two moments that already happen in this room.
Stop the reflex return to the shelf and put the keep-or-go question right there, while the answer is still obvious.
Show both outcomes, one back on the shelf into its group, one into the outbound box.
Land why timing does the work: the same book asked about a year later is a much harder question.
shots: Close on a book being closed on the last page
Close on project binder rings snapping shut
Overhead of the fork, one book to the shelf group, one to the outbound box

short.hook: A book is closed on its last page and the hand stops halfway back to the shelf.
short.standalone_note: Name the trigger as finishing a book or closing out a project binder, and say why asking at that moment is easier than asking a year later, since the pause on its own does not explain itself.

close.standard_beat: Hold the finished unit from the desk chair position, bookends closing every group and a hand's width of slack at every row end, and put the standard on screen with the note that heavy binders and box files never live above head height. Then cut to a book closing on its last page as the trigger.
close.next_zone_teaser: The shelf is settled and anchored, which leaves the corner of this room that runs hot and gets ignored, the printer.

videos.title: Printer Corner Reset: Clearance, a Paper Min Line, and the Backup Printer Test
videos.cold_open_problem: Open on the old printer on the floor of the cupboard, dusty, cables still coiled on top of it, kept because it might be a backup. Establish that nobody has plugged it in for a long time and nobody knows whether it works, so it is not a backup, it is a large object with an undecided status sitting in a corner. Frame the video as settling that today with a test page rather than with a plan to test it sometime.

segments.covers: Only ink, toner, and paper that matches the printer currently plugged in survives, and the backup gets tested now.
beats: Read the model number off the printer that is actually plugged in and hold each cartridge box against it, one at a time.
Show the timing on unmatched cartridges: they sell this week for more than they will ever be worth again, because cartridge value only falls.
Clear the half reams of odd paper, the letterhead with the old address, and the envelopes from two houses ago.

Settle the backup printer on camera. Plug it in and print a test page now. If it prints and you will keep a spare cartridge in stock for it, it is a backup and it gets a home. If you will not plug it in today, it goes to electronics recycling this week.
shots: Macro on the model number label on the printer body
Close on cartridge boxes being held one by one against that label, matches and misses landing in separate piles
Overhead of odd paper and old letterhead being fanned out and binned
Three-quarter of the old printer being plugged in and a test page feeding out

short.hook: An old printer that has not been switched on in years gets plugged in, and the camera holds on the output tray waiting to see whether anything comes out.
short.standalone_note: State the rule before the result, that a printer you will not plug in today is not a backup, so the clip works whichever way the test page goes, and name the spare cartridge condition.

segments.covers: Paper, spare cartridge, and scan tray each get a position in this corner that removes a hunt.
beats: Put the paper bin directly beneath the printer so reloading is a reach rather than a walk.
Set the one spare cartridge in a labelled box beside it, since cartridge boxes all look alike on a shelf.
Build the scan tray with a to-do side and a done side, then show a sheet crossing from one side to the other after it goes through the glass.
Frame the finished corner in one shot so the three positions read together.
shots: Three-quarter of the paper bin sliding into place under the printer
Close on the spare cartridge box being labelled and set beside it
Overhead of the scan tray with a sheet moving from the to-do side to the done side
Locked three-quarter of the finished corner, no hands

short.hook: A single tray with two sides, and a sheet crossing from one side to the other the moment it comes off the scanner glass.
short.standalone_note: Explain what problem the two sides solve, that you otherwise cannot tell what has already been scanned, since the tray by itself looks like ordinary stacking.

segments.covers: Scanner glass and toner dust each punish the obvious cleaning method.
beats: Power the machine off and lift the lid, showing the glass in raking light so the smears read.
Spray cleaner onto the cloth, never onto the glass, since liquid on the platen runs down inside the machine at the edges.
Use a dry cloth for toner dust, because water turns loose toner into ink, which is the mistake that makes the mess permanent.
Vacuum the paper lint around the feed tray, which is what a lot of misfeeds on this machine actually are.
shots: Close on the power switch, then the lid lifting
Raking side-light macro across the scanner glass, smears then clear
Macro of cleaner going into a folded cloth held off to the side
Close on a dry cloth lifting toner dust, then a vacuum nozzle at the feed tray
on_screen_text: Spray the cloth, not the glass

short.hook: A cloth is loaded with cleaner well away from the machine, then scanner glass goes from smeared to clear in one pass.
short.standalone_note: Say both halves of the rule, cleaner on the cloth for glass and dry cloth only for toner, because a viewer who takes only the first half will make the toner worse.

segments.covers: The fuser runs hot and needs air, and nothing sits on the lid.
beats: Show the machine pushed tight to the wall inside the cupboard, name the hazard as burn or fire, and pull it forward to leave clear air behind the fuser.
Trace the power lead and find the strip plugged into another strip, then plug the printer straight into a wall outlet instead.
Clear the top of the lid completely, including the plant and the drink, and name that second hazard as water and electricity sitting directly above the electronics and the paper path.
Point to Chapter 21, the hazard hunt, and treat everything found here the same way: find it, and fix it now.
shots: Beanbag three-quarter behind the printer showing zero clearance, then the gap after it is pulled forward
Close following the lead from the printer to a strip and then to a second strip
Close on the plug going directly into a wall outlet
Overhead of the plant and glass being lifted off the printer lid, lid left bare

short.hook: A hand follows a printer cable to a power strip, and then that strip's cable to a second power strip.
short.standalone_note: Name the fuser heat as the reason this particular machine wants its own wall outlet and clear air behind it, otherwise it reads as generic electrical advice.

segments.covers: A min line and a max line inside the paper bin make the reorder point visible.
beats: Draw a min line and a max line inside the empty paper bin, then load the stack so it sits between them.
Set the rule: when the stack drops to the min line, the next ream goes on the shopping list that day, not the day it runs out mid-job.
Read the bin from standing height at the min line, so the signal works without bending down or counting sheets.
shots: Overhead into the empty bin with a marker drawing two lines on the inside wall
Close on the paper stack sitting at the max line, then at the min line
Three-quarter from standing height showing the min line readable at a glance

short.hook: Two marker lines get drawn inside an empty printer paper bin before a single sheet goes back in.
short.standalone_note: State what each line means and what the min line triggers, ordering the same day rather than the day it runs out, because two marker lines with no rule attached are just marks.

segments.covers: The refill happens when you take the last sheet, while you are already standing at the machine.
beats: Open on the last sheet coming out of the bin and the bin bottom showing, which is the trigger.
Refill from the shelf before walking away from the machine, since the whole rule rests on you already being on your feet at the right spot.
Cut that against refilling later, when the trip has to be made specially and therefore does not get made.
Restate the standard, matched cartridges only, a min line in the bin, and a bare machine top.
shots: Close on the last sheet lifting out and the bin bottom showing
Three-quarter of a turn to the shelf and a ream coming straight back
Overhead of the refilled bin sitting between its two lines

short.hook: The last sheet of paper comes out of a printer bin, and the hands turn straight to the shelf instead of to the door.
short.standalone_note: Name the trigger and the reason it works, that you are already standing at the machine with your hands free, since the clip otherwise just shows someone loading paper.

close.standard_beat: Finish on the corner with the bin between its lines, one labelled spare cartridge beside it, the scan tray split, clear air behind the machine, and a bare lid. Put the standard on screen, then show the last sheet coming out of the bin as the trigger that keeps it stocked.
close.next_zone_teaser: The spare cartridge has a home now, which raises the question of everything else this office has been stockpiling, and the cabinet where it lives.

videos.title: Supply Cabinet Reset: Counting the Bulk Buy and Writing Min and Max on the Shelf
videos.cold_open_problem: Open on the bulk box of 500 envelopes, the multipack of sticky notes, and the case of paper bought because the price was good, all coming out of the cabinet and onto the floor. Establish the genuinely hard part, which is that you were not wrong about the price, so admitting the surplus was a mistake feels like throwing money away twice. Set up what the count will prove: the money left when you bought it, and the shelf space is being paid for now.

segments.covers: Everything comes out and lines up in categories, because the counting is the part that does the work.
beats: Bring the whole cabinet out onto the floor and line it up in categories, since a dozen packs of sticky notes look like nothing until they stand side by side in a row.
Count the true stock of each category and divide it by honest annual use, out loud. Six letters a year against 500 envelopes is a lifetime supply and then some.
Cap it: one open plus one spare of anything used monthly, and a single year of use for everything else.
Box the surplus for a school, a charity shop, or a neighbour this week, and show it leaving the room. Not to the top shelf, and not to a box in the garage.
Clear the dead stock in one sweep, dried glue sticks, dead markers, cracked folders, and adapters nobody can identify.
shots: High angle from the step stool, tripod raised, entire cabinet contents laid out in category rows on the floor
Close on a hand counting envelope packs into a line, one by one
Macro on a dried glue stick and a dead marker going into the bin
Overhead of the surplus being boxed and labelled for the school or charity shop
Close on the box going out the door of the room
on_screen_text: Line it up to see it

short.hook: Packs of sticky notes get counted out into a single line across an office floor, and the line runs past the edge of frame.
short.standalone_note: Do the divide-by-annual-use count on camera with one real category, and state the one open plus one spare cap, because the count without the cap gives the viewer a feeling instead of a rule.

beats: Put one open pack of each consumable at hand height and its backstock directly behind it on the same shelf.
Show the before condition first, a refill hunted out from behind three boxes of envelopes, then the same refill pulled in a single reach with nothing else moving.
Put reams of paper on the bottom shelf, which is doing double duty here since it is also the safety answer.
Read the finished cabinet from the doorway so the layout works without stepping in.

Close on a single reach pulling a refill without moving anything else
Close on reams of paper going onto the bottom shelf
Locked three-quarter from the doorway, cabinet open, no hands

segments.covers: Wiping the emptied shelves is when you find the leak, the split pouch, and the sticky ring.
beats: Wipe the shelves with the cabinet emptied and look as you go rather than after.
Find a pen that has leaked and show the ink stain it left in the shelf board.
Check for a split toner pouch and handle it with a dry cloth rather than a wet one.
Lift a roll of tape that has gone soft and find the sticky ring under it, the sort of thing that only surfaces when the shelf is bare.

segments.covers: Weight belongs low, and a rolling chair is not a step.
beats: Show why the rolling chair fails as a step: a hand presses down on the seat and the castors turn under the load, with nobody standing on it.
Bring an actual step stool into the room and give it a standing place in the corner, so the fix is present rather than fetched, then do the top shelf reach from the stool.
Move reams of paper and boxes of envelopes down to the bottom shelf, and name the second hazard, a slipping box landing on your head and shoulders while your arms are up.
Finish with the top shelf holding only light, rarely needed items.
